Because whatever is desired is accomplished through the worship of God alone,

2.9.m: Many kinds of gods were described by you previously, O Six-faced One,
and diverse methods of worshipping them were described.
All their fruits were spoken of by you individually;

From the worship of Brahmā, O Guha, for yogins following the path of cessation,
the fruit is the attainment of worlds such as Jana, yet it perishes at the end of two parārdhas.
Having accomplished difficult deeds here through great hardship,
if the gain of the fruit is perishable, then what is the use of acquiring it?
The worship of those denizens of heaven whose body,
status, power, and the like are destroyed by time does not please me here.
Tell me, O Guha, of that God who is himself fearless, the remover of fear for others, eternal,

Skanda said:
You, who understand inquiries, ask a great question here, O sinless one.
The answer to this cannot be stated in hundreds of years by one's own reasoning
without the grace of God, O brahmin, even by the best of the wise.
However, by the grace of Vāsudeva, what is known by me I shall declare to you.
Nothing is unmentionable to you, devoted to duty, O noble-minded one.

Vāsudeva is the supreme Brahman; Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the Supreme Puruṣa.
He is the God to be worshipped by the desireless and by those with desires, and even by liberated men.
By the twice-born, by the āśramas, and in every way by women, Śūdras, and others,
he alone is to be pleased through their respective duties with devotion.
Therefore, all action—pertaining to the gods and pertaining to the ancestors—at all times,

2.9.m: and whatever is prescribed in the Veda, must be performed properly only for his pleasure.
Whatever auspicious action is performed here by men for the sake of attaining happiness,
even if well performed, if devoid of connection to Kṛṣṇa,
then it is to be known as perishable, yielding little fruit, and of the nature of the guṇas.
From the conjunction of an inauspicious place and the like, it produces defect in the fruit;
and beset with many obstacles, it does not at all grant men the attainment of their desires.
If this very action is performed for the satisfaction of Śrī Kṛṣṇa,
then, through connection with him, all of it becomes indeed beyond the guṇas.
It yields imperishable fruit, even greater than what was desired by oneself;
and no defect arises in it from association with an improper place or the like.
Moreover, O brahmin seer, by the majesty of the Discus-bearer, no obstacle
can ever prevail against it; it grants the attainment of desired ends.
Even if one’s own meritorious deed is small, nonetheless, O brahmin,
through direct connection with the Supreme Self, it becomes truly exceedingly great.
Just as even a mere spark, through conjunction with a heap of forest wood,
becomes an irresistible conflagration, so does this through connection with Hari.

2.9.m: Therefore, by men abiding in the path of active engagement or of cessation,

In this regard also they cite this ancient history:

The Blessed One, Vāsudeva, who dwells eternally in the city of Brahman,
manifested from Dharma through the daughter of Dakṣa for the welfare of the world.
In the Kṛta Yuga of old, during the Svāyambhuva period, O best of the twice-born,
he appeared in two forms: Nara and Nārāyaṇa.
From the hermitage of Dharma, in order to perform austerity solely for the welfare of men on earth,
those two, Nara and Nārāyaṇa, went to the hermitage of Badarī.
There, the two primordial lords of the world, emaciated and covered in veins,
performed austerity with their own splendor, difficult to behold even by the gods.

Therefore, the discerning ever perform all their rituals,

2.9.s: pravṛttā vā nivṛttā vā kurvate sakalā api .. 25 ..
2.9.d: प्रवृत्ता वा निवृत्ता वा कुर्वते सकला अपि .. 25 ..
2.9.m: whether active or renounced, imbued with devotion to Viṣṇu. // 25
Brahmā, Sthāṇu, Manu, Dakṣa, Bhṛgu, Dharma, and Yama,
Marīci, Aṅgiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, // 26
Vaibhrāja, Vasiṣṭha, Vivasvat, and Soma,
Kaśyapa, Kardama, and others, the lords of creatures, O sage, // 27
and all the gods, all the seers, all the classes, and likewise the stages of life,
worship that very Lord, abiding by the path of active engagement in duty.
Sana, Sanatsujāta, Sanaka, Sanandana,
Sanatkumāra, Kapila, Āruṇi, Sanātana,
Ṛbhu, Yati, and sages such as Haṃsa, who hold lifelong vows—
they worship that very Lord, abiding by the path of renunciation.
Conceiving the gods and the ancestors as limbs of Vāsudeva,
they sacrifice daily with non-violent rites of worship.
For wherever they have been appointed by him according to their qualification,

2.9.s: pravṛtte vā nivṛtte vā dharme te pālayanti tam ..
2.9.d: प्रवृत्ते वा निवृत्ते वा धर्मे ते पालयन्ति तम् ..
2.9.m: whether in the active path or in the path of renunciation, they protect it;

2.9.s: tasya devasya maryādāṃ na krāmantyubhayepi te .. 32 ..
2.9.d: तस्य देवस्य मर्यादां न क्रामन्त्युभयेपि ते .. 32 ..
2.9.m: both of them do not transgress the boundary set by that God.
Whatever among the four goals of life may be most desired by anyone among them,
the Lord, Master of all powers, completely fulfills each and every one.
Even of a slight meritorious deed done with devotion,
the Lord, pleased, grants a great, imperishable, and desired fruit.
Among them, however, those who in this world have attained single-minded devotion to him,
all their desires completely subsided with respect to anything other than Vāsudeva—

2.9.s: dehānte te tu saṃprāpya tasya dhāma tamaḥparam ..
2.9.d: देहान्ते ते तु संप्राप्य तस्य धाम तमःपरम् ..
2.9.m: at the end of their bodies, having reached his abode beyond darkness,
they serve him with love in non-material bodies alone.
Other devotees, in time, through firmness in their worship of him,
when their latent desires are exhausted, go to him just like the single-minded devotees.

2.9.s: yena kenāpi bhāvena tena saṃbadhyate tu yaḥ ..
2.9.d: येन केनापि भावेन तेन संबध्यते तु यः ..
2.9.m: Whoever is bound to him by any disposition whatsoever,

2.9.s: saṃsṛtiṃ na prayātyeva sa tu kvāpyanyajīvavat .. 38 ..
2.9.d: संसृतिं न प्रयात्येव स तु क्वाप्यन्यजीववत् .. 38 ..
2.9.m: never falls into worldly existence anywhere like an ordinary soul.
The desired attainment of karmayoga and of jñānayoga
occurs quickly and without obstacle for men solely through taking refuge in him.
Therefore, that very Lord should be worshipped with love according to the rules
by all people here, for the sake of attaining their desired results.
Even Brahmā, Śiva, and the other gods, though they have attained oneness with Brahman and are free from obstacles,
practice devotion to Śrī Viṣṇu; such are his great virtues.
Thus, O Nārada, has this secret teaching been declared to you in full,
for you possess continual and excessive devotion toward me."

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevasarvopāsyatvanirūpaṇaṃ nāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ .. 3 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्रीवासुदेवसर्वोपास्यत्वनिरूपणं नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः .. 3 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Expounding that Śrī Vāsudeva is to be Worshipped by All', in the glorious Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Skanda said:
He, the best of those who know the Self, addressed in this way by Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Person,

2.9.s: jagāda vākyaṃ jagatāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ tamacyutaṃ lokahitādhivāsam .. 1 ..
2.9.d: जगाद वाक्यं जगतां गरिष्ठं तमच्युतं लोकहिताधिवासम् .. 1 ..
2.9.m: spoke a word to that Acyuta, the greatest in all the worlds, the dwelling-place of the world's welfare.
Nārada said:
"O God, all that you have spoken has been heard by me, whose vast glory is concealed by the form of a seer; / I know in my heart, O Lord, that all of this is only the play of the Lord of All.

2.9.s: tavaiva līlā sakaleyamīśa sarveśvarasyeti vidāmi citte .. 2 ..
2.9.d: तवैव लीला सकलेयमीश सर्वेश्वरस्येति विदामि चित्ते .. 2 ..
2.9.m: I know in my heart, O Lord, that this entire universe is merely your divine play, the Sovereign Lord of All.
By your darśana alone, O Infinite One, my desire is fulfilled, as sought in my heart;

2.9.s: tathāpyahaṃ tattava pūrvarūpaṃ prabho didṛkṣāmi hi kautukaṃ me .. 3 ..
2.9.d: तथाप्यहं तत्तव पूर्वरूपं प्रभो दिदृक्षामि हि कौतुकं मे .. 3 ..
2.9.m: even so, O Lord, I wish to see that primordial form of yours; great is my curiosity."
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

2.9.s: na tatsvarūpaṃ mama dānayajñayogaiśca vaidestapasāpi dṛśyam ..
2.9.d: न तत्स्वरूपं मम दानयज्ञयोगैश्च वैदेस्तपसापि दृश्यम् ..
2.9.m: "That essential form of mine cannot be seen by charitable gifts, sacrifices, yogic practices, Vedic rites, or even by austerity.

2.9.s: ekāntikairbhaktavaraistu bhaktyā hyananyayā nārada dṛśyate tat .. 4 ..
2.9.d: एकान्तिकैर्भक्तवरैस्तु भक्त्या ह्यनन्यया नारद दृश्यते तत् .. 4 ..
2.9.m: It is seen, O Nārada, by the best of devotees who are single-minded, through unswerving devotion.

2.9.s: bhaktistava tvasti mayi hyananyā jñānaṃ ca vairāgyayutaṃ svadharmaḥ ..
2.9.d: भक्तिस्तव त्वस्ति मयि ह्यनन्या ज्ञानं च वैराग्ययुतं स्वधर्मः ..
2.9.m: Your devotion to me is indeed unswerving, accompanied by knowledge, detachment, and adherence to your own duty.
Therefore, you shall obtain that darśana, which is difficult to attain even for the chiefs of the gods.
Being exceedingly pleased by your devotion, I now bid you to behold it:

2.9.s: sitāntarīpaṃ vraja tatra te'yaṃ manorathaḥ setsyati vipravarya .. 6 ..
2.9.d: सितान्तरीपं व्रज तत्र तेऽयं मनोरथः सेत्स्यति विप्रवर्य .. 6 ..
2.9.m: go to the White Island; there this desire of yours will be accomplished, O best of brahmins."
Skanda said:

2.9.s: śrutveti vācaṃ parameṣṭhiputraḥ sopyarccayitvā tamṛṣiṃ purāṇam ..
2.9.d: श्रुत्वेति वाचं परमेष्ठिपुत्रः सोप्यर्च्चयित्वा तमृषिं पुराणम् ..
2.9.m: Having heard this speech, he, the son of Brahmā, worshiped that ancient seer,
soared into the sky equipped with excellent yoga, and then suddenly descended upon Meru.

2.9.s: tasyāvatasthe ca munirmuhūrttamekāntamāsādya gireḥ sa śṛṃge ..
2.9.d: तस्यावतस्थे च मुनिर्मुहूर्त्तमेकान्तमासाद्य गिरेः स शृंगे ..
2.9.m: The sage paused there for a moment after reaching a solitary peak on the mountain;
looking toward the north-west, he beheld an exceedingly wondrous island.

2.9.s: kṣīrodadheruttarato hi dvīpaḥ śvetaḥ sa nāmnā prathito viśālaḥ ..
2.9.d: क्षीरोदधेरुत्तरतो हि द्वीपः श्वेतः स नाम्ना प्रथितो विशालः ..
2.9.m: To the north of the Ocean of Milk lies that vast island famed by the name Śveta,

2.9.s: dedīpyamāno vitatena sarvato jyotiścayenātisi tena nityam .. 9 ..
2.9.d: देदीप्यमानो विततेन सर्वतो ज्योतिश्चयेनातिसि तेन नित्यम् .. 9 ..
2.9.m: continually blazing forth all around with an extensive mass of intensely white light;
with numerous mangoes, asanas, aśokas, āmrātakas, nimba, kadamba, and nīpa trees,
with bilvas, madhūkas, divine trees, plakṣas, banyans, kiṃśukas, and sandal trees,
with sarjas, śālas, jackfruits, tamālas, sage-trees, ketakas, and campakas,
and with kundas, jātīs, and divine mallikās—trees bent under the weight of fruits and flowers;
with many groves of wish-fulfilling trees, and rows of golden plantains and betel-nut palms,
with numerous vast and splendid gardens, and rivers and lakes adorned with blossoming lotuses,
with excellent birds such as swans producing sweet sounds, and beautiful moving herds of deer.

2.9.s: sarvepi jīvāḥ kila yatra muktā vasanti ca sthāvarajaṅgamāśca ..
2.9.d: सर्वेपि जीवाः किल यत्र मुक्ता वसन्ति च स्थावरजङ्गमाश्च ..
2.9.m: where indeed all living beings, both stationary and moving, dwell liberated.

2.9.s: taṃ vīkṣamāṇena ca tena dṛṣṭā bhaktottamāḥ śrīpuruṣottamasya .. 13 ..
2.9.d: तं वीक्षमाणेन च तेन दृष्टा भक्तोत्तमाः श्रीपुरुषोत्तमस्य .. 13 ..
2.9.m: Looking around, he saw the foremost devotees of glorious Puruṣottama,
beyond the senses, freed from all sin, devoid of bodily discharges, and fragrant,
some two-armed and some four-armed, some white and some shining like fresh rainclouds,
with eyes like lotus petals, bodies of balanced proportions, handsome and divine limbs, extremely solid,
with flowing hair, ever youthful, endowed with all auspicious marks,
their hands and feet marked with lotus lines, free from the six waves [of mortal suffering], radiant beyond the sun,

2.9.s: sitāṃśukā dhyānaparāśca saumyāḥ kālopi yebhyo bhayameti nityam.. 16 ..
2.9.d: सितांशुका ध्यानपराश्च सौम्याः कालोपि येभ्यो भयमेति नित्यम्.. 16 ..
2.9.m: dressed in white garments, absorbed in meditation, gentle, and of whom even Time is constantly afraid.
Sāvarṇi said:

2.9.s: atīndriyā nirātaṅkā aniṣyandāḥ sugandhinaḥ .. ke te narāḥ kathaṃ jātāstādṛśāḥ kā ca tadgatiḥ .. 17 ..
2.9.d: अतीन्द्रिया निरातङ्का अनिष्यन्दाः सुगन्धिनः .. के ते नराः कथं जातास्तादृशाः का च तद्गतिः .. 17 ..
2.9.m: Beyond the senses, free from distress, without bodily discharges, fragrant— / who are those men, how were such beings born, and what is their destination?

2.9.s: śvetadvīpaḥ payombhodhau varttate hi dharātale .. tadvāsināmapi kathaṃ proktā'tīndriyatā tvayā ..18..
2.9.d: श्वेतद्वीपः पयोम्भोधौ वर्त्तते हि धरातले .. तद्वासिनामपि कथं प्रोक्ताऽतीन्द्रियता त्वया ..18..
2.9.m: Śvetadvīpa is situated in the ocean of milk upon the surface of the earth; / how then has transcending the senses been spoken of by you even for its dwellers?

2.9.s: ye brahmaṇyakṣare dhāmni saccidānandarūpiṇi.. sthitāḥ syuścinmayā muktāste tathā syurnnahītare .. 19 ..
2.9.d: ये ब्रह्मण्यक्षरे धाम्नि सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणि.. स्थिताः स्युश्चिन्मया मुक्तास्ते तथा स्युर्न्नहीतरे .. 19 ..
2.9.m: Those liberated ones of pure consciousness who abide in the imperishable abode of Brahman, / which consists of being, consciousness, and bliss—they may be so, but surely not others.

2.9.s: etaṃ me saṃśayaṃ chindhi paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me .. tvaṃ hi sarvakathābhijñastatastvāmāśritosmayaham .. 2.9.4.20 ..
2.9.d: एतं मे संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे .. त्वं हि सर्वकथाभिज्ञस्ततस्त्वामाश्रितोस्मयहम् .. 2.9.4.20 ..
2.9.m: Sever this doubt of mine, for my curiosity is great; / you are indeed knowledgeable in all tales, and therefore I have taken refuge in you.
Skanda said:

2.9.s: ekāntopāsanenaiva prākkalpeṣu ramāpateḥ .. ye brahmabhāvaṃ saṃprāptā ajarāmaratāṃ gatāḥ .. 21 ..
2.9.d: एकान्तोपासनेनैव प्राक्कल्पेषु रमापतेः .. ये ब्रह्मभावं संप्राप्ता अजरामरतां गताः .. 21 ..
2.9.m: By exclusive devotion alone to the Lord of Ramā in previous kalpas, / those who attained the state of Brahman and reached agelessness and immortality,

2.9.s: akṣarākhyāḥ pumāṃsaste śvetadvīpe'tra dhāmani .. sevituṃ vāsudevaṃ taṃ sthitā devarṣiṇekṣitāḥ ..22 ..
2.9.d: अक्षराख्याः पुमांसस्ते श्वेतद्वीपेऽत्र धामनि .. सेवितुं वासुदेवं तं स्थिता देवर्षिणेक्षिताः ..22 ..
2.9.m: those beings called 'imperishable' in this abode of Śvetadvīpa / were seen by the divine seer, dwelling there to serve Vāsudeva.

2.9.s: prāpte pralayakāle tu punaścākṣaradhāmani .. sthāsyanti te svatantrāśca kālamāyābhayojjhitāḥ .. 23 ..
2.9.d: प्राप्ते प्रलयकाले तु पुनश्चाक्षरधामनि .. स्थास्यन्ति ते स्वतन्त्राश्च कालमायाभयोज्झिताः .. 23 ..
2.9.m: When the time of dissolution arrives, they will once again dwell in the imperishable abode, / independent and devoid of fear from Time and Māyā.

2.9.s: atrāpi puruṣā ye tu māyājātā ataḥ kṣarāḥ .. tepi sadbhiḥ sādhanairvai jāyante tādṛśāḥ kila .. 24 ..
2.9.d: अत्रापि पुरुषा ये तु मायाजाता अतः क्षराः .. तेपि सद्भिः साधनैर्वै जायन्ते तादृशाः किल .. 24 ..
2.9.m: Even here, men born of Māyā who are consequently perishable / indeed become such through good spiritual practices:

2.9.s: ahiṃsayā ca tapasā svadharmeṇa virāgataḥ .. vāsudevasya māhātmyajñānenaivātmaniṣṭhayā .. 25..
2.9.d: अहिंसया च तपसा स्वधर्मेण विरागतः .. वासुदेवस्य माहात्म्यज्ञानेनैवात्मनिष्ठया .. 25..
2.9.m: By non-violence, austerity, one's own duty, dispassion, / knowledge of Vāsudeva's majesty, steadfastness in the Self,

2.9.s: bhaktyā paramayā nityaṃ prasaṅgena mahātmanām .. harisevāvihīnānāṃ muktīnāmapyanicchayā .. 26 ..
2.9.d: भक्त्या परमया नित्यं प्रसङ्गेन महात्मनाम् .. हरिसेवाविहीनानां मुक्तीनामप्यनिच्छया .. 26 ..
2.9.m: supreme devotion, constant association with great souls, / by desiring not even forms of liberation devoid of service to Hari,

2.9.s: siddhīnāmaṇimādīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ cāpyakāṃkṣayā .. anyonyaṃ śrutikīrtibhyāṃ śrīharerjanmakarmaṇām ..
2.9.d: सिद्धीनामणिमादीनां सर्वासां चाप्यकांक्षया .. अन्योन्यं श्रुतिकीर्तिभ्यां श्रीहरेर्जन्मकर्मणाम् ..
2.9.m: by lacking desire for all supernatural perfections such as minuteness, / by mutual hearing and glorifying of Śrī Hari's births and deeds—
such men certainly arise, O best of sages.

2.9.s: jagatsarge jāyamānepyete kālavaśātkvacit .. na jāyante svataṃtratvānna naśyanti laye'nyavat .. 28 ..
2.9.d: जगत्सर्गे जायमानेप्येते कालवशात्क्वचित् .. न जायन्ते स्वतंत्रत्वान्न नश्यन्ति लयेऽन्यवत् .. 28 ..
2.9.m: Even when the creation of the world occurs, these are never born through the power of Time; / by their independence they do not perish at the dissolution like others.

2.9.s: atra te kathayiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ mune .. yathātratyopi manujastathā bhāvamupeyivān.. 29 ..
2.9.d: अत्र ते कथयिष्यामि कथां पौराणिकीं मुने .. यथात्रत्योपि मनुजस्तथा भावमुपेयिवान्.. 29 ..
2.9.m: In this regard I will tell you an ancient tale, O sage, / of how even a mortal dwelling here attained such a state.

2.9.s: vistīrṇaiṣā kathā brahmañchrutā me pitṛsannidhau .. saiṣādya tava vaktavyā kathāsāro hi sa smṛtaḥ .. 2.9.4.30 ..
2.9.d: विस्तीर्णैषा कथा ब्रह्मञ्छ्रुता मे पितृसन्निधौ .. सैषाद्य तव वक्तव्या कथासारो हि स स्मृतः .. 2.9.4.30 ..
2.9.m: This extensive story, O brahmin, was heard by me in the presence of my father; / that very story, known as the essence of tales, is to be spoken to you today.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śvetadvīpamuktavarṇanaṃ nāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ .. 4 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्वेतद्वीपमुक्तवर्णनं नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः .. 4 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the fourth chapter, entitled "The Description of the Liberated of Śvetadvīpa" in the glorious Vāsudeva-māhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Skanda said:
Anciently, O sage, there was a king named Uparicara Vasu,
the son of Āyu, the ruler of the earth, celebrated as Amāvasu,
a friend of Indra, who attained devotion to the Lord Nārāyaṇa.
Righteous, devoted to the ancestors, propitiating ancestors and gods,
devoted to good conduct, capable, forbearing, free from malice,
benefactor to all, tranquil, devoted to celibacy, pure,
free from anger, moderate in eating, gentle, devoid of vices, a sage,
free from dualities, free from modifications, devoid of pride, resolute, knower of the Self,
free from deceit, respectful to others, a yogin, ascetic, who had conquered his senses;
detached from wealth, sons, wife, kinsmen, and the like,
that king chanted the Nārāyaṇa-mantra daily with devotion.
Then, pleased with him, the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva himself gave him
an empire; he, unattached to it, worshiped Him with reverence.
Concentrated during the five times [of day] according to the prescribed rule,
he worshiped the Lord of gods, and with the remnants of that [offering], the gods and ancestors;
with the remnants of theirs, having distributed to the brahmins and dependents,
he ate the food remnants, devoted to truth, non-violent toward all living beings.
The king recognized the fault in eating the meat of any living being
as equal to a great sin, and he spoke accordingly to his subjects.
With his whole being he worshiped Janārdana, the God of gods,
without beginning, middle, or end, the maker of the worlds, imperishable.
He made his mind firm upon the feet of glorious Vāsudeva,

2.9.s: śrotre ca nityaṃ bhagavatkathāyāḥ śravaṇe nṛpaḥ ..1 1..
2.9.d: श्रोत्रे च नित्यं भगवत्कथायाः श्रवणे नृपः ..1 1..
2.9.m: and the king constantly applied his two ears to hearing the story of the Blessed Lord;

2.9.s: nayane sve mukundasya tadbhaktānāṃ ca darśane..
2.9.d: नयने स्वे मुकुन्दस्य तद्भक्तानां च दर्शने..
2.9.m: his two eyes to the darśana of Mukunda and of His devotees;

2.9.m: Not even a single moment of that royal sage passed
without devotion to the Lord of Ramā, as he observed his vows.
With great provisions indeed, he celebrated Viṣṇu's birthday festivals;
for that purpose he constructed gardens, temples, and pleasure groves.
To him who bore such devotion to Nārāyaṇa, O best of brahmins,
the king of gods himself offered a seat on his own couch.
Indra gave him the extremely beautiful Vaijayantī garland,
made of unfading lotuses, and also abundant jewels.

2.9.m: "One's self, kingdom, wealth, wife, vehicles, and the like—
all that belongs to the Lord": thus he always regarded them.
Desire-prompted, occasional, and perpetual supreme sacrificial rites—
he performed them all with concentrated mind, following the Sātvata injunctions.
Chief brahmins knowledgeable in the Pañcarātra, in the house of that great-souled one,
regularly ate first what was offered to the Lord.
While he, the slayer of his foes, was ruling the kingdom righteously,
no untruthful speech arose, nor did his mind turn wicked,

2.9.s: na ca kāyena kṛtavānsa pāpaṃ paramaṇvapi .. 24 ..

2.9.m: nor did he commit even an atom of sin with his body.
For the nourishment of devotion to the Lord, the great treatise Pañcarātra
the king listened to daily from the mouth of a devotee of the Lord.
Establishing pure righteousness and gladdening all his subjects,
he protected the earth just as Indra protects heaven.
Even among the seven kinds of meat-eaters, in his kingdom
there was not a single person, nor were there any wearing the guise of heretics.
Intractable women, adulterous men,
and those who cause confusion of caste duties were unheard of in his kingdom.
Of the eleven kinds of liquor and the three kinds of surā,
no one in this realm even smelled any while he ruled the kingdom.
Yet, though possessing such virtues, on one occasion out of partiality for the celestials,
due to a false statement he fell from heaven and entered the bowels of the earth.
Having gone underground, he, ever fond of righteousness,
became devoted to Nārāyaṇa and chanted his mantra with steady mind.
By his grace alone, he rose up once again;

Becoming the lord of Cedi once again on earth due to a curse of the ancestors,

Then the king attained the heavenly world in a divine body,
and together with the hosts of supreme seers residing there,
confirming his worship of the Lord, he dwelt there for some time.
Then he attained the supreme, fearless abode of Vāsudeva.

2.9.m: "Indeed, the great king Vasu was a devotee of the Lord.
What untruth did he speak, on account of which he fell from heaven into a hole in the earth?

2.9.m: How was the king freed from that? Tell me this, O Skanda!"
Skanda said:
"Hear, O brahmin, this story of Vasu, who possessed the splendor of Indra,
from the hearing of which instantaneous destruction of all sins occurs.
Formerly, in the Svāyambhuva manvantara, the Indra named Viśvajit
began a great sacrifice called the horse sacrifice, O sage.
Sacrificial beasts, goats and others, were bound there in large numbers, bleating aloud;
and all the hosts of gods, greedy for the offerings, were seated there.
Wandering at will for the welfare of all worlds,
great seers possessing the brilliance of the sun arrived there.
Honored by the host of gods with water for feet, water for hospitality, welcome, and the like,
those great sages saw the animals suitable for sacrifice crying out.
Beholding that elaborate sacrifice, filled with violence,
even of the gods who are of a sattvic nature, they felt great astonishment indeed.
Seeing that violation of dharma, out of compassion those best of brahmins,
endowed with righteous minds, spoke then to the gods headed by Mahendra:"
The great seers said:
Together with the gods and seers, O Mahendra, listen to our words!
Indeed, we proclaim the eternal essence of dharma as it truly is. // 2.9.6.10
At the time of world creation, by Brahmā the supreme lord,
you were created from sattva, upholders of four-footed dharma. // 11
From rajas and tamas, he [created] Manus and rulers of men;
and he created lords of the asuras as upholders of dharma. // 12
Then, for all of you, teaching the rites of sacrifice and the like,
he created the Veda for your welfare, granting the fruits of all desires. // 13
Indeed, non-violence alone is praised in that Veda as the supreme dharma;
the direct slaughter of animals in sacrifice is not approved by the Veda. // 14
For the intent of the Veda is entirely in establishing

2.9.m: Then, situated in the midst of the earth, that king, censuring his own deed
and repenting greatly, showing reverence to those great sages,
constantly repeated in his mind the three-syllabled mantra of the Lord. (1)

he respectfully worshipped Hari, the lord of the gods, in the cavity of the earth. (2)

A man who does not resort to true dharma at any time
is never liberated from the cycle of existence: this is my true word.
Now, O best of brahmins, I shall tell you of the origin of violent sacrifices and the like,
as I previously heard it from the mouth of my father.
In this regard they cite this ancient account,
in which the greatness of Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmī is glorified.
Because of the fault of transgressing against those great sages,
the good intellect of Indra the all-conqueror was destroyed, O sage.
Durvāsas, an ascetic sage who was a portion of Śaṃkara,
wandering at will through the worlds, once went to the river Puṣpabhadrā.
There he saw the wife of the vidyādhara Sumati,
surrounded by companions, coming from heaven to play in the water.
She was holding in her right hand a highly fragrant garland named Madakalā,
woven from golden lotuses of the heavenly Gaṅgā.
Seeing her, the sage approached her
and, like an intoxicated man, begged for that garland held by the vidyādharī.

2.9.s: sāpi praṇamya taṃ sadyo māhātmyaṃ tasya jānatī ..

2.9.m: She too bowed to him at once, knowing his greatness,
and placed that garland around his neck with supreme respect.
Then the sage, pleased at heart, singing as he went like an intoxicated man,
saw the lord of the gods coming on the road to that great river.
His victory was being sung in sweet tones accompanied by rhythm
by apsarases and gandharvas, as he rode upon the lord of elephants.
He was delighted, absorbed in the joy of listening to Rambhā's sweet music,
his gaze fixed on her lotus-face, adorned with umbrella and chowries.
Seeing that Indra did not notice him, the son of Atri
laughed like an intoxicated man and threw the garland from his own neck onto him.
Because Indra had already been possessed by unrighteous creation,
he, overcome by desire, placed it upon the two frontal globes of his elephant.
Its mind drawn by its fragrance, the king of elephants dragged it with its trunk;

2.9.s: saiva śrīḥ satrilokaṃ tvāṃ hitvā līnā'stu sāgare .. 26 ..

Hearing that word which was like a thunderbolt, at that very moment

2.9.m: He then said to him: 'O Śakra, I am certainly not the sage Gautama!
Know me to be Durvāsas, whose entire essence is impatience!
Those other sages are corrupted; they are your followers.
But I, free from desire, do not count worms like you at all!'
From the blazing mass of matted hair and his gaze crooked with knitted brows,

Then Śrī also disappeared from the three worlds into the ocean;
leaving Indra, the apsarases followed Śrī everywhere.

2.9.s: tapaḥ śaucaṃ dayā satyaṃ pādaḥ saddharmaṛddhayaḥ ..

2.9.m: Austerity, purity, compassion, truth, the quarter [of dharma], the riches of true dharma,
the perfections, strength, and goodness followed Śrī on all sides.
Vehicles such as elephants, ornaments made of gold and the like,
gems, jewels, and metallic utensils were cast away.
Food grains, medicinal plants, and oils diminished in a short time;
no milk remained in the udders of cows, buffaloes, and other animals.
Even the nine treasures were lost from Kubera's abode.
Indra, together with the hosts of immortals, came to resemble ascetics performing austerity.
All objects of enjoyment were lost from the three worlds;
gods, daityas, and mortals were all afflicted with poverty.
Then the moon, bereft of splendor, dissolved into water in the great ocean;
a great drought occurred that destroyed grain and seeds.
Crying out 'Where is food? Where is food?', emaciated with hunger and lacking vigor,
abandoning villages and towns, they dwelt in forests and mountains.
Afflicted by hunger, killing domestic as well as wild beasts,
some ate their flesh, cooked or even raw.
The learned sages, however, who walked the path of true dharma,
though dying of hunger, did not eat flesh.
Then the elder seers, seeing them dedicated to fasting,
instructed them, along with the Manus, in the duties during times of distress taught in the Vedas:
"The sages there, whose senses were mostly agitated by hunger,
grasped the reverse meanings of the esoteric statements of the Vedas,
and understood the primary meaning of words such as aja ('unborn', 'goat') to be goats and the like.

2.9.m: Then they said: 'Perform sacrifices, O twice-born!

2.9.m: The violence ordained by the Veda is not violence that brings guilt;
therefore, slay auspicious beasts intended for the gods and the ancestors.
Sprinkled [with consecrated water] for the deities and offered to the ancestors,

2.9.s: bhuñjata svepsitaṃ māṃsaṃ svārthaṃ tu ghnata mā paśūn ..16..

2.9.m: eat the desired meat; but do not slaughter beasts for your own sake.'"
Instructed by them, the royal sages, divine sages, and men according to their individual capacity,
performed sacrifices, except for the single-minded devotees of Hari.
They performed sacrifices such as the cow sacrifice, the horse sacrifice, and the human sacrifice,
and they ate the meat left over from the sacrifices.
Some performed sacrifices to regain lost fortune,
and some for the sake of wives, sons, houses, and the like, or for their own livelihood.
Those incapable of great sacrifices, however, intending them for the ancestors abundantly,
slaughtered animals in ancestral rites and ate and fed others with the meat.
Some people lived on the banks of rivers and the sea;
catching fish with nets, they became nourished by them.
Having slaughtered beasts—cows, goats, and the like—
they offered them to worthy guests who arrived at their homes, O sage.
Then, anywhere, the rule of endogamous marriages
no longer held, due to the confusion of duties and the lack of wealth, houses, and the like.
Brahmins married daughters of kṣatriyas and others, and kṣatriyas and others married daughters of brahmins,
due to the course of time, for the propagation of their respective lineages.
Thus, sacrifices filled with violence were initiated in this great calamity;
dharma remained merely a semblance, while [true dharma] itself followed Śrī.
Adharma, with its offspring, pervaded all three worlds completely
and grew rapidly, irresistible even to the wise.
And the offspring of these poor people were numerous,
and the expansion of their lineage grew immense in the worlds.

From that time forward, the killing of animals in sacrifices and other rites

2.9.m: After a great period of time, even that king of the gods, together with the gods,

2.9.s: ārādhya saṃpadaṃ prāpa vāsudevaṃ prabhuṃ mune .. 31 ..

2.9.m: having worshipped the Lord Vāsudeva, regained prosperity, O sage.
Then, through the grace of Hari, the husband of Śrī and the abode of dharma,
true dharma was established throughout the three worlds just as before.
Even then, certain sages, kings, gods, and human beings,
their good intellects ruined by greed and the tasting of the flavors of desire and wrath,
regard that duty of times of distress as primary even today.
But those single-minded devotees of the Blessed One who have conquered desire and other vices
did not adopt it even in times of distress, let alone at other times.
Thus, O brahmin, how the introduction of animal sacrifice took place in the first kalpa
due to the exigency of a time of distress upon the earth, has been told by me.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye hiṃsrayajñapravṛttihetunirūpaṇaṃ nāma navamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 9 ..

2.9.m: How was Fortune, which had gone to the ocean, obtained again by Indra, O Skanda? / Tell me all of this story that rests on Nārāyaṇa.
Skanda said:
Deprived of Fortune, the king of the gods, even by the Dānavas who were [likewise] deprived of fortune,
was defeated, stripped of his abode, and had all his possessions lost.
In mountain caves and thickets, and here and there in forests,
he wandered together with the guardians of the directions, Varuṇa and the others.
Clothed in garments of bark and antelope skins, feeding on the flesh of beasts and birds,
the gods, Daityas, humans, and Nāgas had identical conduct and accoutrements.
The vessels in the dwellings of everyone were only earthen;

2.9.s: āsanvarākāḥ sarvepi piśācya iva ca striyaḥ .. 5 ..
2.9.d: आसन्वराकाः सर्वेपि पिशाच्य इव च स्त्रियः .. 5 ..
2.9.m: all the people were wretched, and the women were like goblin-witches.
In the beginning there was a drought of twelve years upon the earth;
afterwards, rain fell in some places in small amounts, and in some places not at all.
Thus a hundred years passed for them amidst the miseries of poverty.
Having powerful past karma already begun, they did not die even in the midst of extreme misery.
They lived like the almost dead, like dwellers in hell within the hells.
Even while striving to obtain Fortune through sacrifices and other means, they did not obtain her.
Then, at the end of a thousand years, they went for refuge to Mount Meru;
because of the curse of Durvāsas, all the gods, [now] ill-clad, went to Brahmā.

2.9.s: praṇamya tasmai duḥkhaṃ svaṃ vāsavādyā nyavedayan ..
2.9.d: प्रणम्य तस्मै दुःखं स्वं वासवाद्या न्यवेदयन् ..
2.9.m: Bowing to him, Indra and the others reported their misery;
for right from the beginning he knew the misfortune of the gods due to his omniscience.
Then, having rebuked Indra, Brahmā, together with Śiva,
unable to avert that misery, wished to propitiate Viṣṇu.
Then, intending to worship with austerity him who is fond of austerity,
he approached the Ocean of Milk, accompanied by the host of all the gods.
On its delightful northern shore, they all, observing a vow of fasting,
standing on one foot with upraised arms, performed austerity.
In their hearts they meditated upon Keśava, the destroyer of all distress,
upon Vāsudeva, the husband of Lakṣmī, with their minds made one-pointed.
Then, at the end of a hundred years, Lord Viṣṇu, glorious Kṛṣṇa himself,
showed compassion to the wretched gods who had fallen into extreme peril.
He whose form is invisible even to knowers of the self through abundant austerities,
manifested there through grace, possessing the radiance of a million suns.
First, suddenly flashing forth, only a great orb of light,
white, dense, and peerless, did all the gods see.
In the middle of it, Brahmā and Śiva saw the husband of Ramā,
dark as a rain-cloud, four-armed, holding a mace, a lotus, and the discus,
adorned with a diadem, girdle, bracelets, earrings, and other ornaments,
clothed in yellow silk, possessing a divine and beautiful form.
Their minds overcome with joy, the two bowed down like a staff;

2.9.s: tadicchayā'tha devāśca dṛṣṭvā taṃ ca mudā''naman .. 2.9.10.20 ..
2.9.d: तदिच्छयाऽथ देवाश्च दृष्ट्वा तं च मुदा'ऽनमन् .. 2.9.10.20 ..
2.9.m: and then, by his will, the gods also, seeing him, bowed with joy.
They became exceedingly joyful, like the penniless upon finding a treasure.

2.9.s: baddhāñjalipuṭāḥ sarve bhaktyā taṃ tuṣṭuvuḥ surāḥ .. 21 ..
2.9.d: बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे भक्त्या तं तुष्टुवुः सुराः .. 21 ..
2.9.m: All the gods, joining their palms in reverence, praised him with devotion:
The gods said:
Oṃ! Homage to the Blessed One, to you, Vāsudeva; we meditate upon [you].
To Pradyumna and Aniruddha, and homage to Saṃkarṣaṇa. // 22
To the one whose form is the syllable Oṃ and Brahman, whose form is manifested in three ways,
to the cause of the creation, sustenance, and dissolution of the cosmic egg, and to the one devoid of qualities. // 23
To the one whose form brings delight to the eyes, who destroys the suffering of those who bow down,
homage to you, Keśava, whose form is the independent sovereign Lord! // 24
To the one who brings joy to all his devotees, who deludes time, māyā, and the rest,
to Kṛṣṇa, eternal bliss, homage to the one abiding in true righteousness! // 25
To the one whose renown is able to deliver those submerged in the ocean of worldly existence,
to you of wondrous form, dark as a rain-cloud, homage! // 26
Bearing mace, lotus, conch, and discus with long arms,
to you, protector of the gods, cows, brahmins, and righteousness, homage, homage! // 27
To the most excellent, bestower of desired boons to those who surrender,
to you, known through the Vedas and scriptures, the womb of the Vedas, homage! // 28
To the one seated in the midst of the orb of light, whose divine form is beautiful,
we bow to you, Viṣṇu, who are higher than the highest! // 29
To the one whose greatness lies far beyond speech and mind, whose form is the imperishable,
to the inner controller of all, and to the immense one, homage, homage! // 2.9.10.30
You alone are the giver of happiness to those who have taken refuge in you; therefore we,
exceedingly afflicted by a great calamity, have approached you for refuge. // 31
Because of our offense toward Durvāsas, your devotee and a devotee of the God of gods,
we have been deprived of fortune and have fallen into this miserable plight. // 32
When we were deprived of clothing, food, drink, abode, and other things, O Lord, even dharma

2.9.s: yato vayaṃ ca dharmaśca tvadīyā iti viśrutāḥ ..

2.9.m: For we and dharma are known to be yours;
therefore, you alone ought to make us happy as before. // 34
Skanda said:
Thus entreated by the gods, the Blessed One, that ocean of compassion,
spoke, delighting the gods with a voice deep as a thundercloud. // 35
The Blessed Lord said:

2.9.s: viditaṃ me surāḥ sarvaṃ kaṣṭaṃ vaḥ sadatikramāt ..

2.9.m: O gods, I know all your distress arising from your offense against a virtuous one.
This very day apply the means that I tell you for its cessation. // 36
Having cast all medicinal herbs into the ocean, using Mount Mandara
with the king of serpents as the churning-rope, churn it together with the asuras. // 37
First making peace with the Danujas, carry out the churning of the ocean.

2.9.s: sāhāyaṃ vaḥ kariṣyāmi khedaḥ kāryo na tatra vaḥ .. 38 ..

2.9.m: I will give you assistance; you need have no distress in that regard. // 38

2.9.s: amṛtaṃ ca śriyo dṛṣṭiṃ prāpya pūrvādhikaujasaḥ ..
2.9.d: अमृतं च श्रियो दृष्टिं प्राप्य पूर्वाधिकौजसः ..
2.9.m: Having obtained the nectar and the glance of Fortune, with your vigor greater than before,
you shall be [victorious]; but the Daityas, being averse to me, shall partake only of misery. // 39
Skanda said:
Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu, who destroys the distress of devotees, vanished.
The gods, having bowed to him, began to do what he had told them. // 2.9.10.40

2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णव खण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्रीवासुदेवप्रसादनिरूपणं नाम दशमोऽध्यायः ..10..

Skanda said:
Brahmā and Rudra, having instructed Mahendra and the others to make peace with the asuras,

2.9.s: ājñāpya jagmatuḥ svaṃsvaṃ dhāma devā rasāṃ mune .. 1 ..
2.9.d: आज्ञाप्य जग्मतुः स्वंस्वं धाम देवा रसां मुने .. 1 ..
2.9.m: departed to their respective abodes, O sage, and the gods [went] to the nether region. // 1
Vāsava, skilled in speaking appropriately for the occasion, using diplomacy and sound reasoning,
and enticing them with a share of the fruit, made an alliance with the asuras. // 2
Then the hosts of gods and asuras met together on the shore of the ocean;
having brought great medicinal herbs, they quickly threw them in abundantly. // 3
Then, approaching Mount Mandara, adorned with various herbs,
all of them, uprooting it from its base, prepared to carry it to the ocean. // 4
[Since it was] eleven thousand yojanas deep in the earth,
they were unable to lift it up; then they praised Hari. // 5
Knowing this, the Blessed One commanded Saṃkarṣaṇa, the sovereign of the earth,
to lift up that mountain that was firmly rooted. // 6
With just a single puff of breath, that Lord immediately
hurled it out from that place to a distance of two yojanas. // 7
Beholding that great wonder, all the gods and asuras were delighted;
making loud shouts, they ran and approached its vicinity. // 8
Though strong and striving, with arms like iron bars,
they were unable to lift it up and carry it away, and became despondent, their labor in vain. // 9
Knowing that the hosts of gods were distressed, the all-seeing Lord
commanded Garuḍa to carry it swiftly to the ocean.
Capable of bearing even the cosmic egg with its coverings in sport,

2.9.s: manovegaḥ sa tatretya nijatroṭyaiva taṃ girim ..
2.9.d: मनोवेगः स तत्रेत्य निजत्रोट्यैव तं गिरिम् ..
2.9.m: he, swift as thought, went there, and with his beak alone [bearing] that mountain,
uprooted it, set it down on the shore of the ocean, and returned to Hari.
Then, their minds filled with joy, all the sons of Kaśyapa
summoned Vāsuki with the promise of a share of the nectar.
He arrived there; then they all prepared to churn the ocean.
The Lord of Waters approached them in embodied form and spoke these words:
"If you gods and asuras will give me a portion of the nectar,
then I shall endure the immense agony of the whirling of Mount Mandara."
Saying "So be it," and having made that promise, they first threw in medicinal herbs and creepers,
and wound the king of serpents around that golden mountain.

2.9.s: tato devā hṛdi hariṃ sasmaruḥ kāryasiddhaye ..
2.9.d: ततो देवा हृदि हरिं सस्मरुः कार्यसिद्धये ..
2.9.m: Then the gods remembered Hari in their hearts for the success of their undertaking.
The moment he was remembered, Acyuta, the all-seeing, arrived there.
Beholding him, the hosts of immortals rejoiced, and taking hold
of the front part of the lord of serpents, they stood there, approved by him.
And the Lord, demonstrating his partiality toward the gods,

2.9.s: yatra devāstatra tasthau tato daityāstu cukrudhuḥ .. 18 ..
2.9.d: यत्र देवास्तत्र तस्थौ ततो दैत्यास्तु चुक्रुधुः .. 18 ..
2.9.m: stood where the gods were; at that the Daityas became enraged:
"We are foremost in austerity, learning, and age; how can we take the lower, inauspicious part

2.9.s: kathaṃ tiraśco gṛhṇīmo nedṛṅmūrkhā vayaṃ tviti .. 19 ..
2.9.d: कथं तिरश्चो गृह्णीमो नेदृङ्मूर्खा वयं त्विति .. 19 ..
2.9.m: of an animal? We are not such fools!"
Then Viṣṇu, together with the gods, as if showing them respect,
smiled, gave them the front part, and made the gods grasp the tail.
This was the deed of the Lord of Śrī to protect the immortals
from the burning blasts of the great serpent's venom; but the Daityas did not understand this.
Then those sons of Kaśyapa lifted up Mount Mandara,
radiant with its ridges of gold, having bound their loincloths with leather straps.
Twenty-two thousand yojanas high,
they placed it in the ocean, shouting aloud in extreme eagerness.
Though held by them, having no base, the mountain, because of its immense weight,
sank immediately to the bottom; then they became utterly distraught.
Then the Lord himself, who by all means fulfills the needs of his devotees,
praised by the immortals, assumed the form of a tortoise and lifted the mountain.
Seeing it rise, the faces and hearts of all blossomed with joy,
and it became firmly fixed upon the vast back of the tortoise.
Then, with swift speed and to the best of their strength, they churned the ocean of waters,
the gods and others pitilessly, their faces hissing with exhaustion.
As the mountain was being whirled, many trees fell from it;
the fire born of the friction of the higher trees burned the lions and other beasts dwelling thereon.
Crushed by the great mountain, various aquatic creatures there
met their destruction by the hundreds in the Ocean of Milk.
Like the roaring of a mass of great clouds at the end of a cosmic age,
a mighty sound of churning arose, amplified by reverberations.
By the hissings from the mouth of Vāsuki, whose body was exhausted from being pulled excessively,
the Daityas, deprived of vigor and utterly worn out, looked like glowing embers.

2.9.s: aviṣahyaṃ viṣāgniṃ ca marṣanti bahudhā muhuḥ ..
2.9.d: अविषह्यं विषाग्निं च मर्षन्ति बहुधा मुहुः ..
2.9.m: Enduring the unbearable fire of poison again and again in various ways,
the thousand faces of the serpent king hung downward.
Instantly, urged by the Lord, the all-pervading
Saṃkarṣaṇa of great splendor supported them, enduring the fire of venom.
After the ocean of milk had been churned for one thousand years,
the hālāhala poison arose, spreading in all directions and intermediate directions.
It is called kālakūṭa, which intensely scorches all worlds;
with their bodies burning from it, they took to flight.
Then Brahmā, the lords of creatures, and all the gods praised the lord of Umā
with hymns, O sage, entreating him to drink it.
Then the Lord said to him: "You are the firstborn among the gods;
and this is the firstborn of the ocean: take this poison, O Śiva."

2.9.s: devānāṃ sa bhayaṃ dṛṣṭvā karuṇaścājñayā hareḥ ..
2.9.d: देवानां स भयं दृष्ट्वा करुणश्चाज्ञया हरेः ..
2.9.m: Seeing the fear of the gods, the compassionate one, by the command of Hari,
drew all the poison onto the palm of his hand by the power of yoga.
He drank it, and instantly held it dried within the middle of his throat.
He became known as Nīlakaṇṭha and was called Śaṃkara.
The drops that fell upon the ground from his hand as he was drinking,
serpents, scorpions, and other creatures, as well as certain herbs, took up.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye'mṛtamanthane viṣotpattirnāmaikādaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 11 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्येऽमृतमन्थने विषोत्पत्तिर्नामैकादशोऽध्यायः .. 11 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, named 'The Origin of the Poison during the Churning for Nectar,' in the Vāsudeva Māhātmya of the second [section], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
Skanda said:
Then, delighted, those sons of Kaśyapa approached the place of churning,
and again for a thousand years they churned the ocean of milk.
Even though the ocean was being churned by all of them in that manner, nothing
came forth; and the churners became weary, with panting mouths.
And the great serpent Vāsuki fell into exhaustion of his vital breath;
even Mount Mandara did not remain steadily fixed in one place during the churning.
Seeing them all dispirited, Pradyumna, by Viṣṇu's command,
entered into the gods, the asuras, and the king of serpents, and infused them with strength.
Aniruddha too at that very moment mounted that lord of mountains
and stood with a thousand arms like another great mountain.
Then, having obtained supreme vigor, they churned with speed,
filled with wonder, those hosts of suras and asuras gladly churning the great ocean.
By the power of Nārāyaṇa, the gods and others felt no exhaustion;
and that churning shone brilliantly then, through their pulling equally together.
As the great ocean was churned, there flowed from all around it then
the saps of great trees and juices of many herbs.
From the ocean thus transformed arose the moon, the repository of the digits,
who is spoken of as the presiding lord of the beauty of all medicinal herbs.
Then the wish-granting cow, the presiding deity of cattle,
the cow providing sacrificial offerings, appeared, possessing a luster like that of the cool-rayed moon.
Then a white horse appeared, the presiding deity of horses;
and Airāvata, the lord of elephants, four-tusked and shining like the moon.
Then came the Pārijāta, the divine tree, the king of trees;
then arose the gem of jewels named Kaustubha, resembling a ruby.
Then arose the apsarases, the abodes of beauty and grace;
then the goddess Surā was born, the presiding deity of all intoxicants.
Next came the bow Śārṅga, the presiding deity over all weapons,
and then arose Pāñcajanya, the conch, the presiding deity of musical instruments.
Thereupon the moon, the Pārijāta, and likewise the host of apsarases
at that moment went to the path of the sun and remained there.
The leaders of the daityas quickly seized the intoxicating wine and the king of horses;
the king of gods took Airāvata with the consent of Hari.
The Kaustubha, the bow, and the conch went straight to Viṣṇu,

2.9.s: havirddhānīṃ tu te sarve tāpasebhyo dadustadā .. 17 ..
2.9.d: हविर्द्धानीं तु ते सर्वे तापसेभ्यो ददुस्तदा .. 17 ..
2.9.m: while they all gave the cow yielding oblations to the ascetics.
As the ocean was churned further, Śrī herself appeared directly,
delighting the three worlds, whose brilliance had been lost, with her glance.
All indeed—gods, asuras, humans, and others—desired to take her;
yet because of her majesty none could approach her.
Then Indra, having recognized her as Śrī by the lotus in her hand,

2.9.s: ānandaṃ paramaṃ prāpa brahmādyā ye ca tadvidaḥ ..2.9.12.20..
2.9.d: आनन्दं परमं प्राप ब्रह्माद्या ये च तद्विदः ..2.9.12.20..
2.9.m: attained supreme joy, as did Brahmā and others who knew her nature.
Meanwhile the ocean came in person, [set] her on a golden seat,
saying 'This is my daughter,' and taking her, sat down with her on his lap.
Though the ocean was churned yet more vigorously by those mighty ones,
who were patient and desirous of the nectar, no nectar appeared at all.
Then, slackening their efforts, hopeless of the nectar's emergence,
the sons of Kaśyapa, O sage, became despondent with withered faces.
Seeing them in that state, the blessed Lord, the ocean of compassion,
the all-pervading one, laughing, prepared himself to churn, O brahmin.
Shining with yellow garments, his loin-cloth securely bound by a jeweled girdle,
he grasped the serpent in the middle with two arms on either side.
The daityas, holding the serpent's head, stood on one side;
all the gods, holding its tail, stood on the other.
And standing between them, the Lord churned the ocean with ease,
giving joy to the eyes, his bracelets glittering on his moving hands.
Then Brahmā, standing in the firmament with the foremost seers,
he showered him with flowers, making shouts of victory.
Then, from the churned ocean, the male Dhanvantari was born,
fair-limbed, from a portion of Viṣṇu, holding a jar of nectar in his hand.
Taking that nectar, which is indeed the highest essence
of all liquids such as clarified butter, he approached the presence of Śrī. // 12.30

2.9.s: samaśramebhyo devebhyo dattvā peyaṃ na cānyathā ..4..

even there, a great tug-of-war broke out among them: // 5

2.9.s: ahaṃ pūrvamahaṃ pūrvaṃ na tvaṃ na tvaṃ pibāmyaham ..
2.9.d: अहं पूर्वमहं पूर्वं न त्वं न त्वं पिबाम्यहम् ..
2.9.m: 'I first! I first! Not you! Not you! I shall drink!'

2.9.d: अथ देवा म्लानवक्त्रा दृष्ट्वा दैत्यैर्हृता सुधाम् ..
2.9.m: Then the gods, their faces withered upon seeing the nectar stolen by the daityas,

2.9.s: pīte'mṛte tu tairadya kiṃ kariṣyāmahe vayam .. 9 ..
2.9.d: पीतेऽमृते तु तैरद्य किं करिष्यामहे वयम् .. 9 ..

Skanda said:
Hearing the distress of the gods, the Blessed Lord, who accomplishes the welfare of his devotees,
said to the gods, 'Do not fear,' and desired to recover the nectar from the asuras. // 13.10

2.9.s: sudhākumbhamimaṃ bhadre gṛhītvā tvaṃ vibhajya naḥ ..
2.9.d: सुधाकुम्भमिमं भद्रे गृहीत्वा त्वं विभज्य नः ..
2.9.m: 'Take this jar of nectar, fair lady, and divide it among us;

2.9.d: इत्युक्त्वा तं ददुस्तस्मै तेऽनिच्छन्त्या अपि स्त्रियै ..
2.9.m: Having spoken thus, they gave it to her, even though the woman was unwilling.

When Mohinī came there and was pouring nectar into his mouth,

With the discus that arrived upon His thought, right then,
the Lord, in the form of the illusory woman, cut off his very large head along with the nectar.
Resembling a mountain peak, swallowing the worlds, and roaring loudly,
Hari placed it as a planet for the peace of the worlds.
Having made the gods drink the nectar, the Lord
assumed His male form; and then the gods fought with the Dānavas.
On the shore of the ocean, a battle [took place] between the gods and the Asuras,
[the gods] being exceedingly strong from drinking the nectar and aided by Viṣṇu.
Being struck down in that tumultuous battle by Nara, Indra, and the others,
the Asuras fled and entered Rasātala.
Meanwhile, the sun set; then all the hosts of gods,
celebrating the great festival of her darśana, approached Śrī.

2.9.m: Rambhā, Ghṛtācī, Viśvācī, Menakā, Tilottamā,
and all the apsarases headed by Urvaśī came there.
All the dwellers of Vaikuṇṭha and likewise the dwellers of Goloka,
the foremost attendants of Viṣṇu, arrived there filled with joy.
The eight perfections beginning with Aṇimā, and the nine
treasures beginning with Śaṅkha and Padma, personified, came near Śrī.
The full autumn moon too, then, for the pleasure of Śrī,
dispelled all the darkness of night; the quarters of the sky became spotless.
Then, by the command of Brahmā, Indra began her consecration; / immediately, Tvaṣṭṛ constructed a most magnificent pavilion,
At once Tvaṣṭṛ constructed a most magnificent pavilion,
with long rows of thousands of jewelled pillars, / adorned with diverse, colourful canopies and plantain trees,
adorned with many colourful canopies and plantain trees,
graced with rows of divine wish-fulfilling trees bending with fragrant flowers, / handsome and captivating with diverse components,
furnished with diverse parts, beautiful to behold, captivating the heart,
gleaming with millions of rows of jewel lamps of pure radiance, / with archways and hanging pearl necklaces.
resplendent with archways and hanging strings of pearls.
Seating Śrī on a jewelled throne there accompanied by song and instrumental music,
the great seers performed the consecration.
Airāvata, Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, Añjana,
Puṣpadanta, Sārvabhauma, and Supratīka, the elephants of the quarters,
trumpeting, consecrated [her] with auspicious waters brought from the four oceans,
drawn up in golden jars.
The great rivers, personified, brought waters there;
the Vedas in bodily form, along with the seers, chanted mantras.
Sweet-voiced Gandharvas sang, and hosts of apsarases danced;
other hosts of gods then played musical instruments.
Great joy then arose among all embodied beings in the three worlds.
The brahmins recited the Śrīsūkta and other hymns, and the women sang songs.
Gongs, cymbals, mṛdaṅga drums, paṇavas, ānakas, and gomukha horns,
they sounded; and the clouds thundered like kettle-drums in the sky.
Then there was a shower of flowers accompanied by shouts of victory,
and the wives of Dharma and the supernatural perfections attended upon her.
Then, to her who was well-bathed, two yellow silken garments,
priceless, the ocean gave, and abundant jewel-ornaments.
Indra brought a seat fit for her to sit upon.
Viśvakarman gave bracelets and rings set with precious gems.
The Moon, her brother, gave an excellent nose-ornament;
he likewise gave her a hair-ornament studded with excellent jewels.
The lotus-born Brahmā gave a lotus, Sarasvatī a pearl necklace,
and the Nāgas, headed by Śeṣa, gave her two kingly jewel-earrings.
Durgā gave collyrium and saffron, the mark of marital felicity;
Sāvitrī gave a forehead ornament, and Śacī a betel-box.
The Spring gave flower garlands, and Śaṃkara a neck-string.
The wielder of the noose gave the Vaijayantī garland, and Kubera a jeweled mirror.
Fire gave a priceless bodice, and Yama gave an auspicious fan.
Others too presented her with ornaments suited for that occasion.
Then, considering, "To whom shall I give this adorned maiden?"

2.9.s: siṃdhuḥ papraccha brahmāṇaṃ tadovāca sa sarvavit ..32 ..

2.9.m: the ocean asked Brahmā. Then the all-knowing one said to him:

2.9.s: kanyā taveyamambhodhe mātā mama śivasya ca ..
2.9.d: कन्या तवेयमम्भोधे माता मम शिवस्य च ..
2.9.m: "O ocean, this daughter of yours is the mother of myself and of Śiva,
and indeed of all the gods and worlds; this is certain.
Except for Nārāyaṇa, Vāsudeva, the Supreme Brahman, the Lord of all,
the Supreme Spirit alone, she has no other husband.
Therefore, to the Lord Himself, the cause of joy to the three worlds,
who has arrived and is seated, give her according to the rites, O ocean.
Make your birth fruitful, purifying your lineage.
Deliver [yourself] from the ocean of worldly existence by giving her to the Supreme Self.
Though one, you are renowned in seven forms according to the division of the seven continents;
now, having done this, you will attain great renown."
Addressed thus by Brahmā, the ocean, overjoyed, with his hair standing on end,
deeming himself blessed, wished to give his daughter to Viṣṇu.

2.9.s: tataḥ sahaiva vidhinā sa saṃprārthya tamīśvaram ..
2.9.d: ततः सहैव विधिना स संप्रार्थ्य तमीश्वरम् ..
2.9.m: Then, having implored that Lord along with Brahmā,
he performed the solemn betrothal and then carried out the wedding rites.
Dhanvantari, the Moon, and the gods headed by Indra
were on the ocean’s side at that wedding festival.
In giving garments, ornaments, conveyances, and the like, in the serving of food,

2.9.s: sanmānane ca janyānāṃ mukhyā āsaṃsta eva hi .. 41 ..

2.9.m: and in honoring the members of the wedding party, they indeed took the lead.
And in the auspicious rites for Lakṣmī, the foremost women there
were the rivers headed by Gaṅgā, and celestial damsels headed by Śacī,
the mountain-wives headed by Menā, and the supernatural perfections such as Aṇimā,
the wife of the Moon, Kanti, and all the apsarases, O sage.
Then, adorning the wedding play of the all-pervading Nārāyaṇa,
Brahmā, upon reflection, appointed Dharma and Mūrti as the parents [of the groom]:
"This Dharma is the support of the world, worthy of worship by all embodied beings;
he is fit to be his father, and he has great affection for him.
And this renowned Mūrti, the birthplace of all good qualities,
the daughter of Dakṣa and wife of Dharma, is worthy to be his mother."
Then on Dharma's side, too, the following were foremost in the duties:
Śaṃkara together with Nandīśvara and Gaṇeśa, O sage;
the great seers headed by Marīci, the lords of creatures, the sage Nārada,
the son of Vinatā [Garuḍa], and the attendants headed by Nanda and Śrīdāman.

2.9.m: Durgā and Sarasvatī, mother of the Vedas, were foremost among the women,

Brahmā together with the Vedas and other [scriptures] was on both sides,
as were the Vedic brahmins who were experts in the rites of marriage.
Then, through the grace of Lakṣmī alone, the ocean
procured all the provisions instantly, causing wonder among the gods.
Whatever he envisioned in his mind was brought forth.
he saw instantly right before him; therefore he became exceedingly glad.
In the middle of the pavilion, he caused
an altar for establishing the sacred fire to be built according to the rule by brahmins versed in the Vedas.
He adorned that altar with perfumes, flowers, unbroken grains, and the like,
with various auspicious colors, and with water-jars having sprouts.
Then, having been ceremonially bathed by the lords of sages accompanied by mantras to the sounds of greatly auspicious musical instruments,

2.9.m: having kindled the fire according to rule, he made offerings into it together with the great sages.
Having given to him his lovely daughter, whose gaze was fixed solely upon his lotus feet,

2.9.m: Seated together on a single seat, the lovely mother and father of the universe

2.9.m: The hosts of heavenly women, divided into two groups and seated facing each other,
eager to gaze upon the couple, sang with an abundance of love,
such that, hearing it, all the gods, the great seers, and all the women

2.9.m: Having bowed with devotion and gladly offered excellent unbroken grains and other gifts to the two,
the gods, humble with palms joined, praised them individually with powerful words.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye lakṣmīnārāyaṇavivāhotsavanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 14 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये लक्ष्मीनारायणविवाहोत्सवनिरूपणं नाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः .. 14 ..

Brahmā said:

2.9.s: vicāryyā'haṃ vedānmuhurupagato niścayamimaṃ ramārāme bhaktistvayi dṛḍhatarā yarhyasubhṛtām ..
2.9.d: विचार्य्याऽहं वेदान्मुहुरुपगतो निश्चयमिमं रमारामे भक्तिस्त्वयि दृढतरा यर्ह्यसुभृताम् ..
2.9.m: "Having repeatedly reflected upon the Vedas, I have arrived at this conclusion: O delight of Ramā, when living beings have very firm devotion to you,

2.9.s: bhavettarhyevaiṣāṃ kṣayavirahitā bhoganikarāstathā syurlokā vai paramapuruṣātyaṃtikagatiḥ .. .. 1 ..
2.9.d: भवेत्तर्ह्येवैषां क्षयविरहिता भोगनिकरास्तथा स्युर्लोका वै परमपुरुषात्यंतिकगतिः .. .. 1 ..
2.9.m: only then do imperishable masses of pleasures, the eternal worlds, and the ultimate goal, the Supreme Person, belong to them.
Not knowing this, however, people filled with passion and darkness worship even us gods, O Hari, through various paths of austerity and rites;

2.9.s: ta evoktā mūḍhāḥ kṣayarahitasaukhyaṃ na kuhacillabhante'tastvāṃ vai nijahṛdi dadhe keśavamaham ..2..

2.9.m: they are called fools; nowhere do they obtain imperishable happiness. Therefore, I hold you alone, Keśava, in my heart."
Śaṃkara said:

2.9.m: "The three Vedas, Sāṃkhya, Vedānta, Yoga, the Purāṇa, and likewise the Pañcarātra, O Lord, and the treatises on dharma—
they constantly sing with devotion only your supreme majesty, who are one, in manifold ways.
From you alone, O Lord, the Infinite One, did these scriptures arise in the primeval kalpa, having you as their sole foundation;

2.9.s: ramāsevyapādāmbujaṃ śāstrayoniṃ tamādyaṃ bhavantaṃ bhaje vāsudevam .. 4 ..
2.9.d: रमासेव्यपादाम्बुजं शास्त्रयोनिं तमाद्यं भवन्तं भजे वासुदेवम् .. 4 ..
2.9.m: I worship you, the primeval Vāsudeva, whose lotus feet are served by Ramā, who are the source of scriptures.
Dharma said:
"Your tale, liberating from the bonds of worldly existence, is indeed nectar to embodied souls scorched by the threefold miseries;
destroying the heap of sins of many births, it quickly expands devotion and knowledge of you.

2.9.s: sadaiva sā karṇapathena hṛddarī viśatvanantābhidha sammukhodgatā ..
2.9.d: सदैव सा कर्णपथेन हृद्दरी विशत्वनन्ताभिध सम्मुखोद्गता ..
2.9.m: May it, issuing from the mouth of your devotees, always enter the cave of my heart through the path of the ears, O You whose name is Infinite;

2.9.s: mama tvadanyā haratācca vāsanā dayābdhaye te prabhaviṣṇave namaḥ .. 6 ..
2.9.d: मम त्वदन्या हरताच्च वासना दयाब्धये ते प्रभविष्णवे नमः .. 6 ..
2.9.m: and may it dispel desires other than for you. Homage to you, the ocean of compassion, the all-powerful Lord."
The Prajāpatis said:

2.9.s: dhanyā ete kalpavṛkṣā yadīyāṃ chāyāmetāmāśritastvaṃ sahaśrīḥ ..
2.9.d: धन्या एते कल्पवृक्षा यदीयां छायामेतामाश्रितस्त्वं सहश्रीः ..
2.9.m: "Blessed are these wish-fulfilling trees, whose shade you have resorted to along with Śrī;

2.9.s: dhanyaḥ kartā maṇḍapasyāsya te vai dhanyaiṣā bhūryatra pīṭhaṃ taveśa .. 7 ..
2.9.d: धन्यः कर्ता मण्डपस्यास्य ते वै धन्यैषा भूर्यत्र पीठं तवेश .. 7 ..
2.9.m: blessed indeed is the maker of this pavilion for you, and blessed is this ground where your throne is placed, O Lord!

2.9.s: dhanyo loke nūnameṣomburāśiḥ sākṣāttubhyaṃ yena dattā svakanyā ..
2.9.d: धन्यो लोके नूनमेषोम्बुराशिः साक्षात्तुभ्यं येन दत्ता स्वकन्या ..
2.9.m: Blessed indeed in this world is this ocean, by whom his own daughter was given directly to you;

2.9.s: dhanyāścaite tvāṃ vayaṃ vīkṣamāṇā dhanyeśānaṃ śrīpatiṃ tvāṃ natāḥ smaḥ .. 8 ..
2.9.d: धन्याश्चैते त्वां वयं वीक्षमाणा धन्येशानं श्रीपतिं त्वां नताः स्मः .. 8 ..
2.9.m: and blessed are we who behold you; we bow to you, the blessed Lord, the husband of Śrī."
The Manus said:

2.9.s: dharmaḥ khalu sa hi paramo dharmebhyo mādhava sakalebhyopi ..
2.9.d: धर्मः खलु स हि परमो धर्मेभ्यो माधव सकलेभ्योपि ..
2.9.m: "That indeed is the highest duty among all duties, O Mādhava,

2.9.s: bhaktirbhavati yato vai dharmabhuvi tvayi hi niravadyā .. 9 ..
2.9.d: भक्तिर्भवति यतो वै धर्मभुवि त्वयि हि निरवद्या .. 9 ..
2.9.m: from which unblemished devotion to you arises on the field of dharma.
O Blessed One, the soul of dharma, the bearer of dharma's burden, and the protector of dharma,
to whom dharma is exceedingly dear beyond all, we praise you, the source of dharma."
The seers said:

2.9.s: bhaktyā hīnastvadvimukho vayunārthī śrāmyanbhūyopyasya na siddhiṃ samupaiti ..
2.9.d: भक्त्या हीनस्त्वद्विमुखो वयुनार्थी श्राम्यन्भूयोप्यस्य न सिद्धिं समुपैति ..
2.9.m: "One who is devoid of devotion, turned away from you, yet seeking knowledge, though toiling repeatedly, does not attain success in it;

2.9.s: tarhyāsaktaḥ karmaṇi kāmye tu kutosau saukhyaṃ yāyādakṣayamānandamahābdhe .. 11 ..
2.9.d: तर्ह्यासक्तः कर्मणि काम्ये तु कुतोसौ सौख्यं यायादक्षयमानन्दमहाब्धे .. 11 ..
2.9.m: how then could one attached to desire-prompted action attain imperishable happiness, O great ocean of bliss?

2.9.s: bhaktyā nityaṃ tvāmata eva vayaṃ vai śraddhāyuktā dharmataponigamādyaiḥ ..
2.9.d: भक्त्या नित्यं त्वामत एव वयं वै श्रद्धायुक्ता धर्मतपोनिगमाद्यैः ..
2.9.m: Therefore, through dharma, austerity, the Vedas, and the like, endowed with faith, we constantly
meditate with devotion on you alone—beyond māyā, the controller of time, the noble Lord, the beloved of Śrī, higher than the highest."
Indra said:

2.9.s: bhagavannuruduḥkhitā vayaṃ nanu durvāsasa eva helanāt ..
2.9.d: भगवन्नुरुदुःखिता वयं ननु दुर्वासस एव हेलनात् ..
2.9.m: "O Blessed One, we were deeply afflicted indeed due to our slighting of Durvāsas.

2.9.s: na bhavantamṛte'vituṃ hi no vidhirudrapramukhā ime'śakan .. 13 ..
2.9.d: न भवन्तमृतेऽवितुं हि नो विधिरुद्रप्रमुखा इमेऽशकन् .. 13 ..
2.9.m: Without you, these [gods] headed by Brahmā and Rudra were truly unable to protect us.
Bereft of all wealth, devoid of food, reduced to the level of low wretches on earth,

2.9.s: bhavataiva vayaṃ hṛtāpadaḥ smaḥ sapadi śrīharaye namostu tubhyam .. 14 ..
2.9.d: भवतैव वयं हृतापदः स्मः सपदि श्रीहरये नमोस्तु तुभ्यम् .. 14 ..
2.9.m: we have instantly had our misfortune removed by you alone. Praise be to you, O Śrī Hari!
Agni said:

2.9.s: gīrvāṇadānavanarādyupajīvanānnaṃ yannirmitaṃ hi bhavataiva tato budhāstu ..
2.9.d: गीर्वाणदानवनराद्युपजीवनान्नं यन्निर्मितं हि भवतैव ततो बुधास्तु ..
2.9.m: Since food, the sustenance of gods, dānavas, humans, and others, was created by you alone, the wise

2.9.s: yajñeṣu tena yajanaṃ tava kurvate'tho tvaccheṣamanyadiviṣadbhya upānayanti .. 15 ..
2.9.d: यज्ञेषु तेन यजनं तव कुर्वतेऽथो त्वच्छेषमन्यदिविषद्भ्य उपानयन्ति .. 15 ..
2.9.m: perform worship of you with it in sacrifices, and then offer your remnants to the other gods of heaven.

2.9.s: kāmyeṣu karmasu ratā api yājñikāste tatkarmabandhanata āśu vimucya yānti ..
2.9.d: काम्येषु कर्मसु रता अपि याज्ञिकास्ते तत्कर्मबन्धनत आशु विमुच्य यान्ति ..
2.9.m: Even those sacrificers engaged in desire-prompted rites are quickly freed from the bondage of those actions and attain

2.9.s: brāhmīṃ gatiṃ taditare tu bhavanti caurāḥ śrīyajñapūruṣamahaṃ praṇamāmi taṃ tvām .. 16 ..
2.9.d: ब्राह्मीं गतिं तदितरे तु भवन्ति चौराः श्रीयज्ञपूरुषमहं प्रणमामि तं त्वाम् .. 16 ..
2.9.m: the state of Brahman; but those other than them are thieves. I bow down to that you, the auspicious Spirit of sacrifice.
The Maruts said:

2.9.s: bhaktā ekāntikāste'kṣaraparamapade sevayā te tu hīnaṃ vāsaiśvaryādi necchantyatiśayitasukhaṃ nāpi kaivalyamokṣam ..
2.9.d: भक्ता एकान्तिकास्तेऽक्षरपरमपदे सेवया ते तु हीनं वासैश्वर्यादि नेच्छन्त्यतिशयितसुखं नापि कैवल्यमोक्षम् ..
2.9.m: Your exclusive devotees in the imperishable supreme abode do not desire residence, sovereignty, and the like, nor exalted pleasure devoid of service to you, nor even the liberation of isolation.

2.9.s: tadyuktaṃ tvātmanopi śvapacakulajanurmānayantyuttamaṃ vai taṃ tvāmekāntadharmāśrayaṇamupagatāḥ śrīmahāpūruṣaṃ smaḥ .. 17 ..
2.9.d: तद्युक्तं त्वात्मनोपि श्वपचकुलजनुर्मानयन्त्युत्तमं वै तं त्वामेकान्तधर्माश्रयणमुपगताः श्रीमहापूरुषं स्मः .. 17 ..
2.9.m: Connected with that [service], they consider even birth in an outcaste dog-cooker's family to be truly superior for themselves; we have approached that you, the auspicious Great Person, the refuge of exclusive duty.
The Siddhas said:
To you, the uncaused cause of the creation and other states of multiple universes,
abiding within them and distinct from them, the controller, we bow down.

2.9.s: rudrā ūcuḥ .. māyāyāḥ sarvamohinyā mohanaṃ mohavarjitam ..
2.9.d: रुद्रा ऊचुः .. मायायाः सर्वमोहिन्या मोहनं मोहवर्जितम् ..
2.9.m: The Rudras said: / We bow to you, the infatuator of Māyā who deludes all, yet free from delusion,
the Death of even Mahākāla, the Supreme Person.
The Ādityas said:

2.9.s: prakāśitā yena vayaṃ jaganti prakāśayāmo bhavatā rameśa ..
2.9.d: प्रकाशिता येन वयं जगन्ति प्रकाशयामो भवता रमेश ..
2.9.m: Illuminated by whom we illuminate the worlds, by you, O Lord of Ramā,
we bow down to you, self-luminous, of vast brilliance, whose form is light.
The Sādhyas said:

2.9.s: śāstā nṛpāṇāṃ ca mahoragāṇāṃ daityādhipānāṃ ca surādhipānām ..
2.9.d: शास्ता नृपाणां च महोरगाणां दैत्याधिपानां च सुराधिपानाम् ..
2.9.m: The ruler of kings, of great serpents, of the lords of Daityas, and of the lords of gods;

2.9.s: tvaṃ vai manūnāṃ ca prajāpatīnāṃ rājādhirājāya namostu tubhyam .. .. 21 ..
2.9.d: त्वं वै मनूनां च प्रजापतीनां राजाधिराजाय नमोस्तु तुभ्यम् .. .. 21 ..
2.9.m: indeed, of Manus and of Prajāpatis: homage be to you, King of kings!
The Vasus said:
Whenever on earth a great slaughter of the righteous keepers of the celebrated eternal duty is caused by fractions of asuras,

2.9.s: kadanamuru tadātadā svayaṃ te hyavatarate praṇamāma dharmagoptre .. 22 ..
2.9.d: कदनमुरु तदातदा स्वयं ते ह्यवतरते प्रणमाम धर्मगोप्त्रे .. 22 ..
2.9.m: then and then you yourself descend. We bow to the protector of dharma.
The Cāraṇas said:

2.9.s: caritraṃ śubhaṃ te dhṛtānekamūrtteḥ prabandhairanekairhi gāyanti bhaktāḥ ..
2.9.d: चरित्रं शुभं ते धृतानेकमूर्त्तेः प्रबन्धैरनेकैर्हि गायन्ति भक्ताः ..
2.9.m: Devotees sing in various compositions the auspicious deeds of you, who have assumed manifold forms;

2.9.s: yadu śrotṛvaktṝnpunātyeva sadyo vayaṃ taṃ natāḥ puṇyakīrttiṃ bhavantam .. 23 ..
2.9.d: यदु श्रोतृवक्तॄन्पुनात्येव सद्यो वयं तं नताः पुण्यकीर्त्तिं भवन्तम् .. 23 ..
2.9.m: which immediately purifies listeners and speakers alike, to that you of virtuous renown we bow.
The Gandharvas and Apsarases said:

2.9.s: ye kathāste vihāyānyagāthāḥ prabho kīrttayante'tha śṛṇvanti vā te janāḥ ..
2.9.d: ये कथास्ते विहायान्यगाथाः प्रभो कीर्त्तयन्तेऽथ शृण्वन्ति वा ते जनाः ..
2.9.m: Those people, O Lord, who abandon stories of you and praise or listen to other songs,

2.9.s: duḥkhitāḥ syuśca saṃsārapāśaiḥ sitāstaṃ natāḥ smaḥ śaraṇyaṃ bhavantaṃ vayam .. 24 ..
2.9.d: दुःखिताः स्युश्च संसारपाशैः सितास्तं नताः स्मः शरण्यं भवन्तं वयम् .. 24 ..
2.9.m: become miserable, bound by the fetters of saṃsāra. We have bowed down to you, the refuge.
The Ocean said:

2.9.s: ajita tavā'tha tāvakajanasya mudā'lpamapi draviṇa jalānnavastranamanānyatamena sakṛt ..
2.9.d: अजित तवाऽथ तावकजनस्य मुदाऽल्पमपि द्रविण जलान्नवस्त्रनमनान्यतमेन सकृत् ..
2.9.m: O Unconquered One, if a person gladly performs even slight service to you or to your devotee, even once, by means of wealth, water, food, clothing, or bowing,

2.9.s: carati ha sevanaṃ sa padavīṃ mahatīṃ mahatāṃ vrajati janolpakopi tamahaṃ praṇataḥ karuṇam .. 25 ..
2.9.d: चरति ह सेवनं स पदवीं महतीं महतां व्रजति जनोल्पकोपि तमहं प्रणतः करुणम् .. 25 ..
2.9.m: even if he is insignificant, he attains the exalted status of the great; I bow to that compassionate one.
The Attendants said:
You are our ancestors, you are our kinsman, you are our revered teacher, friend, and master of our soul;

2.9.s: tvamasīśvara eva ca naḥ paramastvamasi draviṇaṃ sakalaṃ tvamasi .. .. 26 ..
2.9.d: त्वमसीश्वर एव च नः परमस्त्वमसि द्रविणं सकलं त्वमसि .. .. 26 ..
2.9.m: you are our supreme Lord, you are our wealth, you are our everything.
Mūrti said:

2.9.s: yatsaṃbandhata eva yānti padavīmuccāṃ mahadbhirnnutāṃ strīśūdrāsuranīcapakṣipaśavaḥ pāpātmajīvā api ..
2.9.d: यत्संबन्धत एव यान्ति पदवीमुच्चां महद्भिर्न्नुतां स्त्रीशूद्रासुरनीचपक्षिपशवः पापात्मजीवा अपि ..
2.9.m: By connection with whom even women, śūdras, asuras, low birds and beasts, and beings born of sin attain an exalted station praised by the great;

2.9.s: yaddhīnā vibudheśvarā api bhavantyarccojjhitāstatkṣaṇaṃ golokādhipatiṃ tameva hṛdaye nityaṃ bhaje tvāmaham .. 27 ..
2.9.d: यद्धीना विबुधेश्वरा अपि भवन्त्यर्च्चोज्झितास्तत्क्षणं गोलोकाधिपतिं तमेव हृदये नित्यं भजे त्वामहम् .. 27 ..
2.9.m: deprived of whom even the lords of the gods become immediately abandoned by worship: I continually worship in my heart that very Lord of Goloka, you.
Sāvitrī said:

2.9.s: tvaṃ sargakāle prakṛtiṃ ca pūruṣaṃ dṛṣṭyā svayotthāpya tatastadātmanā ..
2.9.d: त्वं सर्गकाले प्रकृतिं च पूरुषं दृष्ट्या स्वयोत्थाप्य ततस्तदात्मना ..
2.9.m: At the time of creation, having awakened prakṛti and puruṣa by your glance, then, through them,
having created the principles beginning with mahat, you created multiple cosmic beings in many ways through those presiding deities.
Assuming the role of the creator of the world in the form of the Virāj, [creating] gods, asuras, humans, and serpents,
you made the motionless and moving, O Lord. I have taken refuge in you, the primal creator.
Durgā said:

2.9.s: priyatayā'dhikayā hṛdi cintanaṃ vidadhate tava ye bhuvi te vibho ..
2.9.d: प्रियतयाऽधिकया हृदि चिन्तनं विदधते तव ये भुवि ते विभो ..
2.9.m: Those on earth who perform contemplation of you in their heart with supreme love, O All-pervading One,

2.9.s: na parameṣṭhisukhaṃ na divaḥ sukhaṃ na kamayanti dharaikanareśatām .. 2.9.15.30 ..
2.9.d: न परमेष्ठिसुखं न दिवः सुखं न कमयन्ति धरैकनरेशताम् .. 2.9.15.30 ..
2.9.m: do not desire the bliss of Brahmā, nor the bliss of heaven, nor sole kingship over the earth.

2.9.s: prasabhamarpitamapyatulaṃ tvayā sukhamidaṃ samavāpya ca tatra te ..
2.9.d: प्रसभमर्पितमप्यतुलं त्वया सुखमिदं समवाप्य च तत्र ते ..
2.9.m: Even when this peerless bliss is forcibly granted by you and attained,

2.9.s: tadapahāya na śaktikṛtaḥ kṣaṇaṃ tamu namāmi ca sātvatanāyakam .. 31 ..
2.9.d: तदपहाय न शक्तिकृतः क्षणं तमु नमामि च सात्वतनायकम् .. 31 ..
2.9.m: they are unable to abandon that [contemplation] even for a moment; I bow to that leader of the Sātvatas.
The Rivers said:

2.9.s: varada namanamātraṃ nāmasaṃkīrtanaṃ vā vidadhati tava ye vai jñānato'jñānato vā ..
2.9.d: वरद नमनमात्रं नामसंकीर्तनं वा विदधति तव ये वै ज्ञानतोऽज्ञानतो वा ..
2.9.m: O Granter of boons, those who perform mere bowing or chanting of your name, whether knowingly or unknowingly—

2.9.s: janimṛtiyamabhītestānapi trāyamāṇaṃ narasakhamupayātāḥ smo'dya nārāyaṇaṃ tvām .. 32 ..
2.9.d: जनिमृतियमभीतेस्तानपि त्रायमाणं नरसखमुपयाताः स्मोऽद्य नारायणं त्वाम् .. 32 ..
2.9.m: we have today approached you, Nārāyaṇa, the companion of Nara, who protects even them from the fear of birth, death, and Yama.
The Wives of the Gods said:
The birth of you who have assumed a form on earth is auspicious, and your conduct is marvelous and purifying to the world;

2.9.s: bhavati nirguṇaṃ sarvameva te bhavasi nirguṇabrahma yatparam .. 33 ..
2.9.d: भवति निर्गुणं सर्वमेव ते भवसि निर्गुणब्रह्म यत्परम् .. 33 ..
2.9.m: all of yours is free from the guṇas, because you are the supreme Brahman beyond the guṇas.

2.9.s: tava samāśrayāttāmasā janā api ca rājasāḥ sāttvikāśca ye ..
2.9.d: तव समाश्रयात्तामसा जना अपि च राजसाः सात्त्विकाश्च ये ..
2.9.m: Through refuge in you, people who are tāmasic, rājasic, or sāttvic

2.9.s: nanu bhavanti te nirguṇāstato vayamupāsmahe tvāṃ hi nirguṇam .. 34 ..
2.9.d: ननु भवन्ति ते निर्गुणास्ततो वयमुपास्महे त्वां हि निर्गुणम् .. 34 ..
2.9.m: indeed become beyond the guṇas; therefore, we worship you who are transcending the guṇas.
The Wives of the Seers said:
Of Viṣṇu alone is the pacification of all afflictions for those distressed by great sins and the three kinds of suffering.

2.9.s: pādābjaṃ tava bhavatīti tadvayaṃ vai prāptāḥ smaḥ śaraṇamananta devadeva .. 35 ..
2.9.d: पादाब्जं तव भवतीति तद्वयं वै प्राप्ताः स्मः शरणमनन्त देवदेव .. 35 ..
2.9.m: Your lotus foot, O infinite God of gods, is that [refuge]! / Therefore, we have indeed sought refuge in it. // 35
The Earth said:
Whose face is like the full autumn moon, whose eyes are long like the petals of an autumn lotus,
Who delivers from manifold distress born of separation from Śrī—to that sole Vāsudeva I take refuge. // 36
Sarasvatī said:

having crossed these, each tenfold greater than the last, he reached the wondrous Goloka,
that abode full of splendour, attainable only by exclusive devotees of Hari.
As he went, he saw the wide, unfathomable Virajā river,
fragrant with sandal paste washed off in the bathing of groups of gopīs and gopas,

Its enchanting bank, made of immense crystal stones,
shining with excellent gems—white, green, red, and yellow—he reached;

embellished with mines of jewels such as the Syamantaka and sapphires,

frequented by sweetly chirping swans, kāraṇḍava ducks, and other birds,

2.9.s: vṛndaiḥ kāmadughānāṃ ca gajendrāṇāṃ ca vājinām ..

Having crossed the divine river, then instantly, by the will of the Lord,

made of gold, worthy of sight, one crore yojanas high,
and ten crores of yojanas in width, captivating the mind,
shining with thousands of wish-fulfilling trees, pārijāta and other trees,
with mallikā and yūthikā jasmines, and with clove and cardamom creepers,
with golden plantains and various other trees,
with divine herds of deer, elephants, and sweet-singing birds.
On the delightful ridges of that [mountain] which served as a fortress for that abode,
he beheld vast and charming pavilions for the Lord's rāsa dance,
surrounded by rows of gardens fragrant with blooming flowers,
beautified with four gates having doors studded with jewels,
provided with wonderful archways and thousands of jewelled pillars,
furnished with banana trunks and canopies with hanging pearls,
provided with dūrvā grass, parched grains, unbroken rice, fruits, and auspicious articles,
their courtyards sprinkled with sandal, agallochum, musk, and saffron,
charming with the diverse, melodious sounds of musical instruments.
