2.9.m: In them he saw millions of groups of gopīs,
adorned with priceless garments and ornaments, fine jewel-encrusted bracelets,
girdles, anklets, armlets, and rings,
incomparable indeed in youth, beauty, grace, and voices,
sharing the complexion of Rādhā and Lakṣmī, skilled in amorous arts.
In the pavilions filled with various articles of enjoyment,
they sport and sing charming songs of Kṛṣṇa.
Then in the foothills of that mountain, the sage Nārada,
O Sāvarṇi, saw that great forest named Vṛndāvana,
the beloved sporting ground of Kṛṣṇa and Rādhikā,
delightful with rows of wish-fulfilling trees and ponds filled with lotuses,
shining with various trees bending under the weight of fruits and flowers— / mangoes, hog-plums, nīpas, jujubes, pomegranates,
date palms, areca palms, oranges, coconuts, sandalwoods,
rose apples, citrons, jackfruits, walnuts, celestial pines,
plantains, campakas, grapes, and golden ketakas—
bending under the weight of fruits and flowers, shining with diverse trees,
with mallikā, mādhavī, kunda, clove, and yūthikā [creepers],
served by a gentle, cool, and fragrant breeze,
moist all around with waterfalls flowing from Śataśṛṅga,
rich with the beauty of perpetual spring, adorned with rows of jewel-lamps,
abounding in countless bowers supplied with erotic articles.
resounding everywhere, O sage, with the repeated chanting of Kṛṣṇa's praises by cowherds and gopīs,
with the lowing of cows and calves and the chirping of birds, with the sounds of various ornaments,
and with the churning of curds.
Endowed with thirty-two other forests, enchanting to behold,
adorned with various trees bending under blossoming flowers and fruits,
having seen that, overjoyed, he reached the radiant city of Goloka,
circular, with ramparts of jewels, and adorned with royal highways,
resplendent with crores of aerial chariots of Kṛṣṇa's devotees,
and with chariots studded with supreme jewels and adorned with nets of small tinkling bells,
charming with crores of wondrous mansions standing in rows,
adorned with heaps of great gems and rows of jeweled pillars,
fashioned from the essence of jewels, with delightful pleasure pavilions,
radiant with rows of lamps of supreme gems and with jeweled altars,
smeared with liquids of saffron, agallochum, musk, and red powder,
its courtyards adorned with curds, dūrvā grass, parched grain, betel nuts, and plantain trees,
made auspicious with golden jars filled with water and arched gateways,
its paved gem royal avenues bustling with numerous elephants and horses.
The sage rejoiced upon beholding that great highway densely crowded
with lords of numerous universes—headed by Brahmā and Śaṃkara—who had arrived for the darśana of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, holding offerings in hand,
and with throngs of cowherds and gopīs going to see Kṛṣṇa.
Beholding that great highway so crowded, the sage rejoiced.
Then he reached Kṛṣṇa's temple, wonderful in every way and enchanting,
surrounded by rows of palaces of cowherds such as Nanda and Vṛṣabhānu,
having sixteen gates, moated fortresses,
guarded by individual doorkeepers, each surrounded by a crore of cowherds.
At the gates standing before him, with doors and pillars of jewels,
he saw the doorkeepers seated in order:
Vīrabhānu, Candrabhānu, Sūryabhānu the third,
Vasubhānu, Devabhānu, and next Śakrabhānu,
Ratnabhānu, Supārśva, and then Viśāla and Ṛṣabha,

having crossed beyond the six cakras within themselves,

Illumined by its light, the sun, fire, moon, and stars

This the Sātvatas call Brahmapura, the abode of the Lord,

2.9.m: whom some call Brahman, others Bhagavān, and devotees Viṣṇu and the Supreme Lord.
whose limbs are more enchanting than thousands of Kāmadevas, who is ever youthful, an ocean of compassion,

Having beheld that most wondrous divine form, his senses completely captivated by its beauty and fragrance, / with sight obstructed by tears of bliss and his hair standing on end in love, he became filled with joy.
With his sight blocked by tears of joy, his hair standing on end with love, he was filled with bliss.
Bowing to him like a staff, Nārada, overcome with love,
stood with hands folded in reverence, gazing upon his face.
Hari honored him, having respectfully inquired after his welfare—
the sage who was his exclusive devotee, whom he himself had wished to see.
Having regained his composure through tasting the nectar of the Lord's words,
the sage, filled with the great bliss of beholding him, praised him with devotion.
Nārada said:
Victory to you, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, O Nārāyaṇa, O Lord of the universe!
O Vāsudeva, abode of all, ever beloved to exclusive devotees!
You whose wondrous feet are worshiped by Rādhikā, Kamalā, and the rest,
are indeed the supreme goal for those who seek ultimate good.
You are the eternal Self of eternal souls, the conscious animating the conscious.
Higher than both the perishable and the imperishable, you are supreme Brahman, O Hari!

2.9.s: yathā viśuddhiḥ siddhiśca bhaktyā paramayā tava ..
2.9.d: यथा विशुद्धिः सिद्धिश्च भक्त्या परमया तव ..
2.9.m: Just as purity and perfection come through supreme devotion to you,
it cannot be so for men through other means such as austerity and the rest.
The single divine moonlight of your feet, abiding in the hearts of seekers of liberation,
is capable of immediately dispelling thick darkness, O Lord of the righteous!
You alone are to be worshiped, meditated upon, and known through all the Vedas;
you are established, O Lord, as the Cause of all causes.
The white radiance that exists in each single pore of your skin,
tranquil and consisting of bliss, surpasses the light of ten million moons.
In this imperishable abode, free from qualities, named the immortal,
in this mass of radiance, you ever reside beyond the qualities as the Supreme Person.
From Time, which brings fear to the universe, and from the great terror of Māyā,
devotees are indeed liberated by the strength of worshiping you.
To you, the Lord of the universe, I have come for refuge,
to the Self of all, the all-pervading Brahman, the Great Person, the Infallible One.
In such a way that my devotion to your lotus feet remains always unwavering,
be pleased to grant your grace, O Lord of gods!
Skanda said:
Having been thus praised with devotion by the celestial seer,
the Supreme Lord spoke to the sage, delighting him with speech like nectar.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevadarśanaṃ nāma saptadaśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 17 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्रीवासुदेवदर्शनं नाम सप्तदशोऽध्यायः .. 17 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, titled 'The Vision of Lord Vāsudeva', in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
The Blessed Lord said:

2.9.s: darśanaṃ mama yajjātaṃ tava tattu mahāmune ..
2.9.d: दर्शनं मम यज्जातं तव तत्तु महामुने ..
2.9.m: This vision of me that has occurred for you, O great sage,
is due to your constant, exclusive devotion, your freedom from deceit, and by my own wish.

2.9.s: ahiṃsā brahmacaryaṃ ca tvayi nityaṃ ca taddvayam ..
2.9.d: अहिंसा ब्रह्मचर्यं च त्वयि नित्यं च तद्द्वयम् ..
2.9.m: Non-violence and celibacy are ever present in you, both of these,
along with adherence to one's own duty, tranquility, dispassion, and knowledge of the Self.
association with the virtuous, the eightfold yoga, control of the senses in every way,
living on the food of sages, austerity, and freedom from all vices,
and single-minded devotion to me preceded by knowledge of my majesty—

2.9.s: varttate tena māmatra paśyasi tvaṃ hi suvrata .. 4 ..
2.9.d: वर्त्तते तेन मामत्र पश्यसि त्वं हि सुव्रत .. 4 ..
2.9.m: exist [in you]; therefore, O you of noble vows, you see me here.
Whatever other human beings, too, are endowed with such characteristics,
they too, O brahmin, see me, such as I am, who am dear to the single-minded.
I, this very one here, O brahmin, in this imperishable abode,
united with Rādhā and Lakṣmī, dwell eternally together with those who have taken refuge in me.
Having the nature of Vāsudeva, bestower of the fruits of all actions,
I exist as the inner controller of all embodied beings, entirely independent.
In the great abode named Vaikuṇṭha, four-armed, along with Lakṣmī,
I dwell together with attendants headed by Nanda and Garuḍa.
In the divine abode full of radiance, on the earth in Śvetadvīpa, daily
I grant my darśana at the five prescribed times to the liberated souls of Śveta.
Through my forms named Aniruddha, Pradyumna, and Saṃkarṣaṇa,
I effect the creation, preservation, and dissolution of many tens of millions of cosmic eggs.
At the beginning of creation, Brahmā was created by me from the lotus of my navel;
he propitiated me with austerity and with sacrifices, O Nārada.
Then, pleased with him, I granted him the boons he desired:
‘O Brahmā, you shall obtain the capacity for creating living beings.
By my boon, they shall all abide strictly under your command.
And the eternal Vedas shall flash forth in your intellect.
And you shall have knowledge of my true nature just as it is,

2.9.s: tvayā kṛtāṃ ca maryādāṃ nātikraṃsyati kaścana .. 14 ..
2.9.d: त्वया कृतां च मर्यादां नातिक्रंस्यति कश्चन .. 14 ..
2.9.m: and no one shall transgress the boundary established by you.
To the hosts of gods and demons, and to the great-souled sages
who desire boons, O Brahmā, you alone shall be the grantor of boons.

2.9.s: asādhye yatra kārye ca mohameṣyasi tattvaham..
2.9.d: असाध्ये यत्र कार्ये च मोहमेष्यसि तत्त्वहम्..
2.9.m: And in whichever impossible task you fall into perplexity,
I myself, manifesting as soon as remembered by you, will accomplish it, O Creator.

2.9.s: sṛjyamāne tvayā viśve naṣṭāṃ pṛthvīṃ mahārṇave ..
2.9.d: सृज्यमाने त्वया विश्वे नष्टां पृथ्वीं महार्णवे ..
2.9.m: When the universe is being created by you, and the earth is lost in the great ocean,
I will assume the form of a boar and bring it to its proper place,
having slain the demon Hiraṇyākṣa, who is puffed up with power.

2.9.s: dinānte tava matsyohaṃ bhūtvā kṣoṇīṃ tarīmiva ..
2.9.d: दिनान्ते तव मत्स्योहं भूत्वा क्षोणीं तरीमिव ..
2.9.m: At the end of your day, having become a fish, I shall uphold the earth like a boat,
along with the medicinal herbs, Manu, and the others, until nightfall.
When the descendants of Kaśyapa churn the ocean for nectar, I, having the form of a tortoise,

2.9.s: manthānaṃ kūrmarūpohaṃ dhāsye pṛṣṭhe ca mandaram .. 19 ..
2.9.d: मन्थानं कूर्मरूपोहं धास्ये पृष्ठे च मन्दरम् .. 19 ..
2.9.m: shall support on my back Mount Mandara, the churning-rod that lacks a base.
Assuming the body of a man-lion, O Creator, for the sake of the gods
I will slay the son of Diti, Hiraṇyakaśipu, the destroyer of sacrifices.
The mighty Bali, a great demon, will be born as the son of Virocana;
he will dethrone Śakra from his sovereignty.
When the three worlds have been seized by him and the lord of Śacī is dejected,
I will be born as the twelfth son from Kaśyapa in Aditi.

2.9.s: tato rājyaṃ pradāsyāmi devendrāya divaḥ punaḥ ..
2.9.d: ततो राज्यं प्रदास्यामि देवेन्द्राय दिवः पुनः ..
2.9.m: Then I will give the sovereignty of heaven back to the lord of the gods;
I will establish the gods in their own places, O Creator,
and I will make Bali an inhabitant of the realm of Pātāla.
Then, having been born from Kardama in Devahūti under the name of Kapila,
endowed with detachment, I will set in motion Sāṃkhya, which had been lost in time.
Having become Datta born of Atri in Anasūyā, I will then teach logic
and spiritual knowledge to Prahlāda and Yadu, O Creator.
Having become Ṛṣabha, the son of Nābhi in Merudevī on earth,
I will promulgate the eternal dharma known as the state of the supreme swan.
In the Tretā yuga, I will be Rāma, the upholder of the lineage of Bhṛgu,
and I will eradicate the warrior class who break moral bounds and tread evil paths.

2.9.s: sandhau tu samanuprāpte tretāyā dvāparasya ca ..
2.9.d: सन्धौ तु समनुप्राप्ते त्रेताया द्वापरस्य च ..
2.9.m: When the twilight between the Tretā and Dvāpara [yugas] has arrived,
I will be born as Rāma from Daśaratha in Kauśalyā.
Lakṣmī shall be born as the daughter of Janaka named Sītā;
having broken the great bow of Īśa, I shall take her in marriage.
Then in battle I will slay the terrifying lord of rākṣasas, who harms the divine seers,
the abductor of Sītā, along with his younger brother.

2.9.s: tasya me tu caritrāṇi vālmīkyādyā maharṣayaḥ ..
2.9.d: तस्य मे तु चरित्राणि वाल्मीक्याद्या महर्षयः ..
2.9.m: The great seers headed by Vālmīki will then sing in many ways
the exploits of mine, through the hearing of which sin is destroyed.’
At the concluding junction of Dvāpara and Kali,
to destroy the demons who are a burden to the earth, and to protect dharma and the righteous,
I shall be born from Vasudeva through Devakī in the city of Mathurā. (32)
I, Kṛṣṇa, named Vāsudeva, as well as Saṃkarṣaṇa Bala,
and Pradyumna and Aniruddha will appear in the lineage of Yadu. (33)
The daughter of the cowherd Vṛṣabhānu will be Rādhā;
in Vṛndāvana I shall sport with her, O lotus-born [Brahmā]! (34)
And Lakṣmī will be the daughter of Bhīṣmaka, named Rukmiṇī;
having conquered the kings in battle, I shall marry her. (35)
Having slain the demons who harm dharma and the kings possessed by them,
firmly establishing dharma, I shall rid the earth of her burden. (36)

2.9.s: yena kenāpi bhāvena yasya kasyāpi mānasam ..
2.9.d: येन केनापि भावेन यस्य कस्यापि मानसम् ..
2.9.m: Whosoever's mind in whatever way

2.9.s: mayi saṃyokṣyate taṃtaṃ neṣye brahmagatiṃ parām .. 37 ..
2.9.d: मयि संयोक्ष्यते तंतं नेष्ये ब्रह्मगतिं पराम् .. 37 ..
2.9.m: shall be joined to me, to them all I will grant the supreme state of Brahman. (37)
Having established dharma on earth and caused the destruction of the Yadu lineage,
while all the gods look on, I shall then vanish from the earth. (38)
The heroic deeds of me, Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana and others
will sing in many ways, O brahmin, for they instantly remove sin. (39)
Becoming Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, the son of the sage Parāśara,
I shall divide the branches of the Veda like [those of] a tree. (40)
Relying on Vedic rites, those who torment the three worlds—
those demons I shall delude through guile, having become Buddha. (41)

2.9.s: mayā kṛṣṇena nihatāḥ sārjunena raṇeṣu ye ..
2.9.d: मया कृष्णेन निहताः सार्जुनेन रणेषु ये ..
2.9.m: Those who are slain in battles by me, Kṛṣṇa, accompanied by Arjuna,
when those demons promote adharma on the earth, (42)
then I, the sage Nārāyaṇa, born from the devotee Dharmadeva,

2.9.s: janiṣye kośale deśe bhūmau hi sāmago dvijaḥ..43..
2.9.d: जनिष्ये कोशले देशे भूमौ हि सामगो द्विजः..43..
2.9.m: shall be born on earth in the Kosala country as a twice-born singer of the Sāmaveda. (43)
O dear one, to the seers and Uddhava who have attained human form through a sage's curse,
I, protecting them from demons, shall then establish true dharma, O unborn one! (44)
At the end of Kali, the people on earth turned to mlecchas of great wickedness
I shall slay, having become Kalki, roaming upon a divine steed. (45)

2.9.s: yadā yadā ca vedokto dharmo nāśiṣyate'suraiḥ..
2.9.d: यदा यदा च वेदोक्तो धर्मो नाशिष्यतेऽसुरैः..
2.9.m: And whenever the dharma spoken of in the Vedas is ruined by demons,

2.9.s: prādurbhāvo bhaviṣyo me tadrakṣāyai tadā tadā .. 46 ..
2.9.d: प्रादुर्भावो भविष्यो मे तद्रक्षायै तदा तदा .. 46 ..
2.9.m: then and then my manifestation shall take place for its protection. (46)

2.9.s: tasmāccintāṃ vihāyaiva prajāḥ sṛja yathā purā ..
2.9.d: तस्माच्चिन्तां विहायैव प्रजाः सृज यथा पुरा ..
2.9.m: Therefore, having cast aside anxiety, create living beings as before.' / Having granted these boons to him, I vanished. (47)

2.9.s: yathā tasmai varā dattāstathaiva ca mayā kṛtam ..
2.9.d: यथा तस्मै वरा दत्तास्तथैव च मया कृतम् ..
2.9.m: Just as boons were given to him, in that very manner it was done by me;
I do and shall do [so], O sage, swiftly through my own powers. (48)
Of me, such as I am, O brahmin, the ruler of all embodied beings,
a vision, difficult to attain, has arisen on account of your undivided devotion. (49)
Choose a boon from me as you desire, O best of sages!

2.9.s: prasannosmi bhṛśaṃ tubhyaṃ nāphalaṃ mama darśanam..2.9.18.50..
2.9.d: प्रसन्नोस्मि भृशं तुभ्यं नाफलं मम दर्शनम्..2.9.18.50..
2.9.m: I am exceedingly pleased with you; vision of me is never fruitless. (50)
Skanda said:
Having heard these words of the Lord, Nārada, the best of sages,

2.9.s: manyamāno nijaṃ dhanyaṃ tamuvāca prabhuṃ mune..51..
2.9.d: मन्यमानो निजं धन्यं तमुवाच प्रभुं मुने..51..
2.9.m: considering himself blessed, spoke to that Lord, O sage: (51)
'From the mere vision of you, O Master, my heart's desire is fulfilled;

2.9.s: idaṃ hi durlabhaṃ manye sarveṣāmapi dehinām .. 52 ..
2.9.d: इदं हि दुर्लभं मन्ये सर्वेषामपि देहिनाम् .. 52 ..
2.9.m: for I consider this difficult to attain even for all embodied beings. (52)
Therefore, other than the direct beholding of you, of your devotees,
and of your immortal abode, there is nothing desired to be attained by me. (53)
There is nothing else more difficult to attain anywhere in the sphere of the universe,
which I, from you who are pleased, might ask here, O Acyuta! (54)
Whatever happiness there is in the other world, which may be attained through Vedic deeds alone,

2.9.s: daivaiḥ pitryaiśca labhyeta taccāpyasti hi naśvaram .. 55 ..
2.9.d: दैवैः पित्र्यैश्च लभ्येत तच्चाप्यस्ति हि नश्वरम् .. 55 ..
2.9.m: both divine and ancestral—that too is indeed perishable. (55)

2.9.s: necchāmi tadahaṃ kiñcitsukhaṃ tvattaḥ paraṃ prabho ..
2.9.d: नेच्छामि तदहं किञ्चित्सुखं त्वत्तः परं प्रभो ..
2.9.m: I do not desire any happiness beyond you, O Lord!
Yet I ask one desired boon from you, the best of boon-givers: (56)
may my intellect be ever intensely eager to sing of your virtues
or those of your devotees, increasing my love for you.' (57)
Skanda said:
Having promised 'So be it' to what was thus asked by him, Kṛṣṇa,
having given [him] the Mahatī vīṇā suitable for singing, spoke again: (58)
The Holy One said:
'Go now from here, O divine seer, to the spacious Badarī;
there, with devotion, worship me, the son of Dharma, O you of noble vows!' (59)
For you are my exclusive devotee, guileless at heart;
therefore, I consider you superior even to your father Brahmā.

2.9.s: yādṛśo'haṃ ca yadrūpo yāvāṃśca mahimā mama ..
2.9.d: यादृशोऽहं च यद्रूपो यावांश्च महिमा मम ..
2.9.m: Of what nature I am, of what form, and how great is my majesty—
my exclusive devotees, O sage, know all of that.

2.9.s: hṛdi cintyohamevāsmi satāṃ teṣāṃ ca te mama ..
2.9.d: हृदि चिन्त्योहमेवास्मि सतां तेषां च ते मम ..
2.9.m: I alone am to be contemplated in the heart of those virtuous ones, and they are mine in my heart.

2.9.s: teṣāmiṣṭaṃ na matto'nyanmama tebhyo na kiñcana .. 62 ..
2.9.d: तेषामिष्टं न मत्तोऽन्यन्मम तेभ्यो न किञ्चन .. 62 ..
2.9.m: They desire nothing other than me, and I desire nothing other than them.
Just as devoted wives bring a noble husband under their sway
by their own virtues, so do devotees bring even me under their sway.
Together with Śrī, I follow them as if under their control;

2.9.s: yatrayatra ca te santi tatratatrāhamasmi hi .. 64 ..
2.9.d: यत्रयत्र च ते सन्ति तत्रतत्राहमस्मि हि .. 64 ..
2.9.m: and wherever they are, there indeed am I.
Only through the company of the good can seekers of liberation attain me in this world;
by no other means, O celestial seer—know this to be true.

2.9.s: māmeva yarhi śaraṇaṃ mānuṣāḥ prāpnuvanti ye ..
2.9.d: मामेव यर्हि शरणं मानुषाः प्राप्नुवन्ति ये ..
2.9.m: Whenever human beings take refuge in me alone,
only then are they released from Māyā, the bondage of the soul.

2.9.s: māṃ prapannastu puruṣo yena kenāpi bhāvataḥ ..
2.9.d: मां प्रपन्नस्तु पुरुषो येन केनापि भावतः ..
2.9.m: A person who has surrendered to me through any disposition whatsoever
attains happiness as desired, and does not go to worldly transmigration like others.
Skanda said:
Addressed thus by the Blessed Lord and having attained the desired grace,
Nārada bowed down with tearful eyes and turned back.
Singing of Him alone with his lute, he saw a liberated white being [Śveta-mukta];
as before, he followed him as he walked ahead, O best of brahmins.

2.9.s: sadyaḥ śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ prāpya śvetānpraṇamya tān ..
2.9.d: सद्यः श्वेतं महाद्वीपं प्राप्य श्वेतान्प्रणम्य तान् ..
2.9.m: Quickly reaching the great Śvetadvīpa and bowing down to those white beings,
Nārada turned back, O brahmin, and swiftly went to Meru.
From Meru he then proceeded to the Gandhamādana mountain,
and swiftly descended from the sky toward the spacious Badarī.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīvāsudevāvatārādikathanaṃnāmā'ṣṭādaśo'dhyāyaḥ ..18..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्रीवासुदेवावतारादिकथनंनामाऽष्टादशोऽध्यायः ..18..
2.9.m: Thus ends the eighteenth chapter, entitled 'Narration of the Incarnations of Blessed Vāsudeva,' in the Vāsudeva-māhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Skanda said:
Then he saw the two ancient deities, the best of seers,
performing great austerity, firmly rooted in the Self, observant of great vows,
surpassing even the sun that illuminates all worlds in splendor,
bearing the mark of Śrīvatsa, venerable, wearing matted hair,
with hands bearing the lotus sign and feet marked with the discus,
broad-chested, long-armed, wearing white, fine, dense garments,
with handsome faces, broad foreheads, beautiful eyebrows, and auspicious noses,
endowed with auspicious marks, of divine forms, and of intense radiance.
Approaching them with humility and circumambulating them,
he prostrated himself with eight limbs in devotion and stood before them with folded hands.
Then those two seers, the abodes of austerities, of renown, and of splendor,
abandoned their silence at the conclusion of their morning rite
and, being composed, worshiped Nārada with affection with foot-water and water offering.
They sat on two seats of kuśa grass, and Nārada also [sat down].
When they had sat down there, that place shone forth
as an enclosure of sacrificial fires does with great flames fed by oblations of ghee.
Then Nārāyaṇa spoke words there to Nārada,
who was comfortably seated, rested, and given hospitable and respectful reception.
The venerable Nārāyaṇa said:
O brahmin, was that Blessed Lord, the eternal Supreme Self,

2.9.s: brahmadhāmni tvayā dṛṣṭa āvayo kāraṇaṃ param .. 2.9.19.10 ..
2.9.d: ब्रह्मधाम्नि त्वया दृष्ट आवयो कारणं परम् .. 2.9.19.10 ..
2.9.m: the ultimate cause of us both, seen by you in the supreme realm of Brahman?
Nārada said:
O Lord, by your grace, that Supreme Lord,
Vāsudeva, abiding in the imperishable abode, was seen by me.
And dismissed by him, I have arrived here to attend upon you both.

2.9.s: āsiṣye tatparo bhūtvā yuvābhyāṃ saha nityaśaḥ .. 12 ..
2.9.d: आसिष्ये तत्परो भूत्वा युवाभ्यां सह नित्यशः .. 12 ..
2.9.m: Dedicated to that, I shall abide with you two always.
The venerable Nārāyaṇa said:
Blessed are you, favored are you, that the Lord Himself was seen by you!
For no god or seer whatsoever has seen him, O brahmin.
Only those devotees who have attained similarity with the Imperishable through exclusive devotion
behold him, the cause of all.
That Blessed Lord of divine form is the Supreme Person, difficult to behold.
O Nārada, this statement spoken by me is indeed the truth.
No one in the world is dearer to him than a devotee.
Therefore, O best of brahmins, he revealed himself to you.
His limbs are enveloped in a mass of radiance; his wondrous form transcends the qualities [of material nature];
His nature is unbroken bliss; he is ever pure and imperishable.
Indeed, his form, complexion, and stage of life are not material at all.
Everything belonging to him is divine, as are all his accoutrements.

2.9.s: ekāntikānāṃ bhaktānāṃ sa eva paramā gatiḥ .. 18 ..
2.9.d: एकान्तिकानां भक्तानां स एव परमा गतिः .. 18 ..
2.9.m: He alone is the supreme goal of single-minded devotees.
Even by those who have attained the oneness of the Self with Brahman and who have turned away from the gunas,
devotion is paid to Vāsudeva—such indeed are his qualities.
Who could declare the majesty of this Supreme Self,
the master of inconceivable, infinite powers, O great sage?
He is the Self of the self, and the Self of the imperishable, spotless as space;
perceivable by divine vision, pure existence, the Person, the son of Vasudeva.
He possesses all auspicious qualities, yet is free from the gunas, the Lord of lords,
to be known through supreme knowledge, to be worshipped, the master who knows Brahman.
That Lord of divine form—whoever pleases him

2.9.s: yaḥ prīṇayati dharmeṇa sa dhanyatama ucyate .. 23 ..
2.9.d: यः प्रीणयति धर्मेण स धन्यतम उच्यते .. 23 ..
2.9.m: through single-minded austerity and righteousness is said to be the most blessed.
Therefore, O divine seer, worshipping him with single-minded righteousness,
perform austerity right here, my dear, for some time.
Purified in self through austerity alone, the majesty of that Lord of the virtuous,
as it is being declared in full by me, you shall properly comprehend.
Know austerity to be the means of accomplishing all goals, O sage; it is his heart.
By one who has not performed abundant austerity, that Lord is not brought under control.
Skanda said:
Thus addressed by the blessed Nara-Nārāyaṇa,
he was delighted, and desiring to perform austerity, the wise one said:

2.9.s: iti śrīskande mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsu'devamāhātmye nāradanaranārāyaṇasamāgamo nāmaikonaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..19..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कन्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुऽदेवमाहात्म्ये नारदनरनारायणसमागमो नामैकोनविंशोऽध्यायः ..19..
2.9.m: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, named 'The Meeting of Nārada and Nara-Nārāyaṇa,' in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second [section], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses].
Nārada said:
O Blessed One, declare to me the single-minded righteousness that is approved by you,

2.9.s: prīyate yena viśvātmā vāsudevaḥ sa sarvadā .. 1 ..
2.9.d: प्रीयते येन विश्वात्मा वासुदेवः स सर्वदा .. 1 ..
2.9.m: by which that Vāsudeva, the Self of all, is ever pleased.
The glorious Nārāyaṇa said:

2.9.s: sādhu pṛṣṭaṃ tvayā brahmanmatiste vimalā kila ..
2.9.d: साधु पृष्टं त्वया ब्रह्मन्मतिस्ते विमला किल ..
2.9.m: Well asked by you, O brahmin; your intellect is indeed spotless.

2.9.s: mayi snigdhāya bhaktāya tubhyaṃ guhyamapi bruve .. .. 2 ..
2.9.d: मयि स्निग्धाय भक्ताय तुभ्यं गुह्यमपि ब्रुवे .. .. 2 ..
2.9.m: To you, an affectionate devotee devoted to me, I shall speak even the secret.

2.9.s: dharma eṣa mayā proktaḥ kalpasyādau vivasvate ..
2.9.d: धर्म एष मया प्रोक्तः कल्पस्यादौ विवस्वते ..
2.9.m: This dharma was spoken by me to Vivasvat at the beginning of the kalpa.
That very eternal [dharma] I declare to you, O sage.
Devotion to the Lord—like that of Lakṣmī—along with one's own duty, knowledge, and dispassion,

2.9.s: tasminnananyā bhaktiryā dharma ekāntikaḥ sa vai .. 4 ..
2.9.d: तस्मिन्ननन्या भक्तिर्या धर्म एकान्तिकः स वै .. 4 ..
2.9.m: which is directed toward him without anyone else, is indeed single-minded righteousness.
By that alone the Lord of Goloka himself becomes exceedingly pleased,
and that devotee too finds all his desires completely fulfilled.
Nārada said:
I desire to understand the characteristics of one's own duty and the rest, individually,
from you, the source of the scriptures. You ought to declare them.
Of all the scriptures of the Vedas and Āgamas, O Lord of the virtuous,

2.9.s: mūlaṃ tvameka evāsi yeṣu dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 7 ..
2.9.d: मूलं त्वमेक एवासि येषु धर्मः सनातनः .. 7 ..
2.9.m: you alone are the sole root, in which eternal righteousness is established.
You yourself are the Blessed Lord Vāsudeva visibly present, beyond the imperishable;
for the welfare of all beings you abide here, an ocean of compassion.
Others besides you, such as Brahmā and the rest, are subordinate to the qualities of their own natures;
they cannot know righteousness and the rest as they truly are. Therefore, do you speak.
Skanda said:
Thus questioned by the divine seer, the blessed son of Dharma,
the omniscient one, began to declare one's own duty and the rest in proper order.
The glorious Nārāyaṇa said:
The proper conduct of the classes and stages of life, taken separately,
both general and specific, is termed one's own duty.
First hear the common righteousness of all human beings:
Non-harm is the highest righteousness; it is declared to be the foremost among them.
Even with respect to one's principal duties and livelihood, the absence of malice, even in thought,
toward any living being whatsoever when another course of action exists—that is regarded as [non-harm].

2.9.s: satyā vāgbhūtamātrasya droho na syādyayā tathā ..
2.9.d: सत्या वाग्भूतमात्रस्य द्रोहो न स्याद्यया तथा ..
2.9.m: Truthful speech is that by which no harm comes to any being.
And austerity is defined as the restraint of enjoyments ordained by scripture.
And the practice of purity is twofold, external and internal;

2.9.s: anādānaṃ parasvasya parokṣaṃ vā chalena ca .. 15 ..
2.9.d: अनादानं परस्वस्य परोक्षं वा छलेन च .. 15 ..
2.9.m: refraining from taking others' wealth secretly or through deceit;
celibacy according to propriety, victory over lust, greed, and anger;
joyfully offering wealth to a worthy recipient, contentment with what is obtained by providence;

2.9.s: tīrthe kṣetre ca yajñādau caturvargāptayepi vā ..
2.9.d: तीर्थे क्षेत्रे च यज्ञादौ चतुर्वर्गाप्तयेपि वा ..
2.9.m: even at a sacred ford, sacred field, sacrifice, or to attain the four aims of life,
completely avoiding the killing of oneself or another;
and completely avoiding actions that cause loss of caste;
and restraint of the hands, feet, stomach, genitals, and speech;
and giving up all addictions, liquor, and meat;
abstention from adultery, and observing the good duties of one's family;
fasting on all Ekādaśīs along with the restraints,
and duly observing religious vows on the birthdays of Hari;
uprightness, service to the virtuous, eating food and the like after sharing it,
and devotion to the Lord—these are the universal duties for men.
Brahmin, kṣatriya, vaiśya, and śūdra are declared to be the four castes;
I will explain to you, O sage, their distinct, specific duties.
Tranquillity, self-control, forbearance, purity, faith, devotion to the Lord,

2.9.s: tapo jñānaṃ ca vijñānaṃ vipradharmaḥ svabhāvajaḥ .. 23 ..
2.9.d: तपो ज्ञानं च विज्ञानं विप्रधर्मः स्वभावजः .. 23 ..
2.9.m: austerity, sacred knowledge, and experiential knowledge are the innate duty of a brahmin.
Heroism, courage, generosity, strength, brilliance, affording refuge,
protection of cows, brahmins, and the virtuous, and sacrifice are proclaimed the duties of the warrior caste.
These are indeed the duties of a king, as well as protecting the subjects according to statecraft,
establishing righteousness on earth, and punishing those deserving punishment.
Faith, dedication to giving, service to the virtuous and brahmins,
discontent with the accumulation of wealth, and enterprise are the duties of a vaiśya.

2.9.s: dvijātīnāṃ ca devānāṃ sevā niṣkapaṭaṃ gavām ..
2.9.d: द्विजातीनां च देवानां सेवा निष्कपटं गवाम् ..
2.9.m: Undissimulated service to the twice-born, the gods, and cattle
is declared the specific duty of a śūdra, O best of sages.
Teaching, performing sacrifices for others, and accepting gifts from the pure

2.9.s: viprasya jīvikā proktā tatrāntyā tvāpadi smṛtā .. 28 ..
2.9.d: विप्रस्य जीविका प्रोक्ता तत्रान्त्या त्वापदि स्मृता .. 28 ..
2.9.m: are stated to be the livelihood of a brahmin; among these, the last is considered permissible only in adversity.
The best among the twice-born who perceives fault in performing sacrifices or teaching for others,
for him another fourfold mode of subsistence is also prescribed:

2.9.s: śiloñcha nityayācñā ca śālīnaṃ cocitā kṛṣiḥ ..
2.9.d: शिलोञ्छ नित्ययाच्ञा च शालीनं चोचिता कृषिः ..
2.9.m: Gleaning ears of corn, daily begging, living modestly on what comes unsought, and appropriate agriculture;
among these, each preceding one is to be understood as superior by the best of the twice-born.
A brahmin may live by the livelihood of a vaiśya in times of distress, O Nārada,

2.9.s: atha vā kṣatravṛttyāpi śvavṛttyā na tu karhicit .. 31 ..
2.9.d: अथ वा क्षत्रवृत्त्यापि श्ववृत्त्या न तु कर्हिचित् .. 31 ..
2.9.m: or even by the livelihood of a kṣatriya, but never by dog-like service.
The warrior should live by the weapon, protecting righteousness on all sides;
in distress, he may conduct himself by the livelihood of a vaiśya, or disguised as a brahmin.
The livelihood of a king is stated to be through collecting taxes and the like from non-brahmins,
pleasing all his subjects in accordance with place and time.
Even in times of distress, for a warrior as for a brahmin in every way,
servitude to base persons, which destroys one's own luster, is condemned.
Agriculture, trade, cattle-rearing, and fourthly, living on interest—
these are declared the livelihood of a vaiśya, and the livelihood of a śūdra in distress.
A śūdra should live on the wealth obtained through service to the twice-born;
in times of distress, however, he may take up the livelihood of an artisan and the like.
When freed from distress, everyone, having performed an appropriate expiation,
should again subsist by his own primary livelihood.

2.9.s: cāturvarṇyaṃ satāṃ saṃgaṃ kuryānna tvasatāṃ kvacit ..
2.9.d: चातुर्वर्ण्यं सतां संगं कुर्यान्न त्वसतां क्वचित् ..
2.9.m: The four castes should associate with the good, but never with the wicked;
association with the good bestows liberation, while bad company leads to hell.

2.9.s: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ rasāsvādaṃ jitvā mānaṃ ca matsaram ..
2.9.d: कामं क्रोधं रसास्वादं जित्वा मानं च मत्सरम् ..
2.9.m: Those who have conquered lust, anger, the relish of tastes, pride, and envy,

2.9.s: nirdambhaṃ viṣṇubhaktā ye te santaḥ sādhavo matāḥ .. 39 ..
2.9.d: निर्दम्भं विष्णुभक्ता ये ते सन्तः साधवो मताः .. 39 ..
2.9.m: and are free from deceit, devoted to Viṣṇu—they are considered the good, the virtuous.
Those attached to women, effeminate, attached to the relish of tastes, greedy for wealth,
harmful, puffed up with ostentation, and merely semblance of devotees—they indeed are the unvirtuous.
Demonic endowment resides naturally in the unvirtuous, while divine endowment resides in the virtuous;
resolving thus, those desiring happiness should attend upon the good.

2.9.s: yādṛśāṃ yasya saṃgaḥ syācchāstrāṇāṃ vā nṛṇāmapi ..
2.9.d: यादृशां यस्य संगः स्याच्छास्त्राणां वा नृणामपि ..
2.9.m: Whatever kind of company a person keeps, whether of scriptures or of people,

2.9.s: buddhiḥ syāttādṛśī tasya kāryo'to nāsatāṃ hi saḥ .. 42 ..
2.9.d: बुद्धिः स्यात्तादृशी तस्य कार्योऽतो नासतां हि सः .. 42 ..
2.9.m: such becomes his intellect; therefore, one should never associate with the wicked.
Those men who take delight in serving the virtuous according to their own capacity,
there is indeed no exalted sovereign power unattainable for them.

2.9.s: svadharmasthā api satāṃ drohiṇo ye tu mānavāḥ ..
2.9.d: स्वधर्मस्था अपि सतां द्रोहिणो ये तु मानवाः ..
2.9.m: Even if abiding in their own duty, those men who bear malice toward the virtuous,

2.9.s: sadgatiṃ naiva te yānti kvāpi kenāpi karmaṇā .. 44 ..
2.9.d: सद्गतिं नैव ते यान्ति क्वापि केनापि कर्मणा .. 44 ..
2.9.m: never attain a good state anywhere through any action.
Even if they are devotees of Viṣṇu dedicated to great worship, if toward the virtuous

2.9.s: drohaṃ kuryustadā teṣu na prasīdati sa kvacit .. 45 ..
2.9.d: द्रोहं कुर्युस्तदा तेषु न प्रसीदति स क्वचित् .. 45 ..
2.9.m: they should commit malice, he is never pleased with them. (45)

2.9.s: saddrohiṇastu dehānte yāṃyāṃ yoniṃ brajanti ca ..
2.9.d: सद्द्रोहिणस्तु देहान्ते यांयां योनिं ब्रजन्ति च ..
2.9.m: Those who bear malice toward the virtuous, into whatever womb they enter at the end of the body,
in each and every one they are afflicted with hunger and diseases until the end of their lives. (46)
Only from transgressing against the virtuous does the immediate destruction
of all even great merits, of lifespan, and of riches occur. (47)
Therefore, service to the virtuous must be performed by all who desire happiness;
holy sacred fords should be resorted to, and brahmins and cows should be revered. (48)
Those of evil intellect who revile sacred fords and images of deities,
the extinction of the lineage of those who are born of adultery will surely come about. (49)
When a single brahmin is satisfied with good food, priestly gifts, and the like,
the whole world is satisfied, and Hari himself is pleased. (50)
When malice is done to a single brahmin, malice is done to the whole world.
Therefore, according to one's ability, brahmins, who are forms of Viṣṇu, are to be worshipped. (51)
All the hosts of gods reside in the limbs of cows;

2.9.s: tathā sarvāṇi tīrthāni tāsu tiṣṭhanti sarvadā .. 52 ..
2.9.d: तथा सर्वाणि तीर्थानि तासु तिष्ठन्ति सर्वदा .. 52 ..
2.9.m: likewise, all sacred fords reside in them constantly. (52)
When a single cow is worshipped, all the gods are thoroughly worshipped,

2.9.s: kṛtāni syuśca sarvāṇi tīrthānyapi ca nārada .. 53 ..
2.9.d: कृतानि स्युश्च सर्वाणि तीर्थान्यपि च नारद .. 53 ..
2.9.m: and all sacred fords also are visited, O Nārada. (53)

2.9.s: ekasyā api gordrohe kṛte kvāpi pramādataḥ ..
2.9.d: एकस्या अपि गोर्द्रोहे कृते क्वापि प्रमादतः ..
2.9.m: If harm is done even to a single cow anywhere through negligence,
all the deities are wronged, and so are all sacred fords in their entirety. (54)
Therefore, established in the rules as spoken, the people of the four classes
must act with effort, and they must turn away from prohibitions. (55)

2.9.s: cāturvarṇyetare ye tu teṣāṃ vṛttiḥ kulocitā ..
2.9.d: चातुर्वर्ण्येतरे ये तु तेषां वृत्तिः कुलोचिता ..
2.9.m: As for those other than the four classes, their livelihood suited to their lineage,
devoid of unrighteousness such as theft and violence, is alone conducive to welfare. (56)

2.9.s: varṇadharmā iti proktāḥ saṃkṣepeṇa mayā mune ..
2.9.d: वर्णधर्मा इति प्रोक्ताः संक्षेपेण मया मुने ..
2.9.m: Thus the duties of the classes have been stated briefly by me, O sage.
Now I declare to you the duties of the four life-stages. (57)

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye cāturvarṇyadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..20..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये चातुर्वर्ण्यधर्मनिरूपणं नाम विंशोऽध्यायः ..20..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Duties of the Four Classes', in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second, Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. (20)
Glorious Nārāyaṇa said:
The student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the renunciant—
these four are declared to be the persons of the life-stages, O best of sages. (1)
He who is purified by the life-cycle rites, of pure womb, and has attained twice-born status,

2.9.s: prāptaḥ sa hi brahmacārī taddharmānādito bruve .. 2 ..
2.9.d: प्राप्तः स हि ब्रह्मचारी तद्धर्मानादितो ब्रुवे .. 2 ..
2.9.m: he indeed is a student; I will explain his duties from the beginning. (2)
Living pure in the teacher's house, the student should study the Veda,
with senses subdued, anger conquered, humble, and speaking the truth. (3)
Evening and morning, self-restrained, he should perform the fire oblation and go begging for alms;
he should perform the twilight devotion at the three junctures of the day, and likewise worship of Viṣṇu every day. (4)
Only by the teacher's command should he eat a measured amount of food, undisturbed;
he should be constantly devoted to the service of the teacher and free from vices. (5)

2.9.s: snāne ca bhojane home jape maunamupāśrayet ..
2.9.d: स्नाने च भोजने होमे जपे मौनमुपाश्रयेत् ..
2.9.m: During bathing, eating, fire oblation, and silent recitation, he should maintain silence;
he should not cut his nails or hair, nor scrub his teeth excessively. (6)
He should not excessively wash his clothes, and he should be guileless toward the teacher;
summoned, he should study, and at the beginning and the end he should bow to him. (7)
He should not touch untouchables, nor speak to those with whom conversation is forbidden;
he should never eat uneatable food, nor drink undrinkable liquid. (8)
He should wear a girdle, a hide, a staff, and carry a water-pot,

2.9.s: site dve vāsasī brahmasūtraṃ ca japamālikām .. 9 ..
2.9.d: सिते द्वे वाससी ब्रह्मसूत्रं च जपमालिकाम् .. 9 ..
2.9.m: two white garments, a sacred thread, and a rosary. (9)
With kuśa grass in hand, having matted locks, free of hair ornamentation,
he should avoid body-ointments, flower garlands, and ornaments. (10)

2.9.s: tailābhyaṅgaṃ na kurvīta kajjale nāñjanaṃ tathā ..
2.9.d: तैलाभ्यङ्गं न कुर्वीत कज्जले नाञ्जनं तथा ..
2.9.m: He should not rub himself with oil, nor apply collyrium with lamp-black;
and with effort he should avoid contact with intoxicating liquor and meat. (11)

2.9.s: strīṇāṃ nirīkṣaṇaṃ sparśaṃ bhāṣaṇaṃ krīḍanādi ca ..
2.9.d: स्त्रीणां निरीक्षणं स्पर्शं भाषणं क्रीडनादि च ..
2.9.m: Gazing at, touching, speaking with, or playing with women,
and even a drawing of a woman, the student must avoid in every way. (12)
Except for an image of a deity, a woman made of wood, painted, and the like,
the wise [student] should not touch at all, nor deliberately look upon. (13)
And he should never gaze upon any living creature in copulation;
he should not listen to the virtues or defects of women, nor speak of them. (14)
Without touching, he should salute even his own teacher's wife;

2.9.s: jananyāpi na tiṣṭheta rahaḥsthāne tu karhicit .. 15 ..
2.9.d: जनन्यापि न तिष्ठेत रहःस्थाने तु कर्हिचित् .. 15 ..
2.9.m: and he should never stay in a secluded place even with his mother. (15)
Behaving in this manner, he should dwell there until the completion of his studies.

2.9.s: tato virakto nyāsī syādvarṇī vā naiṣṭhiko bhavet ..
2.9.d: ततो विरक्तो न्यासी स्याद्वर्णी वा नैष्ठिको भवेत् ..
2.9.m: Then, detached, he may become a renunciant, or he may become a lifelong student. (16)
In the Kali [age], ineligibility is stated for those observing lifelong celibacy (naiṣṭhika).
It should be understood that this does not apply to the twilight [of the yuga], from the concise usage of the word 'Kali'.
O brahmin, he may become a forest dweller, or if not dispassionate, he should become a householder.

2.9.s: prājāpatyaṃ ca sāvitraṃ brāhmaṃ naiṣṭhikameva ca ..
2.9.d: प्राजापत्यं च सावित्रं ब्राह्मं नैष्ठिकमेव च ..
2.9.m: Prājāpatya, Sāvitra, Brāhma, and Naiṣṭhika—
such is the fourfold brahmacarya; of these, one should adhere to one according to one's capacity.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye brahmacāridharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 21 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये ब्रह्मचारिधर्मनिरूपणं नामैकविंशोऽध्यायः .. 21 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Duties of a Brahmacārin', in the Vāsudeva-māhātmya of the second [section], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. // 21
Glorious Nārāyaṇa said:
Wishing to become a householder, he should give a fee (dakṣiṇā) to the teacher according to his means,
and only by his permission perform the rite of return from studentship (samāvartana).
Then, according to rule, he should marry a woman suitable to his family, younger in age, free from disease,
devoid of masculine characteristics, and free from sin.
According to his qualification, every day for the pleasure of Kṛṣṇa,
he should then worship the gods, seers, ancestors, and living beings according to rule.

2.9.m: Bathing, the twilight devotions, recitation (japa), burnt offering (homa), self-study of the Veda (svādhyāya), the worship of Viṣṇu,
water libation (tarpaṇa), the offering to all gods (vaiśvadeva), and hospitality to guests he should perform daily.
He should perform virtuous deeds according to his ability with wealth acquired by righteous means.
Unattached, he should support those dependent upon him for maintenance, but never torment [them].
Because of the body or bodily relations, he should not, like a beast,
bear enmity toward others; he should abandon the notion of 'I' and 'mine' with regard to the body and so forth.
Unwearied, he should keep company with the good, the devotees of the Lord (Bhāgavatas);

2.9.s: na straiṇānāṃ vyasanināṃ saṃgaṃ kuryānna lobhinām ..7..

2.9.m: he should not keep company with womanisers, the dissolute, or the greedy.
He should never look upon another man's wife with lustful intent;
nor should he approach his own wife on days of ancestral rites (śrāddha), sacred junctions (parvan), vows, and the like.

2.9.s: prāptopi puruṣaḥ sāṃkhye yoge ca paripakvatām..

2.9.m: Therefore, a wise man should not sit together with his mother, sister, or daughter
in a solitary place, [if she is] a young woman—how much less with any other woman?
Of all inauspicious things, a widow is indeed the most inauspicious;
therefore, looking upon her and touching her robs men of their merit.
If, at the time of departure on a journey, the sight of a widow occurs right in front,
then one must not go; otherwise, death is certain.
The blessings of widowed women are equal to the hissing of the serpent of death;
hence, a householder should fear them as he would demonesses (rākṣasīs).
He should shun liquor, meat, intoxicants, and gambling from afar;
he should never cause injury to any living being, even by speech.
He should daily listen to the deeds of the incarnations of Hari;
faithful, he should perform all actions for the sake of Vāsudeva.

2.9.s: ūrje māghe ca vaiśākhe cāturmāsye malimluce ..

2.9.m: In the months of Ūrja (Kārttika), Māgha, and Vaiśākha, during the Cāturmāsya, and in an intercalary month (malimluca),
as well as on other meritorious occasions, he should observe special observances.
In a sacred place, at an auspicious time, to a worthy recipient according to rule, a householder
should give gifts according to his capacity, and show compassion toward living creatures.
O sinless one, I shall describe to you specifically the sacred places, auspicious times,
and worthy recipients that increase righteousness (dharma).
The best of all regions on earth is that which is inhabited by Me,
where hosts of great sages of noble vows perform austerities.
The sanctity of places arises from the greatness of Hari and His devotees:
Gaṅgādvāra, Madhupurī (Mathurā), and Naimiṣāraṇya;
Kurukṣetra, Ayodhyā, Prayāga, and Gayāśiras;
the city of Vārāṇasī, and the sacred Pulahāśrama;
Kapilāśrama, Śrīraṅga, Prabhāsa, and Kuśasthalī (Dvārakā);

2.9.m: the sacred field named Siddhaprada, and the great lake Pauṣkara (Puṣkara);
Mount Raivata, the sporting ground of the Blessed Lord with Śrī;
likewise Mount Govardhana, and the sacred forest Vṛndāvana;
the seven principal mountain ranges, beginning with Mahendra and Malaya;
the most holy Bhāgīrathī (Gaṅgā), the Yamunā, and the Sarasvatī;
the holy major rivers and streams celebrated in the Purāṇas,

wherever the worship of the image of the Blessed Lord takes place with great festivals;
and wherever there are unswerving devotees of the Lord;
and wherever there are excellent brahmins who are non-violent and devoted to their own duty—
and where animals such as deer roam fearlessly. (27)
Wherever are the descents of Hari, or wherever is his abode,

Now listen, O Nārada: I shall tell the times that increase merit. (29)

2.9.m: The two solstices, the equinox, an eclipse of the sun and moon,

2.9.d: पुण्याः स्युस्तिथयः सर्वा अमावास्या च वैधृतिः .. 31 ..

the asterisms of one’s own birth, and the festival days of Hari’s appearance, (32)
the life-cycle rites and celebrations of oneself, of [one’s] wife, and of [one’s] children,
and whenever a worthy recipient is found: these are the most meritorious times. (33)
The worship of the gods, ancestors, twice-born, and virtuous according to one’s capacity,
and ritual ablution, gifts, recitation, and so forth, indeed yield endless fruit. (34)
The worthy recipient in person, however, is the Blessed Lord Himself, O Nārada,
just as water given to the root satisfies all the branches. (35)
By non-violence, Vedic knowledge, contentment, right conduct, and devotion,

2.9.d: हृदि विष्णुं दधीरन्ये ते सत्पात्राणि वै द्विजाः .. 36 ..
2.9.m: those twice-born who hold Viṣṇu in their hearts are indeed worthy recipients. (36)
The single-minded devotees of the Blessed Lord, who release the bound—
know that those in whom the Blessed Lord Himself resides are worthy recipients. (37)
A wealthy man should cause firm temples of Viṣṇu to be built,
and should also provide endowments for them to secure an ongoing stream of worship. (38)
He should prepare water reservoirs and gardens for the sake of Viṣṇu,
and he should satisfy virtuous people and brahmins with wholesome, delicious food. (39)
He should perform non-violent Vaiṣṇava sacrifices according to his capacity and the rules,
and observe the observances and appearance-festivals of Viṣṇu with abundant provisions. (40)
In the dark fortnight of the month of Prauṣṭhapada, on the day of death, and on auspicious festival days at sacred fords,

2.9.m: he should diligently perform the śrāddha of his parents and of his relatives according to his capacity. (41)

2.9.m: In rituals for the gods and for the ancestors,

2.9.m: He should feed two brahmins in a rite for the gods and three in a rite for the ancestors according to the rule,

2.9.m: A person should never offer meat in a śrāddha, nor should he eat it;
the ancestors are greatly pleased by ascetic food, milk, and clarified butter. (45)
By that non-violence toward every living being through mind, speech, and body,
all the ancestors, being exceedingly compassionate, are satisfied. (46)
Therefore, never through bad company nor through failing to understand the core meaning of scripture,
should a man devoted to Vāsudeva give meat in a śrāddha. (47)
He should perform the observances of Viṣṇu along with the restraints such as celibacy;
intent solely on that, he should not perform any other business on that day. (48)
He should observe the impurity of his own relatives upon birth and death according to the scripture,
and likewise at an eclipse of the sun and the moon. (49)
In a dispute over worldly matters and in deciding them,

2.9.m: those who have abandoned the householder's stage must not be employed, nor vile persons. (50)
Where these are present, that business would never succeed anywhere, O best of the twice-born;

These duties of householders have been declared briefly by me,
by whose practice there will be inexhaustible, desired happiness for men. (52)
Twice-born householders are celebrated as being of four kinds,
according to the distinction of means of livelihood such as gleaning, each with its name, O Nārada. (53)
Next, I shall declare the duties of women, O best of the virtuous,

2.9.m: Even with her father or son, a young woman

2.9.m: A woman, whether married or a widow, should never conceal the appearance of her menses;

Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Now, O sage, I will declare to you the rules for the forest hermit.
The third stage of life is prescribed in the third portion of life's span. // 1
If his wife is compliant in his personal service, dispassionate, and fond of austerity,

2.9.s: yadi patnī bhavettarhi tayā saha vanaṃ viśet .. 2 ..
2.9.d: यदि पत्नी भवेत्तर्हि तया सह वनं विशेत् .. 2 ..
2.9.m: then he should enter the forest together with her. // 2
Otherwise, assigning her maintenance and protection to his sons and others,
he should enter the forest alone, detached [from the world]. // 3
He should dwell there fearless, taking delight in austerity, free from sloth;
he should make a thatched hut for the sacrificial fire, but dwell outside himself. // 4
He should practice the austerity of five fires in summer, dwell in water in the cold season,
and endure downpours in the rainy season, with anger conquered and senses restrained. // 5
He should wear garments made of grass, leaves, deer-skin, or bark.
He should consume wild grains, or wild roots, fruits, and the like. // 6
He may eat [food] cooked by fire, ripened by the sun, or even raw;
moreover, in the absence of teeth, he [may eat food] pounded with a stone or mortar. // 7
He should personally gather food according to the proper time day by day,
or accept at that time [what is] brought by another, but never at any other time. // 8
Even at the proper time, except in an emergency, he should not accept cultivated food;
and with wild grains alone he should perform his fire rituals as before. // 9
He should keep a water-pot, staff, and the equipment for the daily fire offering;
he should wear his head hair, body hair, beard, and nails, and [keep] his teeth uncleaned. // 2.9.23.10
He should bathe without massaging his limbs, and sleep on the bare ground.
He should practice austerity according to the place, time, strength, and condition. // 11
The Phenapas, the Audumbaras, and likewise the Vālakhilyas,
and the Vaikhānasa—thus forest-dwellers are declared to be of four kinds. // 12
According to his ability, for twelve years, or eight, or four in the forest,
he should dwell, or for two, or even just one; then he should take refuge in renunciation. // 13
If intense dispassion arises, then renunciation brings benefit;
otherwise, the twice-born should live in that very forest for the rest of his life. // 14
Having made renunciation according to rule, established in the fourth stage of life,

2.9.s: sācchādanaṃ tu kaupīnaṃ kanthāmekāṃ ca dhārayet.. .. 15 ..
2.9.d: साच्छादनं तु कौपीनं कन्थामेकां च धारयेत्.. .. 15 ..
2.9.m: he should wear a loincloth with a covering, and a single patched garment. // 15
He should carry a staff, a water-pot, and a water-strainer;
at the proper time he should beg alms in the house of a twice-born of good conduct. // 16
An ascetic should not beg alms every day at the house of the same person;
he must not become greedy for flavors, and should eat moderately, once [a day]. // 17
A mendicant should mostly accept alms from one in the forest-dweller stage of life;
for by that extremely pure food, his mind is certainly purified. // 18
Even upon smelling meat or liquor, he should perform the Pārāka penance;
he should be thoroughly pure in cleanliness and conduct, and must not touch Śūdras and others. // 19
He should constantly worship Viṣṇu and eat what has been offered to Viṣṇu;
he should recite the twelve-syllable or the eight-syllable mantra of Viṣṇu. // 2.9.23.20
He should not engage in fallacious debate, nor narrate stories for the sake of a livelihood;
he should not be attached to bad scriptures, nor pursue a worldly profession. // 21
He should study good scriptures that examine bondage and liberation;
he must not build monasteries and the like; he should abandon egoism and possessiveness. // 22
Except during the four months of the rainy season, he should not dwell in one place when there is no calamity;
and through knowledge he should truly understand the nature of the self and of Hari. // 23
Desire, anger, fear, enmity, and the hoarding of money, grain, and the like—
he must never cultivate; the ascetic should observe the restraints and the observances. // 24
Even an ascetic endowed with intense knowledge and dispassion
will surely fall through contact with women, wealth, ornaments, and fine clothes. // 25
A renunciant should avoid fragrant substances such as flowers, sandalwood, and oils;

2.9.s: tyāgī kurvītānyathā tu bhaveddehātmadhīḥ sa vai .. 26 ..
2.9.d: त्यागी कुर्वीतान्यथा तु भवेद्देहात्मधीः स वै .. 26 ..
2.9.m: otherwise, he will indeed come to identify the self with the body. // 26
According to the amount of food one eats, lust for women enters him to that same degree;

2.9.s: ato mitaṃ nīrasaṃ ca bhojanaṃ tyāgino hitam .. 27 ..
2.9.d: अतो मितं नीरसं च भोजनं त्यागिनो हितम् .. 27 ..
2.9.m: therefore, moderate and flavorless food is beneficial for a renunciant. // 27

all of them indeed, at the end of the body, reach the world of Viṣṇu.

2.9.m: That by which the field and so forth are known is indeed declared to be knowledge.
Vāsudeva, the supreme Brahman in the vast imperishable abode,
was in the beginning one without a second, devoid of qualities, having a divine form.
Root-matter, the cause of effects, accompanied by time, in the light of the imperishable,
was then hidden, like the night in the radiance of the sun.
Then, when he had the desire to create the cosmic eggs,
she, the Great Māyā, first became manifest along with time.
Taking up that power of time, through his imperishable nature,

2.9.s: sisṛkṣayaikṣata yadā sā cukṣobha tadaiva hi .. 5 ..
2.9.d: सिसृक्षयैक्षत यदा सा चुक्षोभ तदैव हि .. 5 ..
2.9.m: when Vāsudeva glanced with the desire to create, she was agitated at that very moment.
From her, O sage, tens of millions of pradhānas and puruṣas were born;
and by the will of the Lord, those puruṣas were joined with the pradhānas.
The puruṣas deposited seeds in them, and from them were born
countless cosmic eggs; among them, however, one is now analyzed.
First the mahat arose from that golden virility of the puruṣa;
from it, the egoity; from that, the three qualities, sattva and the rest.
From tamas arose the five subtle elements and the gross elements;
the ten senses from rajas, along with the intellect and the vital breath.
From sattva arose the presiding deities of the senses, and likewise the mind.
Generally, these deities are proclaimed as principles.
Impelled by Vāsudeva, with their respective portions, they brought forth
the divine body named the cosmic form, the shelter of the moving and unmoving.
And since that Virāj person lay in the waters he himself created,
he is called 'Nārāyaṇa' by the Vedic scriptures and the like.
From his navel-lotus arose Brahmā endowed with rajas; from his heart-lotus
was born Viṣṇu, endowed with sattva; and from his forehead, Hara, endowed with tamas.
From these very places also arose the three powers:
there arose Durgā of the nature of tamas, and Sāvitrī of the nature of rajas,
and Śrī of the nature of sattva—all adorned with garments and ornaments.
By command of the Virāj, they went to the three, Brahmā and the others:

2.9.s: durgā rudraṃ ca sāvitrī brahmāṇaṃ viṣṇumantimā .. 15 ..
2.9.d: दुर्गा रुद्रं च सावित्री ब्रह्माणं विष्णुमन्तिमा .. 15 ..
2.9.m: Durgā to Rudra, Sāvitrī to Brahmā, and the last one to Viṣṇu.
From Durgā's portion arose thousands of goddesses, Caṇḍikā and others;
from Sāvitrī's portion were born powers headed by the triple Veda;
and from Śrī's portion alone arose those headed by Dussahā, O sage.
There, the Brahmā who had arisen first from the navel-lotus of the Virāj,
seated on that lotus in the single ocean, saw no one at all.
Not having attained understanding of creation, nor knowing himself,
contemplating, 'Who am I? Whence came I?', he wished to see the support of the lotus.
Entering the stalk and descending, searching for its base,

2.9.s: saṃvatsaraśataṃ yātaṃ tasya nāntaṃ tu solabhat .. 19 ..
2.9.d: संवत्सरशतं यातं तस्य नान्तं तु सोलभत् .. 19 ..
2.9.m: a hundred years passed for him, but he found no end to it.
Coming upward again, weary, he sat down.
The Lord, having an invisible form, said to him: 'Perform austerity! Perform austerity!'
Having heard that, and not seeing its speaker anywhere,
he performed austerity like one instructed by a guru for a divine thousand years.

2.9.s: padme tapasyate tasmai tapaḥ śuddhātmane tataḥ ..
2.9.d: पद्मे तपस्यते तस्मै तपः शुद्धात्मने ततः ..
2.9.m: Then, to him whose self was purified by austerity, performing austerity on the lotus,
Acyuta revealed in deep concentration the abode of Vaikuṇṭha,
where the three qualities belonging to pradhāna, rajas and the rest,
do not exist in the slightest, and where there is no fear of time or māyā.
In that radiance resplendent like ten thousand suns risen together,
he saw Vāsudeva, charming, of divine dark form,
the four-armed, all-pervading Lord holding a mace, lotus, conch, and discus,
clad in yellow garments, adorned with crowns and ornaments of precious gems,
attended by four-armed attendants, Nanda, Garuḍa, and others,
and by the eight perfections and the six divine opulences with hands folded in reverence,
that Lord seated upon a throne together with Śrī.
Bowing low with folded hands, Viriñca stood before him, delighted in heart.
The Blessed Lord said to him: 'O Brahmā, I am pleased with your austerity.

2.9.s: varaṃ varaya mattastvaṃ svābhīṣṭaṃ yatpriyosi me .. 28 ..
2.9.d: वरं वरय मत्तस्त्वं स्वाभीष्टं यत्प्रियोसि मे .. 28 ..
2.9.m: Choose a boon of your desire from me, since you are dear to me.'
Addressed thus by him, Brahmā, knowing that Lord to be the impeller of his austerity,

2.9.s: svaṃ ca viśvasṛjaṃ brahmā yayāce'bhimataṃ varam .. 29 ..
2.9.d: स्वं च विश्वसृजं ब्रह्मा ययाचेऽभिमतं वरम् .. 29 ..
2.9.m: and himself to be the creator of the universe, asked for his desired boon:

2.9.d: प्रजाविसर्गशक्तिं मे देहि तुभ्यं नमः प्रभो ..
2.9.m: 'Grant me the power to produce creatures. Homage to you, O Lord!

2.9.s: tatrāpi ca na baddhyeyaṃ yathā kuru tathā kṛpām .. 2.9.24.30 ..
2.9.d: तत्रापि च न बद्ध्येयं यथा कुरु तथा कृपाम् .. 2.9.24.30 ..
2.9.m: And show such mercy that I may not be bound even in that [task].'
Then the Blessed Lord said to him: 'Your desire will be accomplished.
Meditating through absorption on identity with me, the cosmic person (Virāj),
create offspring. Then, whenever a task cannot be achieved by you, remember me, the giver of desires.'
Having spoken thus, Viṣṇu vanished. Brahmā too, through concentrated absorption,
in his cosmic form beheld within himself all the worlds formerly dissolved.

2.9.s: visargaśaktiṃ saṃprāpya sa sargāya mano dadhe ..

2.9.m: Having obtained the power of creation, he set his mind upon creating.
Then the Sun, full of the light of the Absolute, indeed appeared.
Having placed him in the midst of the cosmic egg, he then created with his mind,
purified by austerity and devotion, the primordial sages, the four Sanas.

2.9.s: prajāḥ sṛjata cetyūce tāṃstadā te tu tadvacaḥ ..
