2.9.m: He said to them, 'Create offspring,' but then they,
the foremost of lifelong celibates, did not accept his command; and the creator of the universe grew angry with them.
From the brow of him who was angered, Rudra, full of darkness, came forth.
Restraining his wrath with his mind, he then created the lords of progeny:

2.9.s: marīcimatriṃ pulahaṃ pulastyaṃ ca bhṛguṃ kratum ..
2.9.d: मरीचिमत्रिं पुलहं पुलस्त्यं च भृगुं क्रतुम् ..
2.9.m: Marīci, Atri, Pulaha, Pulastya, Bhṛgu, Kratu,
Vasiṣṭha, Kardama, Dakṣa, and likewise Aṅgiras.
Then from his heart he created righteousness, and from his back unrighteousness;
from his mind passion, speech from his mouth, and anger from his eyebrows.

2.9.s: śaucaṃ tapo dayā satyamiti dharmapadāni ca ..
2.9.d: शौचं तपो दया सत्यमिति धर्मपदानि च ..
2.9.m: Purity, austerity, compassion, and truth: these four feet of righteousness
he then created from his four faces.
He created the Ṛgveda from the eastern face, and the Yajurveda from the southern;
from the western face he created the Sāmaveda, and from the northern the one named Atharvan.
The histories and Purāṇas, sacrifices, and a hundred brahmins,
and the Vasus, Ādityas, Maruts, Viśvedevas, and Sādhyas, he created from his mouth.
From his arms [he created] a hundred kṣatriyas, and from his thighs a hundred vaiśyas;
from his feet he created a hundred śūdras—these, along with their livelihoods.
He created studenthood from his heart, the householder's life from his loins,
likewise the forest hermitage from his chest, and renunciation from his head.
From his chest [he created] the hosts of ancestors, and the asuras from his loins;

2.9.s: sasarja ca gudānmṛtyuṃ nirṛtiṃ nirayāṃśca saḥ .. 44 ..
2.9.d: ससर्ज च गुदान्मृत्युं निरृतिं निरयांश्च सः .. 44 ..
2.9.m: and from his anus he created death, Nirṛti, and the hells.
Gandharvas, Cāraṇas, Siddhas, serpents, yakṣas, and rākṣasas,
mountains, clouds, lightnings, oceans, and rivers,
trees, beasts, and birds—all things stationary and moving—
Brahmā, identical with Nārāyaṇa, created from his very limbs.
When, even having beheld this creation, he was still not fully pleased,
he meditated on Hari and created, through austerity, knowledge, and absorption,
the seers, the Manus beginning with Svāyambhuva, and human beings as well.

2.9.s: tataḥ prītaḥ sa sarveṣāṃ nivāsāya yathocitam..
2.9.d: ततः प्रीतः स सर्वेषां निवासाय यथोचितम्..
2.9.m: Then, being pleased, for the dwelling of them all as appropriate,
he fashioned the heavenly world, the intermediate world, and the earthly world.

2.9.s: yeṣāṃ tu yādṛśaṃ karma prākkālīnaṃ hi tānvidhiḥ ..
2.9.d: येषां तु यादृशं कर्म प्राक्कालीनं हि तान्विधिः ..
2.9.m: Establishing them in an appropriate place according to the kind of action
each had performed in previous times, the Creator fashioned their livelihoods.
Nectar [he assigned] to the gods; food and herbs to men and seers;
liquor and meat to yakṣas, rākṣasas, asuras, tigers, serpents, and the like;

2.9.s: caklṛpe gomṛgādīnāṃ vṛttiṃ sa yavasādi ca .. 2.9.24.50 ..
2.9.m: and he established grass and the like as the sustenance of cattle, deer, and other beasts.

2.9.s: sa devānāṃ tu viśveṣāṃ havyaṃ vṛttimakalpayat ..
2.9.d: स देवानां तु विश्वेषां हव्यं वृत्तिमकल्पयत् ..
2.9.m: He assigned the sacrificial offering as livelihood to all the gods,

2.9.s: amūrtānāṃ ca mūrtānāṃ pitṝṇāṃ kavyameva ca .. 51 ..
2.9.d: अमूर्तानां च मूर्तानां पितॄणां कव्यमेव च .. 51 ..
2.9.m: and the ancestral offering to the formless and embodied ancestors.
To the powers (śaktis) born of Durgā, [he assigned] the wine, meat, and the like
offered by Daityas, rākṣasas, piśācas, and others intent on worshipping them.
Likewise, to the powers born of Sāvitrī, [he assigned] the wild food of sages, grain, and herbs
offered in sacrifice by seers and others who worship them.
And to the powers born of Śrī, [he assigned] milk-rice, clarified butter, sugar, and the like
offered by gods, asuras, and men devoted to their worship.
Then that lord of the lords of progeny addressed all creatures:
'The gods and the ancestors are to be worshipped with sacrifices consisting of divine and ancestral offerings.'
When worshipped, these will indeed fulfill your desires.
Those who do not worship them will surely go to hell.

2.9.s: itthaṃ kṛtā hi maryādā tena nārāyaṇātmanā ..
2.9.d: इत्थं कृता हि मर्यादा तेन नारायणात्मना ..
2.9.m: In this way the boundary [of conduct] was established by that [Lord] whose self is Nārāyaṇa.

2.9.s: daivaṃ pitryamato nityaṃ janaiḥ kāryaṃ yathāvidhi .. 57 ..
2.9.d: दैवं पित्र्यमतो नित्यं जनैः कार्यं यथाविधि .. 57 ..
2.9.m: Therefore, what is due to the gods and the ancestors must constantly be performed by people according to rule.

2.9.s: tato brahmā sa sarveṣāṃ dharmasetvavanāya ca ..
2.9.d: ततो ब्रह्मा स सर्वेषां धर्मसेत्ववनाय च ..
2.9.m: Then Brahmā, for the protection of the barrier of dharma of all beings,
also established those Manus who were chief among the various classes.
Thus, by the very will of Vāsudeva, from the Vairāja whose form is Brahmā,
manifold creation takes place in every kalpa, O sage.

2.9.s: prākkalpe yādṛśī saṃjñā vedāḥ śāstrāṇi ca kriyāḥ..
2.9.d: प्राक्कल्पे यादृशी संज्ञा वेदाः शास्त्राणि च क्रियाः..
2.9.m: Whatever designations, Vedas, scriptures, and rituals existed in the previous kalpa,
the very same dharmas and authorized persons come to be in the next kalpa.
That Viṣṇu who was mentioned, also having the nature of the Cosmic Person (Vairājapuruṣa),
nourishes all the worlds, maintaining the established bounds.
When the barriers protected by Manu and others are broken
by asuras assuming shapes at will, then Vāsudeva himself,
petitioned by Brahmā and others, manifests upon the surface of the earth.

2.9.s: avatārā bhagavato bhūtā bhāvyāśca santi ye ..
2.9.d: अवतारा भगवतो भूता भाव्याश्च सन्ति ये ..
2.9.m: Whatever avatars of the Lord have been and are to be,

2.9.s: kartuṃ na śakyate teṣāṃ saṃkhyāṃ saṃkhyāviśāradaiḥ .. 63 ..
2.9.d: कर्तुं न शक्यते तेषां संख्यां संख्याविशारदैः .. 63 ..
2.9.m: it is not possible even for those skilled in counting to compute their number.
For the protection of true dharma, the gods, and the virtuous, and for the destruction of their oppressors,
and for the welfare of all beings, the manifestation of the Lord of the virtuous takes place.

2.9.s: sa vāsudevaḥ prakṛtau puṃsi kāryeṣu caitayoḥ ..
2.9.d: स वासुदेवः प्रकृतौ पुंसि कार्येषु चैतयोः ..
2.9.m: That Vāsudeva, immanent in material nature (prakṛti), in the spirit (puruṣa), and in their effects,
also abides distinct, the supreme ruler of all, in his own abode.
Just as Agni, Varuṇa, and others, having pervaded these worlds by their portions,
abide in comfort each in their own world, so too does this Blessed Lord, O sage.
Just as before creation he was existence, consciousness, and bliss, pure, one, and devoid of guṇas,
he remains just the same—taintless—even when immanent [in creation].
Just as ether (kham), entering into wind, fire, water, earth, and their respective effects,

2.9.s: anvīyāpyasti nirlepaṃ yathā pūrvaṃ tathaiṣa hi .. 68 ..
2.9.d: अन्वीयाप्यस्ति निर्लेपं यथा पूर्वं तथैष हि .. 68 ..
2.9.m: remains untainted just as before, so indeed does he.
He is proclaimed to be the object of worship for all, the inner controller, and all-pervading.
Then, at the time of ultimate dissolution, he becomes just as he was formerly.
The Cosmic Person (Vairājapuruṣa) who is mentioned here, called Īśvara,
is to be known as independent, omniscient, and having māyā under his control, O Nārada.
His very manifestations are the three: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,
endowed with the guṇas such as rajas, their activities conforming to their respective guṇas.
Those who have arisen from Brahmā—gods, asuras, humans, and others—

2.9.s: te jīvasaṃjñā hyalpajñāḥ paratantrā bhavanti ca .. 72 ..
2.9.d: ते जीवसंज्ञा ह्यल्पज्ञाः परतन्त्रा भवन्ति च .. 72 ..
2.9.m: are called individual souls (jīvas), of limited knowledge and dependent.
The bodies of individual souls and of rulers are termed 'fields' (kṣetra),
composed of principles beginning with the intellect (mahat); but those who know them are called 'knowers of the field' (kṣetrajña).
Knowledge of the fields and of the knowers of the field, of the primordial nature (pradhāna) and the spirit (puruṣa),
of māyā, of the power of Time, of the Imperishable (akṣara), and of the Supreme Self,
according to their distinct individual characteristics—that is called knowledge.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye jñānasvarūpanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturviśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 24 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये ज्ञानस्वरूपनिरूपणं नाम चतुर्विशोऽध्यायः .. 24 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, titled 'Definition of the Nature of Knowledge', in the Śrīvāsudevamāhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.
The venerable Nārāyaṇa said:
Now I declare to you the definition of dispassion (vairāgya), O best of sages;
it is described as an absence of relish everywhere for perishable things.
Indeed, all the bodily forms beginning from the Māyāpuruṣa
are destroyed by the power of Time of the Blessed Lord, subject to it.
Through direct perception, inference, and verbal testimony, discerning people
have ascertained the unreality of created things and the reality of the self.
This Time operates in the form of the constant dissolution, the occasional dissolution,
the elemental dissolution, and the ultimate dissolution.
These bodies of embodied beings, subject to transformation, constantly waste away,
wherein childhood, youth, and old age are seen in succession.
Yet because of its subtlety, it is not seen, just like the movement of a lamp's flame,
or like the continuous growth of fruit on a tree occurring at every moment.
In each and every stage, great suffering is observed;
and in the waking and other states, suffering recurs again and again.
Abundant suffering that is internal (ādhyātmika) and suffering caused by other beings (ādhibhautika) are seen,
and suffering caused by fate or supernatural forces (ādhidaivika) here exists for embodied beings—only suffering!

2.9.s: hāhā mamāra matputro hā patnī mriyate mama ..
2.9.d: हाहा ममार मत्पुत्रो हा पत्नी म्रियते मम ..
2.9.m: "Alas, alas, my son has died! Alas, my wife is dying!

2.9.s: tātaṃ me'bhakṣayadvyāghro daṣṭā sarpeṇa me vadhūḥ .. 9 ..
2.9.d: तातं मेऽभक्षयद्व्याघ्रो दष्टा सर्पेण मे वधूः .. 9 ..
2.9.m: A tiger devoured my father! My daughter-in-law was bitten by a snake!"
"Alas, alas! Today my great mansion, along with its furnishings, has been burned by fire.
How shall I support my family? Indra has not rained.

2.9.s: sasyaiḥ samṛddhaṃ matkṣetraṃ hāhā dagdhaṃ himāgninā ..
2.9.d: सस्यैः समृद्धं मत्क्षेत्रं हाहा दग्धं हिमाग्निना ..
2.9.m: Alas, alas! My field, rich with crops, has been ruined by frost.
Cattle are being carried off by thieves; all my possessions have been plundered.
I was excessively fined by the king; alas, I was severely beaten by an enemy.

2.9.s: kiṃ karomi ca kaṃ brūyāṃ mātā me vyabhicāriṇī .. 12 ..
2.9.d: किं करोमि च कं ब्रूयां माता मे व्यभिचारिणी .. 12 ..
2.9.m: What shall I do, and to whom shall I speak? My mother is unfaithful.
I will drink poison! Alas, alas, today an enemy dragged away my wife.

2.9.s: hā svasā me hṛtā mlecchairhāhā'riḥ prāpa marmabhit .. 13 ..
2.9.d: हा स्वसा मे हृता म्लेच्छैर्हाहाऽरिः प्राप मर्मभित् .. 13 ..
2.9.m: Alas, my sister has been abducted by barbarians! Alas, alas, an enemy has struck a vital spot.
O beloved, from the intense pain of fever—alas, here are the messengers of Yama!"

2.9.s: itthaṃ rorūyamāṇā hi dṛśyante sarvato janāḥ .. 14 ..
2.9.d: इत्थं रोरूयमाणा हि दृश्यन्ते सर्वतो जनाः .. 14 ..
2.9.m: Indeed, everywhere people are seen weeping aloud in this way.
Because of the states of the body, birth and death [occur] at every moment.
By those who experience their accumulated past karma in the course of time, suffering is endured.
At the end of accumulated past karma, the agony of death arrives, which is truly matchless.
And even having died, great suffering is experienced—the torments of Yama.
Then, in the wombs of viviparous, sprouting, sweat-born, and oviparous [creatures],
being born again and again in accordance with their karma, they die again in sorrow.

2.9.s: nityaḥ pralaya evaṃ te kīrttitaḥ sūkṣmayā dṛśā ..
2.9.d: नित्यः प्रलय एवं ते कीर्त्तितः सूक्ष्मया दृशा ..
2.9.m: Thus the constant dissolution has been described to you from a subtle perspective.

2.9.s: sa jñeyo'tha mune vacmi layaṃ naimittikābhidham.. 18 ..
2.9.d: स ज्ञेयोऽथ मुने वच्मि लयं नैमित्तिकाभिधम्.. 18 ..
2.9.m: That should be understood. Now, O sage, I will speak of the dissolution termed 'occasional'.
That which takes place on the occasion of the night of the Creator of the universe,

2.9.s: naimittikaḥ sa kathito layo dainaṃdinaśca saḥ .. 19 ..
2.9.d: नैमित्तिकः स कथितो लयो दैनंदिनश्च सः .. 19 ..
2.9.m: is declared to be the occasional dissolution; it is also [called] diurnal.
A thousand cycles of four yugas is a day of the Creator of the universe, O sage;

2.9.s: niśā ca tāvatī tasya taddvayaṃ kalpa ucyate .. 2.9.25.20 ..
2.9.d: निशा च तावती तस्य तद्द्वयं कल्प उच्यते .. 2.9.25.20 ..
2.9.m: and his night is of equal length. That pair is called a kalpa.
In each day of his, fourteen
Manus appear, O brahmin, who are guardians of the barrier of dharma.
Among them, the first is Svāyambhuva Manu, then Svārociṣa,
Uttama, Tāmasa, and then Raivata and Cākṣuṣa;
Śrāddhadeva, Sāvarṇi, Bhautya, and after that Raucya;
one named Brahmasāvarṇi, and Rudrasāvarṇi;
then the one named Merusāvarṇi, and Dakṣasāvarṇi is the last.
These fourteen Manus are proclaimed in a single day of Brahmā.
The period of each Manu is seventy-one yugas,
and the duration of a [set of four] yugas is twelve thousand divine years.
When the very end of the fourteenth Manu has arrived,
the evening twilight of the Creator of the universe takes place, O best of sages.
At the close of the day, the cosmic soul withdraws the powers of preservation.
Then Rudra, whose self is the cosmic person, seeks to destroy the three worlds.
At first, a dreadful drought lasting a hundred years occurs.
Then creatures of weak constitution perish completely on the earth.
And the excessively fierce rays of the sun of the cosmic dissolution drink up
all the moisture upon the earth, quickly reaching down to Pātāla.

2.9.s: sārasaṃ caiva nādeyaṃ sāmudraṃ cāmbu sarvaśaḥ ..
2.9.d: सारसं चैव नादेयं सामुद्रं चाम्बु सर्वशः ..
2.9.m: Having completely dried up the water of the lakes, rivers,
and oceans everywhere, that sun leads all the worlds to destruction.
Then the earth becomes devoid of moisture, with all immobile and mobile beings destroyed,
resembling the back of a tortoise, dried and severely shriveled.
Then Kālāgnirudra arises from the mouth of Śeṣa;
he burns the seven lower worlds, the earth, the mid-region, and heaven.
Having incinerated ten worlds, terrifying with whorls of flame,
having depopulated Maharloka, the fire of cosmic dissolution turns round.
The gods, their offices ended, dwelling in the atmosphere and heaven,
severely tormented by the flames of fire, go from Maharloka to Janaloka.

2.9.s: nivṛttidharmā ṛṣayaḥ prāptāḥ siddhadaśāṃ tu ye ..
2.9.d: निवृत्तिधर्मा ऋषयः प्राप्ताः सिद्धदशां तु ये ..
2.9.m: The seers of renounced action who have attained the state of perfection,
even they depart from the surface of the earth to Ṛṣiloka at that time.

2.9.s: uttiṣṭhanti tato ghorā vyomni sāṃvarttakā ghanāḥ ..
2.9.d: उत्तिष्ठन्ति ततो घोरा व्योम्नि सांवर्त्तका घनाः ..
2.9.m: Then dreadful clouds of cosmic dissolution rise in the sky,
resembling herds of great elephants, flashing with lightning, roaring loudly.
Some are smoke-colored, some yellow, some resemble the white lotus,
some resemble the juice of lac, and some resemble the feather of a blue jay.
Having extinguished the great fire, day and night for a hundred years,
raining thick streams, thundering, those dense clouds
fill the interior of the cosmic egg all the way to the Pole Star.
In the waters of that single vast ocean, that cosmic Person...
The Lord, consisting of Aniruddha, lies upon the serpent-king as his bed. (39)
Then the gods and seers under the sway of passion, purity, and darkness,
drawn by their own qualities along with Viriñca,
enter into his belly and sleep in a prolonged slumber. (40)
Those, however, who perceive the oneness of the Self with Brahman and have mastered the three qualities,
worship Vāsudeva solely through the path of cessation of worldly action. (41)
Having made their residence in the four worlds beginning with Mahar,
they dwell comfortably, praising that Virāj-person. (42)
Lord Nārāyaṇa, meditating upon the Supreme Self's
essential nature named Vāsudeva, indeed rests in yogic sleep. (43)

2.9.s: niśānte brahmaṇā sākaṃ sarve te tasya jāṭharāḥ ..
2.9.d: निशान्ते ब्रह्मणा साकं सर्वे ते तस्य जाठराः ..
2.9.m: At the end of the night, all those who entered his belly, together with Brahmā,
are born again as before, qualified according to their past karma. (44)
Thus the occasional dissolution, marked by the destruction of the three worlds,
has been described to you; now I proclaim the elemental dissolution. (45)
Three hundred of such kalpas as described,

2.9.s: ṣaṣṭyādhikaṃ ca yaḥ kālo vedhasaḥ sa tu vatsaraḥ .. 46 ..
2.9.d: षष्ट्याधिकं च यः कालो वेधसः स तु वत्सरः .. 46 ..
2.9.m: along with sixty more, is the time of a year of the Creator. (46)
Fifty of those is a parārdha; the lifespan of Brahmā is considered to be two of those. / When the period called para is completed, a great dissolution occurs. (47)
[Translates the second half of 47: When the period called para is completed, a great dissolution occurs.]
Dissolving his own cosmic body in the form of Rudra the destroyer,
the Virāj-puruṣa desires to return to his own supreme, attribute-free nature. (48)
Then, as before, a drought of a hundred years occurs,
and the fire of time belonging to Saṅkarṣaṇa burns the cosmic egg completely. (49)
Then terrifying clouds of cosmic dissolution rain down,
O sage, for a hundred years with torrents thick as pestles. (50)
The dissolution of the modifications beginning with the Mahat and ending with the gross elements—
of everything indeed—then takes place by the will of Vāsudeva. (51)

2.9.s: āpo grasanti vai pūrvaṃ bhūmergandhātmakaṃ guṇam ..
2.9.d: आपो ग्रसन्ति वै पूर्वं भूमेर्गन्धात्मकं गुणम् ..
2.9.m: The waters first devour the quality of earth, which is smell;
deprived of smell, the earth is then ready for dissolution. (52)
Fire devours the quality of water, taste; then that [water] dissolves.
Wind devours form, the quality of fire; then that [fire] dissolves. (53)
Then space devours touch, the quality of wind;

2.9.s: praśāmyati tadā vāyuḥ khaṃ tu tiṣṭhatyanāvṛtam .. 54 ..
2.9.d: प्रशाम्यति तदा वायुः खं तु तिष्ठत्यनावृतम् .. 54 ..
2.9.m: the wind then subsides, while space remains uncovered. (54)

2.9.s: bhūtādistadguṇaṃ śabdaṃ grasate līyate ca kham ..
2.9.d: भूतादिस्तद्गुणं शब्दं ग्रसते लीयते च खम् ..
2.9.m: The origin of elements (tāmasa ahaṃkāra) devours its quality, sound, and space dissolves.
The senses then dissolve into the fiery ego (taijasa ahaṃkāra). (55)
The deities and the mind dissolve into the pure ego (sāttvika ahaṃkāra).
Whatever has arisen from something indeed dissolves back into that. (56)
Even the threefold ego dissolves into the principle of Mahat;

2.9.s: tatpradhāne ca tatpuṃsi sa mūlaprakṛtau tataḥ .. 57 ..
2.9.d: तत्प्रधाने च तत्पुंसि स मूलप्रकृतौ ततः .. 57 ..
2.9.m: that dissolves into Pradhāna, that into the Puruṣa, and he then into the root Nature. (57)
This is celebrated as the elemental dissolution,
in which individual souls and their lords vanish into the Unmanifest by the will of Hari. (58)
And when Māyā, Puruṣa, and Time, in the splendor of the Imperishable,

2.9.s: tadicchayā tiro yānti sa tveko vartate prabhuḥ ..
2.9.d: तदिच्छया तिरो यान्ति स त्वेको वर्तते प्रभुः ..
2.9.m: disappear by His will, and the one Lord alone remains,
then, O Nārada, that dissolution is to be known as absolute. (59)
Thus, realizing through these four kinds of dissolution by the Lord’s power of time that everything is unreal,
disinterest towards it is called dispassion. (60)
Knowing the gods other than Vāsudeva to be subject to Time and Māyā,

2.9.s: viditvā teṣu ca prītiṃ hitvā tasyaiva nityadā ..
2.9.d: विदित्वा तेषु च प्रीतिं हित्वा तस्यैव नित्यदा ..
2.9.m: and relinquishing attachment to them, the constant service to Him alone

2.9.s: gāḍhasnehena yā sevā sā bhaktiriti gīyate..61..
2.9.d: गाढस्नेहेन या सेवा सा भक्तिरिति गीयते..61..
2.9.m: with deep affection is sung as bhakti. (61)
Hearing, chanting about Him, remembering, serving the feet,

2.9.s: pūjā praṇāmo dāsyaṃ ca sakhyaṃ cātmanivedanam ..62..
2.9.d: पूजा प्रणामो दास्यं च सख्यं चात्मनिवेदनम् ..62..
2.9.m: worship, bowing down, servitude, companionship, and self-offering— (62)
whoever serves Him with reverence through these nine dispositions,

2.9.s: ananyayā dhiṣaṇayā sa hi bhakta itīryate ..63..
2.9.d: अनन्यया धिषणया स हि भक्त इतीर्यते ..63..
2.9.m: with an undistracted mind, is indeed called a devotee. (63)
This bhakti endowed with the three [virtues] headed by one's own duty, O sage,

2.9.s: dharma ekāntika iti prokto bhāgavataśca saḥ..64..
2.9.d: धर्म एकान्तिक इति प्रोक्तो भागवतश्च सः..64..
2.9.m: is declared as exclusive duty, and is also called the Bhāgavata [dharma]. (64)
Only from direct contact with the Lord and with such devotees of His

2.9.s: dharmo hyekāntikaḥ pumbhiḥ prāpyate nānyathā kvacit .. 65 ..
2.9.d: धर्मो ह्येकान्तिकः पुम्भिः प्राप्यते नान्यथा क्वचित् .. 65 ..
2.9.m: is this exclusive duty attained by mortals, never otherwise anywhere. (65)
There is no other supreme means such as this for those seeking liberation,
bringing the highest good to men and destroying all inauspiciousness. (66)
For the realization of this exclusive duty, one should be dedicated to practical yoga,
by which, O best of sages, a person attains freedom from the bondage of actions. (67)
This supreme truth, hidden in the Vedas and the Purāṇas, which destroys hosts of sins, has been proclaimed by me.

2.9.s: ekāgrayā śuddhadhiyāvadhārya sacchraddhayā cetasi te maharṣe .. 68 ..
2.9.d: एकाग्रया शुद्धधियावधार्य सच्छ्रद्धया चेतसि ते महर्षे .. 68 ..
2.9.m: Having grasped it in your mind with a one-pointed, pure intellect and true faith, O great seer,

2.9.s: na vāsudevātparamasti pāvanaṃ na vāsudevātparamasti maṅgalam ..
2.9.d: न वासुदेवात्परमस्ति पावनं न वासुदेवात्परमस्ति मङ्गलम् ..
2.9.m: There is nothing purer than Vāsudeva; there is no greater auspiciousness than Vāsudeva;

2.9.s: na vāsudevātparamasti daivataṃ na vāsudevātparamasti vāñchitam .. 69 ..
2.9.d: न वासुदेवात्परमस्ति दैवतं न वासुदेवात्परमस्ति वाञ्छितम् .. 69 ..
2.9.m: There is no higher deity than Vāsudeva; there is no object of desire superior to Vāsudeva.
Whoever here, even unknowingly, utters his name but once, even at the end of bodily life,

2.9.s: sa puṣkasopyāśu bhavapravāhādvimucyate taṃ bhaja vāsudevam ..2.9.25.70 ..
2.9.d: स पुष्कसोप्याशु भवप्रवाहाद्विमुच्यते तं भज वासुदेवम् ..2.9.25.70 ..
2.9.m: Even an outcaste is swiftly released from the stream of worldly existence. Worship that Vāsudeva!

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye vairāgyabhaktinirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 25 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये वैराग्यभक्तिनिरूपणं नाम पञ्चविंशोऽध्यायः .. 25 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, named 'The Exposition of Dispassion and Devotion', in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second [section], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand [verses]. // 25
Skanda said:
Having heard the exposition of single-minded religious duty spoken by the Blessed Lord,
With an overjoyed mind, that Nārada questioned him once more. / 1
Nārada said:
O Lord, the single-minded duty has been fully expounded by you;
Having heard it, great joy has arisen in my mind. / 2

2.9.s: siddhaye tasya bhavatā kriyāyogo ya ucyate ..
2.9.d: सिद्धये तस्य भवता क्रियायोगो य उच्यते ..
2.9.m: For its perfection, the yoga of action which is spoken of by you,
That which is your doctrine, O Blessed Lord, I desire to understand. / 3
The glorious Nārāyaṇa said:
The procedure of worship of Vāsudeva is celebrated as the yoga of action.

2.9.s: sa tu vedeṣu tantreṣu bahudhaivāsti varṇitaḥ .. 4 ..
2.9.d: स तु वेदेषु तन्त्रेषु बहुधैवास्ति वर्णितः .. 4 ..
2.9.m: Indeed, it is described in many ways in the Vedas and the Tantras. / 4
Due to the variety of the devotees' tastes, and likewise because of the diversity
Of the forms of Vāsudeva, it is expounded in many ways. / 5
Truly, there is no reaching the end of it if it were told in its entirety;
Therefore, I shall tell you in brief that which enhances devotion. / 6

2.9.s: prāptā ye vaiṣṇavīṃ dīkṣāṃ varṇāścatvāra āśramāḥ ..
2.9.d: प्राप्ता ये वैष्णवीं दीक्षां वर्णाश्चत्वार आश्रमाः ..
2.9.m: Those who have received Vaiṣṇava initiation—the four classes, the stages of life,
And the women of the four classes—these are declared to be eligible in this matter. / 7
Twice-borns should worship with mantras declared in the Vedas, Tantras, and Purāṇas, and with the root mantra;
Initiated women and virtuous Śūdras [should worship] with the root mantra.
The root mantra of the glorious Kṛṣṇa is to be known as six-syllabled. / 8
Observing their own respective duties, by all of these, according to the prescribed rule,
Vāsudeva should be worshipped with devotion by those with sincere hearts. / 9

2.9.s: ādau tu vaiṣṇavīṃ dīkṣāṃ gṛhṇīyātsadvaroḥ pumān ..
2.9.d: आदौ तु वैष्णवीं दीक्षां गृह्णीयात्सद्वरोः पुमान् ..
2.9.m: First, however, a man should receive Vaiṣṇava initiation from an excellent guru,
Who is ever established in single-minded duty, born of a brahmin family, and a treasure of compassion. / 10
One endowed with knowledge and devotion, but bereft of his own duty,

2.9.s: sa gurunnaiva kartavyaḥ strīhṛtātmā ca karhicit .. 11 ..
2.9.d: स गुरुन्नैव कर्तव्यः स्त्रीहृतात्मा च कर्हिचित् .. 11 ..
2.9.m: Or one whose mind is captivated by women, must never be made a guru. / 11

2.9.s: prāptā straiṇādgurordīkṣā jñānaṃ bhaktiṃ ca karhicit ..
2.9.d: प्राप्ता स्त्रैणाद्गुरोर्दीक्षा ज्ञानं भक्तिं च कर्हिचित् ..
2.9.m: Initiation received from a womanizing guru will never bear fruit
In knowledge and devotion, just as a young woman uniting with a eunuch [bears no] offspring. / 12
Therefore, having received initiation from a true guru, one should wear a tulasī garland on the neck,
And the upward mark on the forehead and elsewhere made with gopīcandana. / 13
A devotee desiring to worship Viṣṇu, having thoroughly understood from his guru
The rite of worship declared in the scriptures, should then begin the worship. / 14
Rising in the final watch of the night, or at the hour of Brahmā,
A devotee should meditate in his heart for half a muhūrta on Keśava, the destroyer of distress. / 15
Having chanted his names and those of his devotees for a nāḍikā,
Having then performed the rite of purification, he should clean his teeth. / 16
Having first performed a bath for the purification of the body, he should bathe with mantras;
Taking pure earth and other items, he should perform the libation that is part of the bath. / 17
Putting on two washed garments, sitting on a pure seat,

Then he should gather all the offerings, such as garments, sandalwood paste, and flowers,
Free from contact with impure things such as meat and liquor, / 19
Not offered to other gods or ancestors,
Not smelled by human beings, and free from hairs, insects, and the like. / 20
Placing them and the implements of worship on his right side,
He should then light a lamp with clarified butter or with oil. / 21

2.9.m: That image of Kṛṣṇa should be made either two-armed or four-armed;
There, on the two-armed one, he should hold a flute in his two hands. / 24
Or else, on its right hand a discus, and similarly a conch on the other.
Or [she/he] should hold a lotus in the right hand, and the gesture of fearlessness in the left (or upper).
On the hands of the second [four-armed form], however, beginning with the lower right hand in succession,
one should place the mace, the lotus, the conch, and the discus, O best of sages.
On the left side of both forms of Hari, one should place Śrī.
On the left side of the flute-bearer, however, one should place Rādhā, the queen of the rāsa-dance.
Even this twofold image, unbroken, possessed of auspicious marks,
and complete with all limbs, bestows perfection upon the worshipper.
Lakṣmī, however, should be made two-armed in the presence of Vāsudeva,
holding a lotus in her hand, adorned with splendid garments and ornaments.
Like Lakṣmī, Rādhikā too should be two-armed, with a charming smile,
holding a lotus or a garland of flowers in her lotus-hand.

2.9.m: The image of Hari is twofold: immovable and movable.
In the case of the former, invocation and ritual dismissal are not to be performed.
Nor should invocation and the like be performed for the subsidiary deities of its limbs.

2.9.s: na ca diṅniyamo'rcāyāṃ tasyāḥ stheyaṃ tu sammukhe ..32..

2.9.m: Nor is there a rule of direction regarding worship of it, but one should stand facing it.
In the case of a Śālagrāma stone as well, precisely thus invocation and the like are not to be performed.
Elsewhere, in the case of a movable image, that [invocation etc.] must be performed by their respective worshippers.
Even there, in the case of a wooden or painted image, contact with water and unguents
must not be performed by the worshipper; [only] wiping clean is to be done.

2.9.s: udaṅmukhaḥ prāṅmukho vā calāyāṃ sammukho'tha vā ..
2.9.d: उदङ्मुखः प्राङ्मुखो वा चलायां सम्मुखोऽथ वा ..
2.9.m: Facing north, or facing east, or else facing directly toward the movable image,
one should worship Hari according to one's capacity, with offerings as obtained.
He, the Soul of all, pleased even with water offered
with faith and sincere devotion, is satisfied—how much more so with complete worship!
Ornaments of jewels, gold, and the like, presented by a person devoid of faith and the like,

2.9.s: caturvidhaṃ cāpyannādyaṃ dattaṃ gṛhṇāti no mudā .. 37 ..
2.9.d: चतुर्विधं चाप्यन्नाद्यं दत्तं गृह्णाति नो मुदा .. 37 ..
2.9.m: and the fourfold food and other offerings given, he does not accept with joy.
Therefore, O sage, for his own welfare, a devoted person must perform
the regular worship of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, who swiftly bestows all desired objects.

2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named "Ascertainment of the Qualification for Kriyāyoga and Related Topics," in the Śrī Vāsudeva-māhātmya of the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

with both hands placed upon his thighs, gazing at the tip of his own nose.
Likewise in the northeast, Pāñcarātra, white, wearing a forest garland,

The garments of these four should be white, fine, and dense,
and their eyes should be broad like lotus petals.

All of these are two-armed, bearing matted locks and beards, lean,
ascetics who are to be depicted carrying staffs and water pots.

2.9.m:
Outside the lotus, in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
one should place the eight directional guardians headed by Indra, each according to his direction, along with their mounts.
In the east one should place Indra mounted upon Airāvata, four-armed,
bearing a thunderbolt, goad, lotus, and the boon gesture, resembling gold,
clad in lovely safflower-dyed garments, adorned with various ornaments,
with red-cornered, large eyes, endowed with all auspicious marks.
In the southeast corner one should place Agni, copper-colored, four-armed,
holding in his hands a spear, a lance, a sruc-ladle, and a sruva-ladle,
seated in a golden chariot with four parrots, having the wind as his charioteer,
three-eyed, wearing smoke-colored garments, with tawny beard, matted hair, and eyes.
In the south one should place Yama, dark, with golden garments,
four-armed, carrying a staff, sword, battle-axe, and noose,
mounted upon a frenzied buffalo, adorned with various ornaments.
In the southwest one should install the lord of the south-west (Nirṛti), whose hair stands upright and who has odd eyes,
holding a sword and a noose, two-armed, mounted upon a human corpse;

Then, in the west, [one should place] Varuṇa, who has the lustre of a sapphire,
clad in white garments, four-armed, adorned with a necklace of pearls,
mounted upon a chariot of seven swans, holding a noose with two hands,

clad in dark blue, bearded, seated upon a palanquin,
with a yellowish left eye, wearing various ornaments and clad in armor.

on the side of Umā, a forehead-mark is to be made on the brow, along with a parting of the hair.
One half is smeared with ashes, and the other half is adorned with saffron;
one half has a serpent as a sacred thread, and the other half is adorned with a necklace.
On the left half, a swelling breast covered by a bodice should be fashioned;
on the waist a golden girdle, and on the foot a golden anklet;
a safflower-dyed garment, both hands adorned with bangles,
holding a trident and a rosary, with jeweled rings.
On the right half, a serpentine girdle is to be made, and an elephant hide as garment;
the hands have serpent-bracelets and hold a mirror and a lotus.
Such a Mahādeva, mounted upon a bull, one should install.
In this manner the worshiper should perform the installation of the lords of the eight directions.
Outside the city, then, the worshiper should install the eight planets,
abiding in their respective directions and mounted upon their respective chariots.
In the eastern direction one should install there the Sun, clad in yellow garments,
vermilion-colored, two-armed, with lotuses in his hands, standing upon a chariot.

The chariot of this radiant one has one wheel with twelve spokes,
and seven green-hued horses are harnessed on the left.
Then in the south-east corner Bhṛgu (Venus) is to be placed, white, clad in white,
holding a staff and a water-pot, two-armed, gentle in appearance,
standing in a golden chariot with ten dappled horses.
And in the south one should install Mars, red, clad in red garments,
four-armed, bearing a mace, a spear, a trident, and the gesture of granting boons.
One should make his chariot golden, provided with eight red-brown horses.
And Rāhu in the south-west corner is clad in blue, four-armed,
with a terrible mouth, having the form of darkness, holding a shield, a sword, a spear, and a trident;
he is to be made standing in an iron chariot drawn by eight horses colored like black bees.
And Saturn is to be placed in the west, with a radiance like sapphire,
bearing a bow and a trident, two-armed, with downcast eyes, clad in dark garments,
standing in an iron chariot yoked with eight variegated horses.
Then in the north-west corner one should place the Moon, clad in white garments,

white-hued, holding a mace, two-armed, and seated in a chariot.
On his watery chariot with three wheels of a hundred spokes,
ten horses lustrous like jasmine flowers are yoked on both sides.
In the north, Mercury is two-armed, gentle, his hands granting boons and fearlessness, reddish,
clad in green garments, to be depicted standing in a golden chariot with eight tawny horses.
And in the north-east Guru (Jupiter) is to be placed, golden-colored, clad in white garments,
two-armed, lotus-eyed, holding a staff and a water-pot,
seated in an excellent golden chariot drawn by eight pale-white horses.
In this way the worshiper should install the subsidiary deities of the Lord,
all of them in order in the places up to the pericarp, the mountain, and the city.
A wealthy person should install actual idols of the subsidiary deities of Vāsudeva,
while another may place areca nuts, or flowers and unbroken grains of rice, etc.
Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Rules for Constructing the Worship Maṇḍala' in the Section on Ritual Practice (Kriyāyoga) of the Glorious Vāsudevamāhātmya in the Second Section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

2.9.m: Śrī Nārāyaṇa said: / On the ground purified by digging, sprinkling, smearing, and the like, / and beautifully decorated with various colours, one should place a four-legged pedestal. / Facing east, the worshipper should arrange the legs of the pedestal at the corners. / Upon those four [legs] he should install the [principles], beginning with Dharma, in the form of lions: / he should place white Dharma in the south-east, and red Jñāna in the south-west; / yellow Vairāgya in the north-west, and black Aiśvarya in the north-east. / Then on the side-timbers of the pedestal, in the directions beginning with the east, in order, / he should place Manas, Dhī, Citta, and Ahaṅkāra, respectively green, red, white, and black. / The three qualities of Rajas, Sattva, and Tamas—red, white, and black—/ are to be installed, O best of sages, on the upper rim of the pedestal. / Then upon the four side-timbers in the form of the inner organs of mind, / he should place the śaktis beginning with Vimalā, two on each timber: / he should place two fair-limbed ones, Vimalā and Utkarṣiṇī, in the east, / playing a beautiful vīṇā, clad in green garments and well adorned; / he should place Jñānā and Kriyā in the south, clad in yellow garments and shining like dawn, / one playing cymbals and the other the mṛdaṅga drum; / he should place Yogā and Prahvī in the west, dark in complexion and wearing reddish-brown garments, / both playing flutes together, yet individually; / then he should place Satya and Īśānā in the north, gold-coloured, / clad in dark garments, both playing the parivādinī lute; / and one named Anugrahā, with folded hands, is to be placed upon the rim. / All of these [śaktis] should be made two-armed and adorned with fine ornaments. / Above the pedestal he should make a white island with a white cloth; / in the middle of it he should make an eight-petalled lotus with a radiant pericarp. / Leaving aside a twelfth portion beyond the field of the lotus, / he should divide its interior into equal parts with three circles: / the first [circle] there is the place of the pericarp; the middle one belongs to the filaments; / the third belongs to the petals, with the tips of the petals extending outward. / All around it he should construct a city with four gates.

2.9.m: With various colouring substances such as turmeric, saffron, and the like, / or with husked rice-grains, one should make the beautiful lotus and other designs there. / In the middle, the worshipper should make the pericarp of the lotus splendid with a golden colour, / and all around it, O sage, he should make the eight petals in the eight directions red, / or else golden in colour. / He should make the eastern gateway red, and the southern one black, / the western one yellow, and the northern one resembling crystal. / In the space between the city and the lotus having placed diverse flowers, / and having installed Śrī Kṛṣṇa in the middle, he should place Rādhikā on his left. / Then behind this Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa he should place Saṃkarṣaṇa, / four-armed, holding an umbrella, fair-limbed, and wearing blue garments. / To the right of the Lord he should place Pradyumna, wearing yellow garments, / four-armed, cloud-dark, standing and holding a fly-whisk. / And to the left of Hari he should place Aniruddha, wearing reddish-brown garments, / dark like a sapphire gem, standing and holding a fly-whisk. / All three of these should be made adorned with various ornaments, / with priceless gem-studded crowns, and enchanting with their youthfulness. / Then he should place the avatars of Hari on the eight filaments in order, / two on each one, thus indeed sixteen upon the eight: / he should install Vāmana and Buddha on the eastern filament in front, / both of them cloud-dark, compassionate, and observant of celibacy, / wearing white garments, holding an open lotus in the right hand / and the gesture of fearlessness in the left hand, peaceful, and wearing sacred threads; / then he should place Kalki and Paraśurāma in the south-east corner, / Kalki holding a sword in his hand there, and the other holding an axe in his hand; / both are to be made fair-skinned, red-eyed, with matted hair, wearing white garments, / wearing sacred threads, and with immense fury cast aside; / and he should install Hayagrīva and Varāha on the southern filament; / Hayagrīva should have the face of a horse, a human body, and four arms.

2.9.m: holding a conch and other attributes, golden-colored, wearing divine white garments. / Varāha, however, should have a boar's face, a human body, and four arms, / holding a conch, discus, mace, and lotus, and wearing yellow garments; / he may be honey-tawny in color, or else two-armed. / Then one should install Matsya and Kūrma in the southwest filament; / below the waist they have their [creature] forms, but above they have human shape, / both holding a conch in the left hand and a mace in the right, / with dark and beautiful bodies, adorned with ornaments. / One should place Dhanvantari and Nṛsiṃha in the western filament; / Dhanvantari wears white garments, is fair-limbed, and holds a pot of nectar. / Nṛsiṃha has a lion's face, a human body, and is endowed with a mane; / he has the hue of a blue lotus, is two-armed, and bears a mace and a discus. / In the northwest one should place both Haṃsa and Dattātreya wearing matted hair, / in the garb of yogins, white, holding a staff and water pot in their hands. / Then one should place Vyāsa and Gaṇapati in the northern filament; / there Vyāsa is large-eyed, dark in color, wearing white garments, / two-armed, holding the Vedas, possessing very reddish-brown matted locks, / wearing a white sacred thread, and equipped with a pavitra ring. / Gaṇapati should have an elephant's face, a single tusk, and be red, / wearing red garments, and possessing a serpent for a sacred thread, / pot-bellied and four-armed, holding a noose, goad, and the gesture of bestowing boons, / and with one hand holding a delightful book and writing pen. / Then the worshipper should place Kapila in the northeast filament, / and the sage Sanatkumāra, a lifelong celibate. / Kapila should be made fair-limbed, wearing charming white garments, / holding a lotus and the gesture of fearlessness with his two hands, with a peaceful form. / The sage Sanatkumāra should be made by the worshipper / resembling a five-year-old child, sky-clad, and bearing small matted locks. / Having thus established the deities in the filaments of the lotus,

2.9.m: the worshipper should place the attendants in the middle of the eight petals. / There, first in the east, one should place Viṣvaksena and Garuḍa; / then in clockwise order, one should place Prabala and Bala, / Kumuda and Kumudākṣa, Sunanda and Nanda, / Śrutadeva and Jayanta, and one should install Vijaya and Jaya; / then Pracaṇḍa and Caṇḍa, and Puṣpadanta and Sātvata. / Thus two by two in regular order one should install them in the eight positions. / All of these are four-armed, bearing a conch, discus, lotus, and mace; / they should be crowned, dark-complexioned, wearing yellow garments, and well-ornamented. / In the intervals between the middles of the petals, one should install the eight supernatural powers, / skilled in order at playing various auspicious musical instruments: / aṇimā, laghimā, prāpti, prākāmya, and mahimā, / īśitā, vaśitā, and the eighth, kāmāvasāyitā. / These have the luster of golden color, are adorned with all ornaments, / hold flutes, vīṇās, and the like in their hands, and are dressed in multicolored garments. / Then on the eight petal-tips one should install the Vedas and the treatises; / there he should install the Vedas in the cardinal directions, and the treatises in the intermediate directions. / In the east one should place the Ṛgveda, holding a rosary, white, / dwarfish, pot-bellied, gentle, lotus-eyed, and clad in white garments. / In the south one should place the Yajurveda, of medium limbs, slender-waisted, / yellow-eyed, thick-necked, yellow-complexioned, and wearing reddish garments, / bearing a garland of beads in the left hand and a thunderbolt in the right. / In the west one should place the Sāmaveda, tall, with the splendor of the sun, / holding a rosary in the right hand and a conch in the left, / dressed in gold cloth, large-eyed, intent on singing. / In the north one should place the Atharva[veda], white-limbed, wearing blue garments, / bearing a rosary in the left hand and a club with a skull in the right, / with the radiance of fire, copper-colored eyes, and aged in years. / In the southeast corner one should place the Dharmaśāstra, seated on a lotus,

2.9.m: white, and bearing with his two arms an incomparable pearl necklace. / In the southwest one should place Sāṃkhya, pot-bellied, with long hair and nails,
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having sipped water and controlled his breaths, then, composed in mind,
having bowed to the chosen deity and others, he should mention the place and time:
“For the accomplishment of unswerving devotion, the worship of Vāsudeva
I shall perform”—having thus formed the intention, he should then perform the rite of nyāsa.

2.9.s: nyāse mantrā dvādaśārṇo gāyatrī vaiṣṇavī tathā..
2.9.d: न्यासे मन्त्रा द्वादशार्णो गायत्री वैष्णवी तथा..
2.9.m: The mantras for nyāsa are the twelve-syllabled, the Vaiṣṇava Gāyatrī,
the eight-syllabled mantra of Nārāyaṇa, and the six-syllabled mantra of Viṣṇu.
These are prescribed for twice-born men, but for others here three [are prescribed]:
the eight-syllabled mantra of Vāsudeva, the five-syllabled mantra of Hari,

2.9.s: ṣaḍarṇaḥ keśavasyeti nyāse home ca saṃmatāḥ .. 4 ..
2.9.d: षडर्णः केशवस्येति न्यासे होमे च संमताः .. 4 ..
2.9.m: and the six-syllabled mantra of Keśava are approved for nyāsa and for oblations.
Then, on the limbs of the image of Śrī Viṣṇu just as on one's own limbs,
he should perform all the nyāsas with those mantras, and then wipe the image with a cloth.
