2.9.m: Placing a water-jar on his left side and invoking into it
the sacred fords, he should worship it with offerings such as perfume and flowers.
Sprinkling the worship materials and himself with that water,

2.9.s: śaṃkhaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ ca saṃpūjya bhūtaśuddhiṃ samācaret..7..
2.9.d: शंखं घण्टां च संपूज्य भूतशुद्धिं समाचरेत्..7..
2.9.m: worshiping the conch and the bell, he should perform the purification of the elements.
Having burned the body consisting of sin with the internal fire and wind,
firmly concentrated, he should contemplate the identity of his purified self with Brahman.
Then, having assumed the nature of imperishable Brahman, he should meditate in his heart on Lord Rādhākṛṣṇa
with an undistracted mind, while performing breath control.
Having visualized the downward-facing navel-lotus, resembling a plantain flower,
he should unite the downward apāna breath with the upward prāṇa.
Bringing that [breath] into the lotus stalk, together with it he should draw
that lotus upward; then, sounding loudly, it reaches the heart,
and blossoming there, shining in the space of the heart.
There, in that mass of splendour, he should meditate on the husband of Śrī Rādhikā,
who possesses splendour surpassing even that, who is exceedingly delightful to behold and tranquil,
seated or standing, whose divine form is composed of pure consciousness,
adolescent in age, more handsome than ten million gods of love,
distinguished by divine limbs that are fully symmetrical with his beauty,
with a body radiant as the autumn moon, with two long and handsome arms,
with lotus feet having reddish, soft soles and lovely toes,
putting the moon to shame with the brilliance of his raised, red, and glossy nails,
with the beauty of a pair of feet wearing tinkling small bells, anklets, and ornaments,
with well-rounded calves and splendid symmetrical knees and thighs,
with hips beautified by yellow garments fastened by a girdle of fine gems,
with three folds above an elevated belly and a deep navel,
with a broad and raised chest adorned with the Śrīvatsa curl,
ornamented with hanging necklaces of various strands such as the devacchanda,
wearing garlands of various fragrant flowers and a golden sacred thread,
adorned with bracelets on hands resembling blossoming red lotuses,
with several rings of fine gems shining on his fingers of delicate joints,
sounding a flute that is sweet and charms everyone,
with broad shoulders, hidden collarbones, and armlets shining on his mighty arms,
with a forest garland humming with swarms of bees drawn by wandering fragrances,
with a neck resembling a conch, shining with an exquisite necklace and the Kaustubha gem,
with a beautiful chin and the lustre of lower lips red as bimba fruit,
with a face resembling the full moon shining with the grace of a bright smile,
with an attractive, handsome nose shaped like a sesame flower,
with makara-shaped earrings shining on symmetrical ears,
with ear-ornaments consisting of bunches of varied flowers sparkling above the ears,
with cheeks splendid with the moonlight radiance of even and delicate teeth,
with delightful eyes broad as lotus petals and red at the corners,
with a broad, high forehead and eyebrows acting like the bow of the god of love,
with curly, fine, black, glossy, and enchanting hair,
bearing a crest on a diadem inlaid with various fine gems,

2.9.s: premṇā nijaṃ vīkṣamāṇaṃ prasannaṃ snigdhayā dṛśā .. 27 ..
2.9.d: प्रेम्णा निजं वीक्षमाणं प्रसन्नं स्निग्धया दृशा .. 27 ..
2.9.m: graciously looking upon his devotee with love and an affectionate gaze.
Having meditated thus on Kṛṣṇa, he should then reflect upon Rādhā at his left side:
two-armed, with limbs radiant like gold, wearing an immaculate safflower garment,
with a nose-ring made of jewels gleaming beside symmetrical ears,
a youthful maiden, with eyes like a fawn's, with full, elevated, and firm breasts,
slender-waisted, broad-hipped, adorned with a jeweled girdle,
having manifold divine ornaments, smiling with a face like a blooming lotus, // 2.9.28.30
her hands shining with jeweled rings, armlets, bracelets, and other ornaments,
her lotus feet radiant with tinkling swan-like anklets, // 31
bearing an auspicious mark of fine Kashmir saffron shining upon her broad forehead,
with lips red like bimba fruit, lovely cheeks, and mālatī blossoms woven into her braided hair, // 32
gazing upon the Lord with love, holding a lotus in her hand.
Having thus meditated upon Rādhikā there, he should worship the Lord together with her. // 33

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye kriyāyoge śrīrādhākṛṣṇasvarūpadhyānanirūpaṇaṃ nāmā'ṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 28 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये क्रियायोगे श्रीराधाकृष्णस्वरूपध्याननिरूपणं नामाऽष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः .. 28 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, entitled "Delineation of the Meditation on the Form of Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa" in the [section on] ritual yoga of the glorious Vāsudevamāhātmya, in the second, Vaiṣṇava Section, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. // 28
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:
Having worshiped him mentally with diverse kinds of offerings,
the devotee should invoke him and establish him in the image with the mudrā of establishment. // 1
Then, having invoked the deities of his limbs severally with their respective mantras,
or with the mantras of their names, he should firmly establish them. // 2
He should play instruments such as the bell, or clap hands.
Then he should have him cleanse his teeth as if he had just awakened from sleep. // 3
With water mixed with śyāmāka grain, viṣṇukāntā flowers, dūrvā grass, and lotuses,
he should offer this foot-water to the Lord; then [he should offer] water for the guest-offering and sipping water. // 4
Sandalwood, unbroken rice, flowers, tips of darbha grass, sesame seeds, mustard seeds,
barley, and dūrvā grass he should put into the arghya vessel filled with water. // 5
Scented with nutmeg, cloves, cardamom, kaṅkola, and uśīra root,
he should offer water for sipping; then he should bathe Hari. // 6
First he should perform anointing with fragrant floral oil;
then he should perform unction with a paste of aromatic substances. // 7

2.9.s: kṣīreṇa dadhnā cājyena madhunā sitayā tathā ..
2.9.d: क्षीरेण दध्ना चाज्येन मधुना सितया तथा ..
2.9.m: With milk, curd, clarified butter, honey, and likewise sugar,
undistracted, he should bathe Hari severally with their respective mantras. // 8
Having caused him to bathe with fragrant, pure, and warm water,
he should briefly worship him on the bath pedestal with scents and other offerings. // 9
Then, having cast aside the used flowers and other offerings toward the north, the twice-born
should perform the ceremonial bath either with the Sāman hymns beginning with Rājana, or with the lore of the Great Puruṣa,
or with the Śrīsūkta and the Viṣṇusūkta. // 2.9.29.10
Initiated women and śūdras, however,
should perform the ceremonial bath with the thousand names or with the one hundred and eight names of Hari. // 11
Then, having wiped him with a cloth, he should dress him in priceless garments
with great love, and also Rādhā and the others according to his capacity. // 12
He should give a fine, white, auspicious sacred thread to the Lord,
and put ornaments of gems, gold, and other materials on him together with his limbs. // 13
According to the season, on the proper places, and as appropriate with sandalwood paste,
he should make forehead marks and body anointing with saffron, camphor, and other substances. // 14
And having adorned Rādhikā with appropriate ornaments,
he should apply decorative leafy drawings and a tilaka mark with kumkuma and unbroken rice. // 15
Then, having shown him a mirror, [and having adorned him] with flower garlands, crest ornaments, and the like,
he should worship him with a thousand tulasī shoots and leaves; // 16

2.9.s: tulasyā vā'tha puṣpeṇa pratyekaṃ nāma vaiṣṇavam ..
2.9.d: तुलस्या वाऽथ पुष्पेण प्रत्येकं नाम वैष्णवम् ..
2.9.m: or, reciting each Vaiṣṇava name ending in the dative with 'namaḥ',
he should worship the Lord with a tulasī leaf or a flower. // 17
Then, having offered fragrant powders of aromatic substances and auspicious articles,
he should offer ten-ingredient incense or nectar-scented incense and the like. // 18
He should offer a lamp made with ghee and lit with two wicks.
He should present a great food offering, pure and prepared according to his capacity: // 19
saṃyāva cakes, milk rice, apūpa cakes, śaṣkulī pastries, sugar candy, laddu sweets,
crisp pūrikā cakes, polikā flatbreads, cooked rice with mung beans, and cooked vegetables,
and curds, milk, ghee, and other items, placed upon a four-legged stand. // 2.9.29.20
He should then feed him with love, offering drinking water midway.
When half a muhūrta has elapsed, he should offer water for washing the hands. // 21
Having assigned the Lord's leftover food to deities such as Viṣvaksena,
he should set it aside elsewhere for himself and wipe that ground. // 22
Then he should offer a mouth-perfume, a prepared betel roll
combined with areca-nut powder, cloves, cardamom, mace, and nutmeg. // 23

2.9.s: phalaṃ ca nālikerādi dattvā śaktyā ca dakṣiṇām ..
2.9.d: फलं च नालिकेरादि दत्त्वा शक्त्या च दक्षिणाम् ..
2.9.m: And having offered fruits such as coconuts, and a priestly fee according to his capacity,
One should perform the great waving of lamps preceded by songs and instrumental music.
Offering double handfuls of flowers, one should then praise Him with His own hymn;
singing and dancing before Him, one should perform the chanting of His names.

2.9.s: muhūrttaṃ sa vidhāyetthaṃ kṛtvā caiva pradakṣiṇām ..
2.9.d: मुहूर्त्तं स विधायेत्थं कृत्वा चैव प्रदक्षिणाम् ..
2.9.m: Having done this for a muhūrta and having circumambulated [the deity],
one should make a prostration like a rod on the ground to His right, horizontally.
A man should perform either an eight-limbed or a five-limbed prostration;
a woman, however, [should perform] only a five-limbed one, never otherwise, O best of sages!
With feet, hands, knees, chest, head, eyes,
speech, and mind—thus the eight-limbed prostration is declared.

2.9.s: bāhubhyāṃ caiva manasā śirasā vacasā dṛśā ..
2.9.d: बाहुभ्यां चैव मनसा शिरसा वचसा दृशा ..
2.9.m: With both arms, mind, head, speech, and eyes—
this is the five-limbed prostration; these two are preeminent in rituals of worship.

2.9.s: bhītaṃ māṃ saṃsṛteḥ pāhi prapannaṃ tvāṃ prabho iti ..
2.9.d: भीतं मां संसृतेः पाहि प्रपन्नं त्वां प्रभो इति ..
2.9.m: ‘O Lord, protect me, frightened of worldly existence, who have taken refuge in You!’

2.9.s: tataḥ saṃprārtha svādhyāyaṃ śaktyā kurvīta naityakam .. 2.9.29.30 ..
2.9.d: ततः संप्रार्थ स्वाध्यायं शक्त्या कुर्वीत नैत्यकम् .. 2.9.29.30 ..
2.9.m: Having prayed thus, one should perform daily recitation of sacred texts according to one's capacity.

2.9.s: dhyātvā śeṣāṃ ca taddattāṃ gṛhītvā śirasādarāt ..
2.9.d: ध्यात्वा शेषां च तद्दत्तां गृहीत्वा शिरसादरात् ..
2.9.m: Having meditated and respectfully placed upon one’s head the remnant given by Him,
one should establish Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa, invoked as previously, in the lotus of the heart,
and dismiss the attendant deities to their respective places.

2.9.s: karaṇḍake vā śayyāyāṃ mandire pratimāṃ hareḥ ..
2.9.d: करण्डके वा शय्यायां मन्दिरे प्रतिमां हरेः ..
2.9.m: Having laid Hari's image to rest in a basket, on a bed, or in the shrine,
and having closed the door, one should perform the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice.
Distributing the food offered to Hari among those dependent upon him,
and having eaten himself, he should spend the rest of the day with discourses about Him and the like.
Whoever worships Viṣṇu every day with devotion according to this prescribed method of great worship
becomes His attendant.
Ascending a celestial aerial chariot, radiant and desired even by the gods,
the worshipper, having a celestial body, goes to the abode of Hari known as Goloka.
Even he who worships Him day after day with an aim for results
also attains righteousness, desire, wealth, and desired liberation.
Unable to perform the rite of worship in this manner,
one should worship Hari alone, together with Rādhā, with devotion by means of whatever articles of worship are obtained.
A twice-born should worship Śrī Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa with the twelve-syllable mantra, another with a name-mantra;
devotion alone grants success in this regard.
Especially on the eleventh day of the fortnight, on the festival of Hari’s birth, and on other occasions,
the great worship alone must be performed by all Vaiṣṇavas according to their capacity.
Whoever performs even mere consecration in a temple built by another,
his sins destroyed, truly attains universal sovereignty.
And a wealthy man who has a beautiful, sturdy temple made for Hari
attains undisputed sovereignty even over the three worlds.
He who perpetuates the continuous flow of worship through the grant of a livelihood—
that man certainly attains great happiness in the world of Viṣṇu.

2.9.s: pratiṣṭhāṃ mandiraṃ pūjāṃ kāraye ttrīṇyapīha yaḥ ..
2.9.d: प्रतिष्ठां मन्दिरं पूजां कारये त्त्रीण्यपीह यः ..
2.9.m: Whoever causes all three to be made here—consecration, a temple, and worship—
certainly attains lordship equal to that of Vāsudeva.

2.9.s: harervṛrttiṃ haredyastu kṛtāṃ svena pareṇa vā ..
2.9.d: हरेर्वृर्त्तिं हरेद्यस्तु कृतां स्वेन परेण वा ..
2.9.m: Whoever confiscates a livelihood dedicated to Hari, whether granted by himself or by another,

2.9.s: kalpamekaṃ sa vai bhuṃkte narake yamayātanāḥ .. 44 ..
2.9.d: कल्पमेकं स वै भुंक्ते नरके यमयातनाः .. 44 ..
2.9.m: truly suffers the torments of Yama in hell for an entire kalpa.
The doer, the one who causes it to be done, the helper, and the one who approves—

2.9.s: caturṇāṃ hi phale bhāgaḥ sukṛtasyetarasya ca ..45..
2.9.d: चतुर्णां हि फले भागः सुकृतस्येतरस्य च ..45..
2.9.m: the share in the fruit of a good deed as well as of the other belongs indeed to these four.
Thus the rule of the yoga of action has been expounded by me, O Nārada,
by which single-minded duty may be accomplished in this world for those whose minds are intent upon it.
Contemplating sense-objects in the mind while outwardly performing the worship of Hari,

2.9.s: saṃbhāreṇāpi mahatā na yathoktaṃ phalaṃ labhet.. .. 47 ..
2.9.d: संभारेणापि महता न यथोक्तं फलं लभेत्.. .. 47 ..
2.9.m: even with abundant provisions, one does not obtain the stated fruit.
Restraining his own mind, which wanders here and there in vulgar pleasures, from that [distraction],
one who desires liberation should become intent upon the worship of Viṣṇu.
Even those of great vows, those of immense austerities, those who have thoroughly studied the Vedas, those who are intelligent,

2.9.s: sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ pariśīlayantaḥ siddhiṃ na yāntyeva vinārcanaṃ hareḥ .. 49 ..
2.9.d: सांख्यं च योगं परिशीलयन्तः सिद्धिं न यान्त्येव विनार्चनं हरेः .. 49 ..
2.9.m: and those practicing Sāṃkhya and Yoga do not achieve perfection at all without the worship of Hari.

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye kriyāyoge śrīvāsudevapūjāvidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..29..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये क्रियायोगे श्रीवासुदेवपूजाविधिनिरूपणं नामैकोनत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ..29..
2.9.m: Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, entitled 'Determination of the Rite of Worship of Śrī Vāsudeva' in [the section on] the Yoga of Action, in the Glorious Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second [part], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.
Skanda said:
Having heard thus the rite of worship of Vāsudeva, that Nārada,
pleased, asked that supreme teacher of sages again.
Nārada said:
The yoga of action of great fruit has been properly declared by the Blessed One,
which is to be performed with a single mind by those desiring perfection.
Regarding that, the restraint of the mind even for the wise, O good guru,

2.9.s: duṣkaraḥ kiṃ punastarhi nṛṇāṃ karmātmanāṃ bhuvi .. 3 ..
2.9.d: दुष्करः किं पुनस्तर्हि नृणां कर्मात्मनां भुवि .. 3 ..
2.9.m: [since control of the mind is] hard to accomplish even for men of wisdom, O good guru, how much more then for human beings bound to action on earth?
And without it, the worship of Hari does not grant the desired fruit;
therefore you ought to tell me the means of controlling it.
Skanda said:
Thus questioned by the sage, that lord of sages who sees all,
Nārāyaṇa, the companion of Nara, spoke to Nārada:
The venerable Nārāyaṇa said:

2.9.s: satyameva mune vakṣi manasosti balaṃ mahat ..
2.9.d: सत्यमेव मुने वक्षि मनसोस्ति बलं महत् ..
2.9.m: Truly indeed, O sage, do you speak: the mind possesses great strength;
even when it is conquered, discriminating people have no trust in it, as in an enemy.
There is no other enemy equal to the mind for embodied beings;
yet through the practice of meditation on Viṣṇu, free from defect, it is indeed calmed.
Because it is difficult to restrain, like an unbroken horse,
it is therefore restrained through good means by men endowed with dispassion.
Many are the means in that regard, and among them, O noble-minded one,
the practice of the eightfold yoga is supreme, immediately yielding its fruit.
The restraints, observances, O brahmin, postures, breath-control,

2.9.s: pratyāhāro dhāraṇā ca dhyānamaṃgaṃ tu saptamam ..
2.9.d: प्रत्याहारो धारणा च ध्यानमंगं तु सप्तमम् ..
2.9.m: withdrawal of the senses, concentration, and meditation is the seventh limb;
and absorption is declared to be the eighth of yoga, in this sequence.
Among these, non-violence, celibacy, truthfulness, non-stealing, and non-possession—

2.9.s: ete pañca yamāḥ proktāḥ sādhanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ ..11 ..
2.9.d: एते पञ्च यमाः प्रोक्ताः साधनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ..11 ..
2.9.m: these are declared to be the five restraints, to be accomplished with effort.
Purity, austerity, contentment, Vedic recitation, and the worship of Viṣṇu—

2.9.s: ete ca niyamāḥ pañca dvitīyāṃgatayā matāḥ .. 12 ..
2.9.d: एते च नियमाः पञ्च द्वितीयांगतया मताः .. 12 ..
2.9.m: these five are considered observances as the second limb.
Discarding the restlessness of the limbs, staying at ease—
that is called posture, such as svastikāsana, which overcomes the affliction of the pairs of opposites, O sage.
The holding of the vital breaths moving in all directions into a single region,
according to the method taught by the guru, is called breath-control.

2.9.s: cale vāyau calaṃ cittaṃ sthire tasminsthiraṃ tataḥ ..
2.9.d: चले वायौ चलं चित्तं स्थिरे तस्मिन्स्थिरं ततः ..
2.9.m: When the breath moves, the mind moves; when it is steady, the mind is steady;
therefore, this must be practiced always in a suitable place by inhalation, retention, and exhalation.
The drawing back inward of the mental activities
and of the senses away from their respective objects is declared to be withdrawal of the senses.
Fixing the mind along with the vital breath in any place such as the navel,
upon the form of Vāsudeva, is spoken of as concentration.
The contemplation one by one of each separate limb
of the Lord, such as his lotus-feet, is known as meditation.
The restraint of the vital breath and mind with intense love in Hari—
that is declared to be absorption, sought after by yogins.
Through these eight limbs learned from an accomplished good guru,

2.9.s: yogaḥ siddhyati vai puṃsāṃ samādheḥ pakvatātmakaḥ .. 2.9.30.20 ..
2.9.m: yoga consisting of the maturity of absorption is attained by men.
There is no other means for the complete restraint of the mind equal to this
for men seeking liberation: know this, O Nārada.
Even from Madana, the great enemy of ascetics and shaker of the universe,
there is never any fear for a yogin.
Having known the time of death that is to come,
the knower of yoga voluntarily casts off his body in this way through absorption:
Pressing the anus with his heels, drawing up the breath residing in the two feet
slowly, slowly, he brings it to the seat of death;
meditating on Keśava with his mind and reciting his six-syllabled mantra,
he then brings this breath to the place of Prajāpati;

2.9.s: tato nābhiṃ ca hadayamuraḥ kaṇṭhaṃ ca yogavit ..
2.9.d: ततो नाभिं च हदयमुरः कण्ठं च योगवित् ..
2.9.m: then to the navel, the heart, the chest, and the throat, the knower of yoga
dedicated to Vāsudeva brings the breath between the eyebrows.
In each of these six places separately,
the yogin practices the restraint and release of the breath, mind, and senses
until mastery over it is achieved.

2.9.s: jitaṃjitaṃ vihāyaiva sthānaṃ yāti paraṃ param ..
2.9.d: जितंजितं विहायैव स्थानं याति परं परम् ..
2.9.m: Leaving each place as it is conquered, he proceeds to the next and the next;

2.9.s: prāptasya sthānakaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ tadabhyāse śramo na hi .. 28 ..
2.9.d: प्राप्तस्य स्थानकं षष्ठं तदभ्यासे श्रमो न हि .. 28 ..
2.9.m: for one who has reached the sixth station, there is indeed no effort in its practice.
Then, having blocked the seven apertures, causing the breath united with the senses and the mind

2.9.s: prāpayya tālu vrajati brahmarandhraṃ sa yogavit .. 29 ..
2.9.d: प्रापय्य तालु व्रजति ब्रह्मरन्ध्रं स योगवित् .. 29 ..
2.9.m: to reach the palate, that knower of yoga goes to the brahmarandhra.
Then, having abandoned the latent impressions of objects made of māyā,
his mind solely on Vāsudeva, he casts off his body.
Then [he reaches] the abode of the blessed Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, beyond darkness,
Reaching [that place], serving him, endowed with a divine body, he rejoices. // 31
Thus has the summary of the scripture on yoga been related to you, O brahmin.

2.9.s: jitvā tena manaḥ svīyaṃ tamārādhaya sarvadā .. 32 ..
2.9.d: जित्वा तेन मनः स्वीयं तमाराधय सर्वदा .. 32 ..
2.9.m: Having conquered your own mind by means of it, worship him at all times. // 32

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśīti sāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye'ṣṭāṃgayoganirūpaṇaṃ nāma triṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 30 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीति साहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्येऽष्टांगयोगनिरूपणं नाम त्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 30 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, named “Exposition of the Eight-limbed Yoga,” in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second [part], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 30
Skanda said:
Having heard all these righteous words of the Lord as they were,

2.9.s: niḥsaṃśayo muniḥ prāha taṃ praṇamya kṛtāñjaliḥ .. 1 ..
2.9.d: निःसंशयो मुनिः प्राह तं प्रणम्य कृताञ्जलिः .. 1 ..
2.9.m: the sage, free of doubt, bowed to him with folded hands and spoke: // 1
Nārada said:
All my doubts have been destroyed by your grace, O Lord.
The māhātmya of Vāsudeva has been fully understood by me. // 2
Performing tapas right here together with you for some time,
and constantly listening to knowledge and the rest, I shall bring my soul to maturity. // 3
Skanda said:
Having spoken thus, Nārada, permitted also by him,
dwelt there performing tapas for a thousand divine years. // 4
And every day, at the appropriate time, he heard from Hari's mouth
dharma, knowledge, and the rest; thus the king of yogins attained maturity there. // 5

2.9.s: snehaṃ ca paramaṃ prāpa sa śrīkṛṣṇe'khilātmani ..
2.9.d: स्नेहं च परमं प्राप स श्रीकृष्णेऽखिलात्मनि ..
2.9.m: And he attained supreme affection for Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the Soul of all;
intent constantly on singing [his] virtues, he became foremost among devotees of the Lord. // 6
Then, to that perfected yogin who had attained supreme steadfastness in devotion,
the Lord, pleased, the creator of welfare for all embodied beings, spoke: // 7
Śrī Nārāyaṇa said:

2.9.s: siddhosi tvaṃ maharṣe'dya gaccha lokahitaṃ kuru ..
2.9.d: सिद्धोसि त्वं महर्षेऽद्य गच्छ लोकहितं कुरु ..
2.9.m: You have attained perfection today, O great seer; go, work for the benefit of the world.
You ought to propagate the exclusive dharma everywhere. // 8
Skanda said:

2.9.s: ityājñāṃ śirasā tasya sa ādāya jagadguroḥ ..
2.9.d: इत्याज्ञां शिरसा तस्य स आदाय जगद्गुरोः ..
2.9.m: Placing on his head that command of the teacher of the world,
as he was departing, he then praised him, bowing down and standing with folded hands: // 9
Nārada said:
Salutations, salutations to you, O Lord, teacher of the world, O Nārāyaṇa, of uncreated, divine form!

2.9.s: anantakalyāṇaguṇākarastvaṃ dāse mayi prītataraḥ madā syāḥ .. 2.9.31.10 ..
2.9.d: अनन्तकल्याणगुणाकरस्त्वं दासे मयि प्रीततरः मदा स्याः .. 2.9.31.10 ..
2.9.m: You are a mine of boundless auspicious qualities; may you ever be most pleased with me, your servant! // 10

2.9.s: tvaṃ vāsudevosi jagannivāsaḥ kṣemāya lokasya tapaḥ karoṣi ..
2.9.d: त्वं वासुदेवोसि जगन्निवासः क्षेमाय लोकस्य तपः करोषि ..
2.9.m: You are Vāsudeva, the abode of the world; you perform tapas for the welfare of the world.
O Master of the lords of yoga, established in tranquillity, sovereign of those delighted in the Self, you are the true guru of the paramahaṃsas! // 11
You are the all-pervading lord, the foremost of seers, the imperishable self, and the regulator of the souls and their rulers.
The witness, the supreme Person, self-dependent, from whose knit brow great Time arose! // 12
O Lord, through your self alone, the cosmic Puruṣa with his Māyā, you perform the play of creating and [sustaining] the worlds;

2.9.s: tathāpyakarttā nanu nirguṇosi bhūmā parabrahma parātparaśca.. 13 ..
2.9.d: तथाप्यकर्त्ता ननु निर्गुणोसि भूमा परब्रह्म परात्परश्च.. 13 ..
2.9.m: yet indeed you are the non-agent, devoid of guṇas, the Infinite, the supreme Brahman, and higher than the highest! // 13
True, self-luminous, of inconceivable power, your form is to be contemplated by those whose self has become Brahman,
O teacher of the great vow [of celibacy], O sovereign among great sages, O you whose splendour strips away the pride of the god of love! // 14

2.9.s: tapasvināṃ ye ripavaḥ prasiddhāḥ krodho raso matsaralobhamukhyāḥ ..
2.9.d: तपस्विनां ये रिपवः प्रसिद्धाः क्रोधो रसो मत्सरलोभमुख्याः ..
2.9.m: Those well-known enemies of ascetics—anger, passion, malice, and greed foremost among them—

2.9.s: apyāśramaṃ tepi kadāpi veṣṭuṃ nemaṃ kṣamā hyeṣa tava pratāpaḥ .. 15 ..
2.9.d: अप्याश्रमं तेपि कदापि वेष्टुं नेमं क्षमा ह्येष तव प्रतापः .. 15 ..
2.9.m: are not able even to encompass this hermitage at any time; such is your power! // 15
Formed of the Vedic metres, formed of knowledge, the immortal path, the embodiment of dharma, the nourisher of the creation of dharma,
uprooter of the creation of adharma, great-souled, you are imperishable, undecaying, the kinsman of the unmanifest! // 16

2.9.s: nirdoṣarūpasya tavā'khilāḥ kriyā bhavanti vai nirguṇā nirguṇasya..
2.9.d: निर्दोषरूपस्य तवाऽखिलाः क्रिया भवन्ति वै निर्गुणा निर्गुणस्य..
2.9.m: For you whose form is faultless, all your actions are free from guṇas, for you are devoid of guṇas.
You, the Lord and Master, are to be worshipped by those seeking dharma, wealth, and pleasure, and by those who desire liberation. // 17
You alone are capable of protecting from great danger—from time, māyā, Yama, and the cycles of rebirth.
Overlooking the faults of your devotees, you are greatly compassionate, truly affectionate to your devotees. // 18

2.9.s: dhṛtāvatārasya hi nāmamātraṃ rūpaṃ ca vā yaḥ smaredantakāle ..
2.9.d: धृतावतारस्य हि नाममात्रं रूपं च वा यः स्मरेदन्तकाले ..
2.9.m: Whoever, at the time of death, remembers merely the name or the form of you who have assumed an avatar—

2.9.s: sopi prabho ghoramahāghasaṃghātsadyo vimukto divamāśu yāti .. 19 ..
2.9.d: सोपि प्रभो घोरमहाघसंघात्सद्यो विमुक्तो दिवमाशु याति .. 19 ..
2.9.m: even he, O Lord, freed at once from the terrifying mass of sins, goes swiftly to heaven. // 19

2.9.s: taṃ tvāṃ vihāyā'tra tu yo manuṣyo dehe tridhātāvapi dehikeṣu ..
2.9.d: तं त्वां विहायाऽत्र तु यो मनुष्यो देहे त्रिधातावपि देहिकेषु ..
2.9.m: Abandoning such a one as you, that man here who becomes attached to the body made of three humours and to bodily things,

2.9.s: jāyātmajajñātidhaneṣu sajjate sa māyayā vañcita eva mūḍhaḥ .. 2.9.31.20 ..
2.9.d: जायात्मजज्ञातिधनेषु सज्जते स मायया वञ्चित एव मूढः .. 2.9.31.20 ..
2.9.m: to wife, children, kin, and wealth—he is a fool, utterly deceived by māyā. // 20

2.9.s: tvadbhaktiyogyo naradeha eva yaṃ kāmayante'pi ca nākasaṃsthāḥ ..
2.9.d: त्वद्भक्तियोग्यो नरदेह एव यं कामयन्तेऽपि च नाकसंस्थाः ..
2.9.m: The human body alone is fit for devotion to you, which even those residing in heaven desire.

2.9.s: tvadbhaktihīnaṃ hi divopi saukhyamahaṃ tu jāne narakeṇa tulyam .. 21 ..
2.9.d: त्वद्भक्तिहीनं हि दिवोपि सौख्यमहं तु जाने नरकेण तुल्यम् .. 21 ..
2.9.m: For I consider even the happiness of heaven, devoid of devotion to you, to be equal to hell. // 21

2.9.s: tapastrilokyāḥ kuruṣe sukhāya tatrāpi te bhāratavāsipuṃsu ..
2.9.d: तपस्त्रिलोक्याः कुरुषे सुखाय तत्रापि ते भारतवासिपुंसु ..
2.9.m: You perform tapas for the happiness of the three worlds; even so, your grace toward men residing in the land of Bhārata
is far greater, since having taken an avatar here, you shine forth wandering [among them]. // 22

2.9.s: tasyāśrayaṃ ye tava nātra kurvate ta eva śāstreṣu matāḥ kṛtaghnāḥ ..
2.9.d: तस्याश्रयं ये तव नात्र कुर्वते त एव शास्त्रेषु मताः कृतघ्नाः ..
2.9.m: Those who do not take refuge in you here are considered in the scriptures to be ungrateful indeed.

2.9.s: atastavaikāśrayameva bāḍhaṃ kurvatyajasraṃ mayi te'stu tuṣṭiḥ..23..
2.9.d: अतस्तवैकाश्रयमेव बाढं कुर्वत्यजस्रं मयि तेऽस्तु तुष्टिः..23..
2.9.m: Therefore, may you be pleased with me who constantly and firmly take refuge in you alone. // 23

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye śrīnaranārāyaṇastutinirūpaṇaṃnāmaikatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ ..31..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये श्रीनरनारायणस्तुतिनिरूपणंनामैकत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ..31..
2.9.m: Thus ends the thirty-first chapter, named “Exposition of the Praise of Śrī Nara and Nārāyaṇa,” in the Vāsudevamāhātmya of the second [part], the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. // 31
Skanda said:

2.9.s: iti stutvā tamīśānaṃ nāradaḥ sa yayau tataḥ ..
2.9.d: इति स्तुत्वा तमीशानं नारदः स ययौ ततः ..
2.9.m: Having thus praised that Lord, Nārada then departed from there
to the original hermitage of Vyāsa, named Śamyāprāsa, O brahmin. // 1
Respectfully honored by him with rising to greet him, offering a seat, and other courtesies,

2.9.s: tasmā ekāntikaṃ dharmmaṃ prāha jijñāsave sa ca ..2..
2.9.d: तस्मा एकान्तिकं धर्म्मं प्राह जिज्ञासवे स च ..2..
2.9.m: he declared the singular dharma to him, who was eager to know.

2.9.s: tato brahmasabhāṃ gatvā brahmaṇaḥ śṛṇvato muniḥ ..
2.9.d: ततो ब्रह्मसभां गत्वा ब्रह्मणः शृण्वतो मुनिः ..
2.9.m: Then, having gone to the assembly of Brahmā while Brahmā was listening, the sage
instructed the gods, ancestors, and great seers present there in that [dharma].
And the sun-god, stationed there, again heard this dharma, O sage,
in its entirety from Nārada, which had formerly been heard from Nārāyaṇa.
He respectfully spoke it to the Vālakhilyas who move in front of him;
and on Mount Meru they imparted it to the assembled gods headed by Indra.
Having heard this dharma from them, the sage Asita, O best of brahmins,
having once gone to the world of the ancestors, recited it to the ancestors.
Those ancestors, headed by Aryaman, spoke it to King Śaṃtanu;
and he narrated it in truth to Bhīṣma, his own son.
He too, at the end of the Bhārata war, when asked by the King of Dharma,
spoke it while lying upon the bed of arrows in that great assembly.

2.9.s: tatra śrutvā nāradopi sthitaḥ sadasi sādaram ..
2.9.d: तत्र श्रुत्वा नारदोपि स्थितः सदसि सादरम् ..
2.9.m: Having heard it there, Nārada also, present respectfully in that assembly,

2.9.s: kailāse śaṃkaraṃ prāha sa ca māṃ munisattama .. 9 ..
2.9.d: कैलासे शंकरं प्राह स च मां मुनिसत्तम .. 9 ..
2.9.m: spoke it on Kailāsa to Śaṃkara, and he [spoke it] to me, O best of sages.
It has been related by me to you, O brahmin, as you asked and are devoted to dharma;
for my father indeed said to me: 'This must be given to a worthy recipient.'
By whomever this māhātmya of the Lord of the Sātvatas was heard,

2.9.s: sa sa tasminparāṃ bhaktiṃ cakāra svavimuktaye .. 11 ..
2.9.d: स स तस्मिन्परां भक्तिं चकार स्वविमुक्तये .. 11 ..
2.9.m: that person developed supreme devotion to him for their own liberation.
The royal seer Yudhiṣṭhira as well, having heard the māhātmya of Devakī's son
proclaimed by Bhīṣma, rejoiced together with his brothers.
Hearing that his own maternal cousin was the cause of all causes,
that great-minded king plunged into an ocean of wonder.
The king recognized the vyūha manifestations beginning with Vāsudeva
and all the incarnations beginning with the Boar as belonging to this very husband of Ramā.
Then the king, along with his younger brothers, became exceedingly devoted
to Kṛṣṇa in his divine human form, O best of brahmins.
And having heard this account, all the divine, royal, and brahmin seers,
whoever was present there in that assembly, were also filled with wonder.

2.9.s: kṛṣṇameva paraṃ brahma viditvā te narākṛti ..
2.9.d: कृष्णमेव परं ब्रह्म विदित्वा ते नराकृति ..
2.9.m: Knowing Kṛṣṇa in human form to be none other than the supreme Brahman,
they attained devotion to him, bowing down to him with reverence.
Such is his greatness; therefore you too, O wise one,
worship that very Vāsudeva with wholehearted devotion.
This greatness of the venerable Vāsudeva has been narrated to you by me;
it pacifies evil desires and increases devotion to the Blessed One.
Whatever narratives have been related to you by me in this Purāṇa,
this, O brahmin, is their essence, extracted by churning alone.
This is the essence of the Vedas and Upaniṣads, of Sāṃkhya and Yoga,
of the entire Pāñcarātra and the legal codes, O sinless one.
This brings fortune, fame, and longevity; it is supremely auspicious,
sung directly by the Blessed One, and the destroyer of all misfortunes.
Whoever hears this sacred text, recites it, or reads it,
their intellect will become unwavering and spotless toward Vāsudeva.
And those people will become his single-minded devotees;
possessing the nature of Brahman, they go at last to the realm of Brahman, beyond darkness.

2.9.s: dharmārthī labhate'nena dharmaṃ kāmaṃ ca kāmukaḥ ..
2.9.d: धर्मार्थी लभतेऽनेन धर्मं कामं च कामुकः ..
2.9.m: One who desires dharma obtains dharma through this; a passionate person obtains desire;
one who desires wealth gains wealth; one who desires liberation attains supreme liberation.
A seeker of learning obtains learning, and a sick person is freed from disease;
by merely listening to this, the destruction of all sins takes place.
A brahmin attains Vedic splendor, and a kṣatriya attains lordship over men;

2.9.s: dhanaṃ vaiśyaḥ sukhaṃ śūdraḥ śravaṇādasya cāpnuyāt..27..
2.9.d: धनं वैश्यः सुखं शूद्रः श्रवणादस्य चाप्नुयात्..27..
2.9.m: a vaiśya attains wealth, and a śūdra attains happiness from hearing this.
Hearing this before going into battle, a king achieves victory;

2.9.s: prāpnuyātstrī ca saubhāgyaṃ kanyā ca svepsitaṃ varam ..28..
2.9.d: प्राप्नुयात्स्त्री च सौभाग्यं कन्या च स्वेप्सितं वरम् ..28..
2.9.m: a woman attains good fortune, and an unmarried maiden attains the husband of her choice.
From hearing and reciting this crest-jewel of all sacred treatises,

2.9.s: yaṃ yaṃ yaḥ kāmayetkāmaṃ taṃtaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. ..29..
2.9.d: यं यं यः कामयेत्कामं तंतं प्राप्नोति मानवः .. ..29..
2.9.m: whatever desire a person may desire, that very desire they obtain.
Therefore, O best of brahmins, always reciting this with devotion,
you should worship him who is affectionate to his devotees with body, speech, and mind.
Sauti said:
Having drunk this nectar of words issuing from the lotus face of Mahāsena, that Sāvarṇi
he devoted himself to the son of Vasudeva, the supreme Brahman in human form, the all-auspicious. (31)

2.9.s: yūyaṃ ca sarve nigamāgamajñā brahmaṇyadevaṃ bhajanīyamīśam ..
2.9.d: यूयं च सर्वे निगमागमज्ञा ब्रह्मण्यदेवं भजनीयमीशम् ..
2.9.m: And you all, knowers of the Vedas and Āgamas, remaining steadfast in your own duties,
worship him alone, the adorable Lord, God of the Brahmins, of exalted renown, the blessed Vāsudeva! (32)
Homage be to Vāsudeva, the master of the abode of Goloka, whose form is a mass of light, for the increase of the bliss of devotion! (33)

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe śrīvāsudevamāhātmye granthasaṃpradāyapravṛttinirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvātriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 32 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे श्रीवासुदेवमाहात्म्ये ग्रन्थसंप्रदायप्रवृत्तिनिरूपणं नाम द्वात्रिंशोऽध्यायः .. 32 ..
2.9.m: Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, titled "Account of the Transmission of the Tradition of the Text," in the Śrīvāsudevamāhātmya, in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the great Skandapurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. (32)

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe dvitīye vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍe vāsudevamāhātmyaṃ sampūrṇam.. 2-9 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे द्वितीये वैष्णवखण्डे वासुदेवमाहात्म्यं सम्पूर्णम्.. 2-9 ..
2.9.m: Thus the Vāsudevamāhātmya in the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, of the great Skandapurāṇa is complete. (2.9)

2.9.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇe dvitīyaṃ vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍaṃ sampūrṇam .. 2 ..
2.9.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराणे द्वितीयं वैष्णवखण्डं सम्पूर्णम् .. 2 ..
2.9.m: Thus the second section, the Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa, in the great Skandapurāṇa is complete. (2)
